articleTitle: An Improved Object Detection Algorithm Based on YOLOv10
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Object detection is still an important research topic in computer vision. For years, YOLO series object detection framework has been the object of research and improvement by many researchers since its appearance. In this paper, the improved space-to-deepth downsampling convolution algorithm is used to replace the convolution downsampling algorithm of YOLOv10 aiming at the shortcoming that the downsampling convolution process in the original detection algorithm can not retain more spatial information. We introduced RepCSP module to improve C2f module in YOLOv10. By mixing up linear attention mechanism, the feature extraction module and linear attention mechanism are integrated, and the feature extraction ability of the model is improved. Combined with the improved convolutional downsampling network, the improved C 2fRepCSP module and the integrated linear attention mechanism, the model is trained and evaluated on VOC 2007 and VOC 2012 data sets, and the results show that the detection accuracy of the model has been improved.

articleTitle: A Target-Barrier Repairment Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In this paper, we focus on the shortest repair path problem for target-barrier. Firstly, an S-elite centroid opposition-based (SCO) learning mechanism is designed, thereby enhancing the diversity of candidate solutions. The SCO learning mechanism is incorporated into the Kepler optimized algorithm (KOA)'s elite solution screening process. Additionally, Discretized S- Elite Centroid Opposition-based learning KOA (DSCOKOA), a discretization scheme tailored to the shortest repair path problem is designed, converting the originally continuous problem-solving KOA algorithm into one that can handle discretization problems. Considering the scenario where close to the target is not allowed, the repair path should bypass the safety range set around the target. This is treated as an obstacle, and the path is preprocessed before repair to ultimately provide the shortest path repair solution.

articleTitle: Modeling of All-Vanadium Redox Battery Based on Dual Stream Network with Attention Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Accurate voltage prediction for all-vanadium redox batteries (VRBs) affects the efficiency and safety of battery. In this paper, we propose a self-attention-based dual-stream neural network (SA-DSNN) model for voltage prediction under various working conditions. This approach independently processes temporal and condition data streams to reduce the noise interference. Using neural networks tailored to each of stream can more effectively extract intrinsic features. In particular, self-attention mechanisms are employed to enhance critical information. The features from both streams are fully integrated in output layer to generate final predictions. Experimental results indicate that the proposed method enhances the generalization and accuracy of VRBs model across different time scale.

articleTitle: A Feature-Enhanced Deep Learning-Based Signal Detection Algorithm for MU-MIMO-NOMA Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Deep learning (DL)-based signal detection al-gorithms for multi-user multiple-input multiple-output non-orthogonal multiple access (MU-MIMO-NOMA) systems can avoid the error propagation caused by iterative interference cancellation compared to operations research based methods but are still limited by high computational complexity. To address the aforementioned challenge and improve the re-training speed when the modulation mode changes, a data-driven feature-enhanced deep learning (DL)-based hierarchical transfer learning-augmented (DD-DTL) signal detection algorithm with low complexity is proposed, which introduce a nonlinear transformation layer to extract the high-dimensional features of receive signals. The proposed algorithm integrates the channel estimation and signal detection, performing implicit successive interference cancellation (SIC) to avoid the error propagation. Additional, a hierarchical transfer learning strategy is combined to improve the retraining speed under different modulation schemes, enabling the network to quickly update with only 5% of the training dataset while achieving good signal detection performance.

articleTitle: Technical Features and Coverage Performance Simulation of Low-Earth Orbit Mega-Constellation
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: This paper investigates the constituent elements, characteristics, and development status of Low Earth Orbit (LEO) Mega-Constellations. It also analyzes their global coverage performance through simulations using the Systems Tool Kit (STK). The study begins with an overview of the fundamental components of LEO Mega-Constellations, including orbital parameters, frequency bands, and service types, and assesses their impact on system performance. Following this, the paper reviews prominent LEO Mega-Constellation proj ects, such as Starlink, OneWeb, Kuiper, and GW, highlighting their technological advancements, operational models, and market impacts. The global coverage capabilities of these constellations are then evaluated through STK simulations to determine their effectiveness across various application scenarios. The findings indicate that LEO Mega-Constellations offer substantial global coverage benefits but also encounter challenges such as orbital congestion and spectrum management. This paper provides valuable insights for the future development of LEO Mega- Constellations and offers recommendations for optimizing related technologies.

articleTitle: A Lightweight Signaling Solution Based on MQTT for Peer to Peer Video Call System
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Along with the popularity of 5G mobile networks and the impact of the epidemic, there is a growing demand for video calls on mobile. The signaling protocol for video calls plays a very important role in maintaining the session state, we propose a lightweight signaling solution for video calls, which is based on MQTT protocol and takes advantage of MQTT's lightweight features. We have tested the system's functionality and signaling traffic consumption, and the results show that the system has complete video call functionality, is very traffic efficient at the signaling level, and has good call establishment delay.

articleTitle: Perspectives on Artificial Intelligence Integration in Higher Education: Moral Implications and Data Privacy Concerns
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: University students in Latin America have varying perceptions and interactions with artificial intelligence (AI) tools, particularly Chat GPT, within their educational environments. A quantitative cross-sectional survey involving 220 participants gathered insights through an online questionnaire addressing key themes such as accessibility, social attitudes, dependency on AI, privacy concerns, and the need for institutional guidelines. Analysis revealed that while students appreciate the potential of AI to enhance personalized learning experiences, significant concerns regarding the protection of their personal data and privacy were also evident. Findings underscore the critical need for universities to establish clear policies governing the ethical use of AI technologies in education. Understanding student perspectives enables educators and policymakers to navigate the challenges and opportunities presented by AI in academic settings, ensuring responsible and effective use of these tools.

articleTitle: Resource Allocation in UAV Edge Computing Communication System
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) communication holds paramount importance in modern communication systems, especially in scenarios like real-time reconnaissance during natural disasters. However, the resource limitations of UAVs often hamper their ability to efficiently handle time-sensitive tasks. To augment the computational prowess of these aerial vehicles, we propose a novel approach involving a network of multiple UAVs deployed with Mobile Edge Computing (MEC) devices. This study delves into the deployment of MEC devices on UAV platforms, enabling task offloading for the swift processing of time-sensitive tasks across the entire UAV network. We formulate a problem focused on minimizing delays in UAV edge computing systems while adhering strictly to power constraints. However, the highly non-convex nature of this problem poses significant challenges in finding effective solutions. To overcome these challenges, we introduce a Penalty Dual Decomposition (PDD) method that iteratively tackles the problem, thereby deriving the optimal task offloading and transmission power allocation. Simulation results reveal that our proposed task offloading and transmission power optimization algorithm outperforms traditional methods, achieving a commendable 23.7% reduction in delay.

articleTitle: An Improved Loop Timing Synchronization Scheme for Frequency-Hopping Systems Based on MSK
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In remote wireless communication systems, clock deviation can severely affect the reception performance by causing symbol asynchronization, necessitating symbol timing synchronization. Traditional feedback-based synchronization schemes face challenges in frequency-hopping communication systems due to the discontinuity of the carrier signal, leading to issues such as lock loss and slow lock-in speed. In this paper, we propose an improved loop symbol timing synchronization scheme based on MSK signals, which is applicable to scenarios with signal discontinuity. This scheme utilizes interpolation to synchronize the output signals. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed scheme exhibits excellent synchronization performance and maintains a certain level of interference resistance even under low signal-to-noise ratios.

articleTitle: Spectrally Efficient Communication System Based on Combined Chirp in Low SNR Environment
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Chirp signal emerges as a promising technique for wireless communication systems in next-generation networks, owing to its better multipath diversity exploitation. However, due to the scarcity of radio spectrum resources, continuously increasing the bandwidth reduces spectral efficiency, imposing significant challenges to communication systems. In this paper, we design a high spectral efficiency transmission system based on the combination of chirp signals with different slopes, incorporating both up-chirp and down-chirp signals. To enhance system reliability, the linear equation-solving algorithm is innovatively combined with matched filtering. We further leverage oversampling to enhance system detection performance under low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) conditions and rigorously derive the gain expressions. Extensive simulations demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in terms of bit error rate (BER) performance and spectral efficiency in low SNR environment.

articleTitle: Edge Computing-Enabled Real-Time Resource Allocation System Based on Satellite Cluster
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: With the rapid advancement of satellite communication and remote sensing technology, there has been a dramatic surge in data generated by satellites. Real-time in-orbit processing enables more efficient data handling and immediate response capabilities. Existing research mainly focuses on static resource allocation strategies, with scant attention given to resource allocation and cluster monitoring under dynamically varying task requirements and frequent node changes. In this paper, we propose an edge computing-enabled real-time resource allocation (ECRA) system. Specifically, we adopt the satellite clusters policy to investigate the effect of cluster behavior on task execution, the clusters with three strategies: shortest propagation distance strategy, longest duration strategy, and minimal computational redundancy strategy. Based on the satellite cluster, we run image-processing tasks in the established Kubernetes cluster. The ECRA system depicted through Grafana, performance metrics such as CPU utilization, memory usage, and network traffic. The experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of satellite clusters in resource utilization rates, execution times, and resource allocation under high loads across different strategies.

articleTitle: A Deep Learning-Based Algorithm for Multi-Feature Processing and Signal Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In the field of signal detection, traditional signal processing algorithms encounter challenges in effectively integrating multiple features for joint detection. To address this issue, we propose a multi-feature fusion detection algorithm. This algorithm processes various signal features, including matched filtering results, Short-Time Fourier Transform (STFT) features, and wavelet transform features. For the matched filtering results, we employ a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network, while a convolutional neural network (CNN) is utilized for processing time-frequency domain features. After processing multiple features and performing a weighted summation of the results, the algorithm yields the final detection outcome. Simulation results indicate that the algorithm demonstrates a high level of detection accuracy.

articleTitle: Spatio-Temporal Traffic Prediction Under Multi-Scale Dynamic Convolution
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Traffic flow prediction remains a challenging task due to the complexity of spatio-temporal dependencies and the dynamic nature of traffic patterns. Traditional methods often struggle to efficiently model long-term dependencies and adapt to dynamic changes in traffic networks, leading to suboptimal prediction performance. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a novel traffic flow prediction model that integrates multi-scale convolutional networks and dynamic graph convolutional networks. By replacing the traditional Transformer architecture with Linformer, the model significantly reduces computational complexity while efficiently processing long sequential data. Additionally, the introduction of multi-scale convolutional networks allows for effective extraction of flow features at short, medium, and long time scales, enhancing prediction accuracy across different horizons. The incorporation of Dynamic Graph Convolutional Networks (Dynamic GCN) enables dynamic adjustment of the adjacency matrix, allowing the model to adaptively capture changes in spatio-temporal relationships within the traffic network. Experimental results show that the proposed model outperforms existing approaches in short-, medium-, and long-term traffic flow prediction tasks across multiple datasets, demonstrating its effectiveness in addressing the complexities of spatio-temporal dependencies and dynamic changes.

articleTitle: Faster-CEASC+: A Lightweight Object Detection Network for Drone Images
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: As Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) technology continues to advance and become more widespread, object detection on UAVs has become a critical task. Constrained by the size and energy consumption of UAVs, deploying lightweight object detection models on them is a better choice. However, previous work has focused on the partial lightweighting of the network structure. This paper proposes a fully lightweight object detection model for the entire network structure, called Faster Context-Enhanced Adaptive Sparse Convolutional Plus (Faster-CEASC+). The paper's first contribution is that we design an extremely lightweight detection head, CEASC+, which maintains high accuracy. Moreover, our model also features a lightweight backbone that balances FLOPs and FPS. Extensive experiments on the VisDrone-DET2018 dataset demonstrate that compared to the state-of-the-art detector, generalized focal loss V1-CEASC, our model improves significantly by 1.1 mAP and 124.6% FPS, while reducing 60.8% FLOPs.

articleTitle: Three-Stage Framework for Predicting Fault Modes and Remaining Useful Life in Aircraft Engines
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: The prediction of Remaining Useful Life (RUL) for aircraft engines has been a focal point in predictive maintenance research, given its critical role in reducing maintenance costs and ensuring aviation safety. Accurately forecasting RUL is challenging as aircraft engines experience multiple fault modes during continuous operation, each impacting prediction accuracy. To address this, we propose a three-stage RUL prediction framework. In the first stage, an autoencoder reduces the dimensionality of the sequence data. In the second stage, time series clustering are applied to the reduced sequences to label the fault modes. Finally, in the third stage, a joint model is trained to simultaneously predict both the fault mode and the RUL. Experiments conducted on the public C-MAPSS dataset demonstrate that our method achieves performance gains of 4.1% and 13.1% in Root Mean Square Error and Scoring Function, respectively, with a fault mode prediction accuracy of 98.8%. Compared to other studies, our approach not only improves predictive performance but also effectively identifies the fault modes and RUL of the samples.

articleTitle: An Optimized Diff Algorithm Based on Myers
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Virtual DOM technology is the key to efficient rendering of modern front-end frameworks (such as Vue, React), and its performance largely depends on the efficiency of Diff algorithm when comparing and updating new and old virtual nodes. Vue2 uses Diff algorithm based on tree structure, but with the increase of application scale, the current Diff algorithm has performance bottleneck when dealing with complex UI updates and large-scale nodes. To solve this problem, this paper proposes an optimized Diff algorithm based on Myers algorithm to improve the comparative performance of virtual DOM in Vue2 framework. The optimization scheme of this paper combines the minimum editing distance calculation method of Myers algorithm and virtual DOM tree structure, and reduces unnecessary node comparison through multi-level segmentation and difference point prediction mechanism. In addition, a jump strategy is designed to speed up the Diff process in frequent UI update scenarios.

articleTitle: A Refinement Framework of CS-MRI Using the Fast Low-Rank Approximation
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Compressed sensing magnetic resonance imaging (CS-MRI) enables fast acquisition, which is highly desirable for numerous clinical applications. However, the quality of the MR images will depend upon the rate of undersampling. Especially, under the extremely undersampling case, if the image obtained by a conventional CS-MRI method is not satisfied, is any remedial measure could be made? In this paper, a refinement framework of CS-MRI will be proposed as the remedial measure. In the refinement framework, the MR image obtained by using the conventional CS-MRI method, will be taken as the training image. A low-rank model associated with a self-learning scheme will be established for the refinement framework. To preserve more detail features and to reduce the complexity, a partial singular value thresholding (SVT) method and an adaptive selection of the regularization parameter will be employed to establish the solver. Numerical simulations show that the proposed framework can be the remedial measure to improve the quality and robustness of MR image reconstruction in the low sampling case.

articleTitle: Cross-Platform Emotion Analysis and Hot Word Mining Method Based on Live Broadcast Room Bullet Screen
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: With the vigorous growth of the live streaming industry, the live streaming barrage data encompasses a considerable amount of valuable user emotion and topic information. This paper centers on the three live streaming platforms of Douyin, Kuaishou, and Xiaohongshu. By applying the methods of emotion analysis and hot word extraction, it conducts a comparison and analysis of the emotional tendencies and hotspots of users from different platforms in live streaming interactions. The findings reveal that users of Douyin have more positive emotions and focus on entertainment stars and fashion topics. Users of the Kuaishou platform have neutral emotions and are concerned about life services and local culture; while the emotions of users are more negative, and they are interested in skin care, beauty, and lifestyle. The cross-platform analysis approach proposed in this paper can offer data support for the optimization of live streaming content and user profiling.

articleTitle: Error Probability Minimization for Short-Packet Backscatter Communications
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Most of Internet of Things (IoT) applications are relying on short packet communications (SPC), while the error probability (EP) of SPC in backscatter communications (Back-Com) has not been sufficiently investigated. Motivated by this, in this work, we minimize the overall EP for a short-packet BackCom network, where multiple sensors sequentially modulate their short-packet information on the energy signal transmitted by the energy source and then backscatter the modulated signal to the receiver. Specifically, we formulate a non-convex mixed integer nonlinear programming problem that minimizes the overall EP by jointly optimizing the short-packet blocklength and power reflection coefficient (PRC) of each sensor. To address it, we derive the expression of the optimal PRC at each sensor in a closed form. Substituting the optimal PRC into the formulated problem, the problem can be transformed into two subproblems that are proved to be convex. Then the optimal blocklength is determined by that of the subproblem that achieves a lower EP. Simulation results show that our proposed scheme outperforms the benchmark schemes in terms of the overall EP.

articleTitle: A 3D Swin Transformer Fusion Network for Brain Tumor Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Glioma is a deadly brain tumor, and its diagnosis and treatment are crucial for patients. In this study, we propose a novel automatic brain tumor segmentation model 3D-SwinFusionNet, which combines the features of U-Net and Swin Transformer.By incorporating the Advanced Swin Transformer (AST) and Double Residual Block (DRB), the model improves feature extraction and the capture of local information. Additionally, it includes a segmentation head designed to optimize feature information and reduce decoding errors, thereby enhancing segmentation accuracy to some extent. The experimental results show that our proposed method has the lowest HD value of 2.32 and the highest DICE coefficient of 95.45% The design of 3D-SwinFusionNet performs well in addressing the challenges of medical image segmentation and may help improve the efficiency and accuracy of glioma diagnosis.

articleTitle: Improved Dung Beetle Algorithm to Optimize BP Neural Network Air Quality Index Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Aiming at the problems of BP neural network parameter adjustment difficulty and poor accuracy of prediction model, multi-strategy Improved Dung Beetle Optimization Algorithm (FLADBO) was proposed to optimize the prediction model of BP neural network, Logistic chaotic mapping was introduced to solve the problem of uneven initial population distribution, and elite reverse strategy was introduced to improve the diversity of population. In the foraging stage, dynamic weights were used to improve the searching ability of dung beetles. In order to balance the ability of global search and local search of the algorithm, the flood algorithm (FLA) is fused and the nonlinear adjustment parameter R. Comparing the improved dung beetle optimization algorithm with other intelligent bionic algorithms in 13 benchmark test functions, the results show that the improved dung beetle optimization algorithm has stronger optimization performance, higher convergence accuracy and better stability. Then, FLADBO algorithm was used to optimize the initial weights and thresholds of the BP network model, and the FLadBO-BP AQI prediction model was constructed. Finally, 900 groups of AQI data collected were put into the prediction model for testing and analysis. The experimental results showed that, Compared with BP neural network model, DPO-BP model and PSO-BP model, FLADBO-BP model has higher accuracy in predicting AQI.

articleTitle: LASAR Imaging Algorithm Based on Keystone Transform and Beamforming Principle
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Sampling rate and aperture array as key to imaging quality will be affected by the antenna size and the arrangement spacing in linear array synthetic aperture radar (LASAR). Under the condition of the relatively fixed array arrangement, the algorithm based on keystone transform and beamforming principle is proposed in this paper to improve the sampling rate and aperture array. Firstly, the keystone transform is used to correct the range cell migration (RCM), and the limitation of the Nyquist sampling rate is solved by beamforming principle. Then insufficient sampling rates is improved by spectrum estimation in the along-track direction. Finally, the simulation results demonstrate that the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Chinese Resume Named Entity Recognition Based on ChineseBERT
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: The existing methods for recognizing named entities in Chinese electronic resumes have been found to have low accuracy. While the BERT pre-training model has been demonstrated to achieve higher accuracy compared to traditional models, the masking language modeling task may result in the random masking of a part of a single or consecutive word in the Chinese language environment. This practice may result in the loss of complete word information. In other words, when masking, the entire word is masked instead of a portion of the characters, which can better preserve the semantic integrity of Chinese. The Chinese BERT pre-training model is employed to embed words in the input text, thereby obtaining dynamic word vectors and resolving the issue of polysemy. BiLSTM is utilized to obtain contextual structural features, which are employed to deeply my semantic relations. The spliced vectors are then input to the CRF layer for Viterbi decoding, which enables the learning of constraint relations between labels and the subsequent output of the correct labels. The experimental results demonstrate that the method achieves an F1 value of 94.86% in the Resume e-resume dataset.

articleTitle: Improved Action Recognition Algorithm for Video Surveillance Based on PoseC3D
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: The precise recognition of human action is of great significance for intelligent monitoring and video analysis. Previous researchers have utilized many methods to detect human action, but the accuracy and robustness of these methods remain to be improved. Skeleton-based action recognition methods have reported high accuracy and robustness, but these methods have not fully utilized multiple modalities for feature fusion. In order to solve the above problems, a multi-modality feature fusion based video surveillance personnel action recognition method is proposed by combining the two methods. The SlowOnly network is used to extract RGB modality features. The Faster R-CNN and Lite-HRNet networks are used to obtain skeleton modality data. The PoseC3D network is used to extract skeleton modality features. The early and late fusion of RGB modality features and skeleton modality features are performed. Then the action recognition results of video surveillance personnel are obtained. The experimental results on the NTU RGB+D public dataset under the X-Sub standard show the following points. In the action recognition model based on a single skeleton modality, PoseC3D has a higher recognition accuracy than GCN methods, reaching 92.8%. In the action recognition model based on RGB modality, recognition accuracy has reached 95.4%. The action recognition model based on multi-modality feature fusion has a higher recognition accuracy than the recognition model based on a single modality, reaching 96.1%.

articleTitle: Design of the Intelligent Linker Control System Based on 5G Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In the era of the Internet and the burgeoning development of smart cities, urban systems, and services are increasingly interconnected, leading to enhanced resource utilization efficiency and refined urban management. The advent of 5G technology marks a significant milestone, further integrating into the fabric of daily life and offering unprecedented opportunities for urban infrastructure advancements. This paper introduces a novel 5G-enabled smart grid system designed to address the prevalent issue of unreliable traditional traffic light systems, which are prone to frequent malfunctions with unidentified fault points. Our innovative product leverages an STM32 microcontroller to actively monitor and diagnose traffic light systems, pin-pointing the exact location of malfunctions with precision. This capability not only ensures the reliability of traffic management but also significantly enhances the responsiveness and safety of urban traffic flow. By harnessing the high-speed connectivity of 5G networks, our system facilitates real-time monitoring and control, thereby optimizing traffic management and contributing to the broader goals of smart city development. This research presents a comprehensive analysis of the system's architecture, the integration of 5G technology, and the performance evaluation of the proposed solution. The findings underscore the potential of our 5G smart grid system to revolutionize urban traffic management, offering a scalable and efficient solution to the challenges posed by legacy traffic light infrastructures.

articleTitle: nDrain: A Robust Log Template Mining Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Log template mining is an important step in analyzing logs. Drain is an important log template mining algorithm that performs well in handling various types of logs. However, Drain assumes that the first word of log entries belonging to the same log template is the same. However, not all logs meet this condition. Therefore, this paper proposes a robust log template mining algorithm based on the Drain algorithm, which we call nDrain. nDrain uses TFIDF to collect keywords from log templates and classifies log messages based on these keywords. We completed experimental verification using the public logs provided by Loghub. The experiment shows that compared to Drain, the accuracy of nDrain is improved on 5 types of logs.

articleTitle: Enhancing Multi-Speaker Audio Generation with Limited Samples Based on Acoustic Signals
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: His paper presents a method for enhancing multi-speaker audio generation using limited samples based on acoustic signals. The proposed approach improves the existing variational inference text-to-speech (VITS) model by incorporating the vector quantized variational autoencoder (VQVAE) network and the attention mechanism to enhance audio generation quality for different speakers. Traditional VITS models trained on large and high-quality datasets can generate high-quality text-to-speech outputs with good generalization. However, with small datasets, the VITS model often struggles to maintain audio quality and speaker characteristics. To address these limitations, we introduce the VQVAE network to discretize continuous acoustic features into tokens, effectively capturing essential speaker characteristics such as timbre and articulation. The attention mechanism further improves the model's ability to focus on these critical speaker-specific features, especially in multi-speaker scenarios. Experimental results show that our enhanced model not only excels in generating natural and high-quality speech for the original speaker but also effectively generalizes to other speakers. This method demonstrates significant improvements in naturalness and speaker characteristic retention, making it particularly effective for multi-speaker audio generation in scenarios with limited data.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of DOA Estimation System Based on Software Defined Radio
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Direction of Arrival (DOA) estimation is an important fundamental problem in wireless signal processing. The current research on DOA estimation is mainly carried out in the MATLAB software simulation environment, but there is a large difference between the pure software simulation and the actual results. In order to better study the practical application, this paper uses two Universal Software Radio Peripheral (USRP) as the hardware base, and combines the Simulink software platform to realize the ratio amplitude algorithm direction measurement. In the paper, the reasons and solutions for amplitude calibration as well as data synchronization in the system are firstly described, then the formula of the amplitude ratio algorithm is fitted by the measured data, and finally the DOA estimation system is implemented and tested by USRP and Simulink. The experimental results show that the system is capable of accomplishing the DOA estimation function, which provides a convenient and reliable experience for source angle estimation as well as signal processing researchers.

articleTitle: An Intent-Driven Network Security Policy Generation Method
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Aiming at the problems of existing network security policy generation relying on subjective judgment, inefficient generation and not being able to update in time, an Intent-Driven Network Security Policy Generation (IDSPG) method is proposed. Firstly, alert information is generated based on the attribute attack graph (AAG) and mapped to the security intent with the security intent template; Secondly, combined with the network information knowledge graph, the intent is further translated into the RDF format as a transitional strategy; The dynamic generation of transitional policies to the underlying network security policies is completed through the RDF analysis. The experiments show that the method proposed in this paper can correctly generate the security policies corresponding to the security intents, and has greater improvement in the generation efficiency and correctness.

articleTitle: An Interference Sources Localization Method Using ADS-B Data for GNSS
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Since Automatic Dependent Surveillance Broadcast (ADS-B) system obtains the location information of aircrafts through GNSS, the effect of interference towards GNSS will be reflected in ADS-B data. An ADS-B data based localization method for GNSS blanket interference sources using clustering algorithm and circle fitting is proposed in this paper. Firstly, the starting points and the ending points of each fracture trajectory, which is just caused by GNSS blanket jammers, are extracted. Then, density-based spatial clustering of applications with noise (DBSCAN) clustering algorithm is used to exclude the noise points contributed by some random factors. After that, circle fitting is executed to realize the division of the point sets corresponding to different interference sources. Meanwhile, the estimation of the number and the position coordinates of interference sources are finished. Simulation results demonstrate that the average localization error of the proposed method can be reduced by 74% compared with the baseline scheme, i.e. the minimization cost function method (MCFM) under the scenario with single interference source. Moreover, the proposed schemes can be applicable to solve the localization issue of multiple interference sources, while MCFM method doesn't work in this case.

articleTitle: Scene Image Retrieval Based on Salient Local Feature Aggregation and Geographic Information
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In order to improve the mean average precision (mAP) of scene image retrieval, this paper proposes a scene image retrieval algorithm based on salient local feature aggregation and geographic information, and establishes a scene database that can be verified by the algorithm. On the basis of “probabilistic proposal” selection and weighted aggregation of local detectors of PWA algorithm, image retrieval is carried out by means of geographic information filtering. The addition of geographic information provides more reference features for scene image retrieval, which can improve the accuracy and efficiency of the algorithm. The construction of scene image database with geographic information and scalability provides a test basis for similar algorithms

articleTitle: Research on Credit Loan Rating Based on LightGBM Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: To meet the demand of customer credit scoring in the loan market, the paper uses machine learning algorithm to build a credit scoring model based on the collected credit data of a region to predict the customer's lending risk level. Firstly, data cleaning and exploratory analysis were carried out to obtain complete standby credit loan data; Secondly, Pearson correlation analysis and thermodynamic diagram are used to select and process characteristic independent variables and dependent variables; Finally, LightGBM model is used for training, and compared with many mainstream prediction algorithms. The complete algorithm model in the paper can achieve more than 97% in prediction accuracy, recall rate and F-1 Score evaluation index.

articleTitle: Nesterov Momentum Based Optimization Algorithm for Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Optimization algorithms play a crucial role in deep learning. These algorithms, specifically designed for deep learning, are used to update neural network parameters and minimize the loss function. The importance of optimization algorithms in deep learning cannot be overstated. While the initialization of network parameters determines whether the model will converge, the performance of the optimization algorithm directly influences the training efficiency of the model. In an effort to boost the efficiency of model training, this paper presents a new optimization algorithm called Fast-Adan, which builds upon the original Adan algorithm to enhance its speed of convergence. This is achieved by optimally adjusting the step size in gradient descent through the appropriate selection of second-order momentum at each iteration. Our FastAdan algorithm exhibits superior generalization and convergence characteristics. On a theoretical level, the convergence properties of the algorithm are analyzed, and convergence bounds are established. To demonstrate the algorithm's effectiveness, we trained three models and performed extensive tests in non-convex optimization scenarios. The experimental reveal that Fast-Adan not only converges faster and with greater precision compared to established algorithms but also maintains strong generalization abilities.

articleTitle: Feature Point Detection Based on FPN and Attention Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In order to solve the problem of low repeatability and accuracy in feature point detection in weak texture regions, the SuperPoint model is integrated with feature pyramid FPN, position Attention, and channel Attention in this paper. Utilizing feature pyramid FPN for multi-scale fusion of feature maps to obtain feature maps containing multi-scale information, in order to obtain sufficient feature points and improve the repeatability of feature point detection. By mapping features through positional Attention and channel Attention, we obtain feature dependencies in both spatial and channel dimensions, thereby enhancing feature relationships and improving the accuracy of feature point detection. Finally, the improved SuperPoint feature point detection model was validated on the Hpatches dataset, and the results showed that the improved SuperPoint model improved repeatability by 2.11 %. In addition, when the pixel difference thresholds were 1, 3, and 5, the accuracy increased by 1.49%, 1.68%, and 2.17%.

articleTitle: Pedestrian Behavior Recognition on Roads Based on Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: With the exploration and development of autonomous driving technology, road pedestrian video analysis functionality is gaining increasing attention. Through the use of artificial intelligence for safety level analysis of road pedestrian behavior, traffic accidents can be reduced. Traditional in-vehicle pedestrian safety alert algorithms use computer vision to detect pedestrian positions, and radar to calculate pedestrian distance and assess collision risk. These recognition algorithms follow simple logic, which can easily overlook hidden dangers during driving. For example, when pedestrians engage in activities like pushing and shoving in what the vehicle system deems a safe area, they may suddenly move to the center of the roadway, significantly increasing the likelihood of a traffic accident. Many other risky pedestrian behaviors exist, such as looking down at their phones, making phone calls, Walk side by side (SBS), carrying large items, running, etc. Considering the variety of pedestrian behaviors and the current limitations of video behavior recognition (BR) algorithms, which cannot be directly applied to driving scenarios, and the lack of publicly available datasets, several high-risk road behavior video datasets were created. A BR method based on deep learning, called C3dTe, was proposed. The C3dTe algorithm was trained and tested using publicly available datasets like UCF101 and HMDB51. Experimental results show that the C3dTe algorithm achieved a maximum recognition rate of 98.33% on the UCF101 dataset and 68.82% on the HMDB51 dataset. On the custom road scene dataset, the recognition rate exceeded 82%, demonstrating its effectiveness in identifying road pedestrian behaviors.

articleTitle: Design of a Mental Health Question-answering System Based on a Knowledge Graph
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: With the progress and development of society, the pace of life is becoming faster and faster, which has greatly increased people's pressureForce. Mental health becomes an important indicator of health status. Due to the insufficient popularization of mental health knowledge and the imperfect development of the mental health service system, people lack the understanding of mental illness knowledge, and psychological problems are not well solved. Therefore, it is necessary to build a mental health Q&A system. As a good method for storing information intelligently, knowledge graph can provide a strong knowledge reserve for the Q&A system.

articleTitle: Soft-Aided Error-and-Erasure Decoding of BCH-SPC Product Codes with Bit Marking
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel soft-aided error-and-erasure decoding method for product codes with Bose-Chaudhuri-Hocquenghem (BCH) and single parity check (SPC) component codes based on bit marking. We mark all the reliable bits in the decoding of BCH component codes according to scaled reliability to reduce miscorrection, and we only flip the unreliable bits in the decoding of SPC component codes. A backtrack scheme is introduced to further improve the performance. The complexity of our proposed decoder is much lower than those of conventional soft-aided iterative decoders as the reliability of each bit remains unchanged when decoding, and only ternary message is exchanged between the component decoders. Simulations show that the proposed decoding method outperforms previous decoder by 0.1 dB, and the computational complexity is reduced by about 60% compared with 5G-LDPC codes at the cost of about 0.5dB performance loss.

articleTitle: HSToR: Enhancing Scalability for Optical Circuit Switched Networks with Recirculation
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Combining optical circuit switches (OCSes) and electrical packet switches (EPSes) has emerged as an appealing architecture for data centers. However, in this hybrid data center network architecture with widespread application, challenges persist in data packet scheduling and buffer management for OCS-based matching patterns due to spatial and temporal traffic pattern constraints. Given the demand-agnostic way for OCS configurations, where each switch can only provide matching between input and output ports at any given time. In other words, the availability of optical circuits is intermittent, resulting in potential blockage of flows between them when optical circuits are unavailable. Traditionally, in the event of flow blockage, multiple queue buffers are maintained at Top-of- Rack (ToR) switches, with the number of queues corresponding to the number of destinations. Unfortunately, the “per-destination queue” approach suffers from poor scalability. To address this issue, we propose HSToR, a novel design for ToR switches, aimed at enhancing scalability and data transfer efficiency in optical circuit switched networks. Experimental results demonstrate that HSToR achieves high scalability, maintains lower latency as the network scales, better addresses packet loss during buffering, and sustains high throughput and link utilization.

articleTitle: Development and Application of Artificial Intelligence Literacy Through BERT-Based Knowledge Engineering
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: A new BERT-based system is proposed and applied in real teaching scenarios in higher education aiming to enhance the researcher's and students' programming efficiency. The research and learning of academic landscapes are transformed from conventional teaching methods or approaches to innovative ones, especially influencing the Higher Education (HE) context. AI exploration raises common sense worldwide and gradually becomes a lifelong learning objective. This study aims to explore the evolution of AI literacy pedagogies for both students and researchers in the two teaching styles universities in higher education scenarios. Some innovative teaching activities are implemented to enhance the researchers' and students' AI literacy. The theoretical framework (‘conversational framework’) employed in the study plays a role as the rationale for the engineering pedagogy. The experimental results and collected teaching data indicate that the system can assist both the students' and researchers' learning interests and learning efficiency.

articleTitle: A Prediction Method For Ozone Concentration Based on GCN-BiLSTM-Attention
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: As one of the major air pollutants, ground-level ozone has significant impacts on human health and the environment. To effectively address air quality issues and improve urban living conditions, predicting ozone concentration has become an urgent task. Existing neural network prediction models increasingly consider the correlation of time and space, known as spatiotemporal prediction. These models take into account both temporal and spatial features, often outperforming simple sequence models such as Recurrent Neural Networks (RNN). Ozone predictions typically exhibit spatiotemporal correlations, with ozone detection values in different areas influencing each other, especially in urban settings. Therefore, this paper incorporates these spatiotemporal features into the modeling process and proposes a GCN-BiLSTM-Attention spatiotemporal neural network for ozone concentration prediction. To integrate spatiotemporal features simultaneously, BiLSTM is first used to compress features along the time dimension of each node. Then, GCN is employed to transfer and fuse information between nodes, ultimately obtaining the embedded representation of the nodes in the graph. The features of all nodes are then pooled to obtain a comprehensive representation of the input spatiotemporal data, which is finally fed into a fully connected layer to predict ozone values for the next 24 hours. Experimental results show that this model achieves the best prediction accuracy, with an average MAE value of 10.7021 and a goodness of fit of 0.91. Compared to baseline models such as GRU and LSTM, the performance is significantly improved.

articleTitle: A New SAR Autofocus Method Based on Error Coefficient Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: To address the problem of blurred Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) imaging caused by motion errors, this paper proposes a new SAR autofocus method based on the traditional Minimum Entropy Autofocus (MEA) algorithm. First, we model the phase error in SAR images as a polynomial error and divide the error characteristics into high-order error and low-order error. Then, we propose a Restormer and Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) Model (RCM) to estimate the error coefficient, where the feature extraction network based on Restormer is used to predict the low-order error coefficient and the feature extraction network based on CNN is used to predict the high-order error coefficient. Finally, we compensate the predicted phase error in the original SAR image to obtain the focused SAR image. The experimental results show that the SAR focused image obtained by our proposed method has better results in entropy and contrast metrics.

articleTitle: BC-PASys: A Blockchain-Based Secure and Reliable Peer Assessment System for Online Course
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Online learning has become popular due to its flexibility and convenience. However, the huge number of e-works will increase the pressure on teachers. Peer assessment can effectively solve the problem by utilizing the scores of learners. However, there are two main problems (low security of data and low credibility of results) in traditional assessment systems. Blockchain is essentially a distributed database system with the characteristics of decentralization, traceability, difficulty in being tampered with, and high security. Therefore, integrating blockchain technology into peer assessment can solve the problems mentioned above. This paper applies blockchain technology to peer assessment to design and implement a secure and reliable peer assessment system (BC-PASys). The system proposed in this study can ensure the security of origin assessment data and the reliability of peer assessment results, which can finally promote the large-scale application of peer assessment and enrich the application scenarios of blockchain technology.

articleTitle: Improved YOLOv5 Model Based Specific Bolt Detection for Automobile Manufacturing
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In automotive automation production, the absence of bolts in special structural components can pose significant safety risks. Current deep learning-based object detection systems in workshops often face challenges such as complex deployment and detection difficulties. To ensure efficiency and simplify deployment while maintaining accuracy, this paper proposes a bolt detection solution based on the improved YOLOv5 model named YOLOv5sSLC. The proposed technique includes two key enhancements. First, a small object detection layer is added to capture feature information of small targets, improving the detection of bolts with various sizes and reducing false detection rates, thereby increasing accuracy. Second, the integration of the Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM) enhances feature representation capabilities, further improving detection precision. Comparative experiments demonstrate that the YOLOv5sSLC model improves the capture rate and detection accuracy of bolt targets, with a 3.7% increase in MAP and a 4% increase in precision being achieved. Therefore, the YOLOv5-sSLC model can be effectively deployed in workshops, to meet real-time detection requirements and to provide technical support for many low-cost, non-contact workshop environments.

articleTitle: Modeling and Optimizing the 5G RRC State Machine to Reduce Terminal Energy Consumption
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: With the popularization and wide application of mobile terminals, addressing the issues of substantial energy consumption, low utilization of radio resources, and lackluster compatibility of conventional energy management strategies becomes significantly important. In this paper, we propose an enhanced Radio Resource Control (RRC) state machine, eRRC, to reduce the energy consumption of 5G user equipment. The basic idea is to dynamically configure the state parameters in real time according to the traffic behaviors when transmission. Specifically, we self-develop an energy monitor embedded in the terminal operation system, which can meticulously record the nuanced energy consumption patterns during each traffic transmission stage. Further, eRRC adapts the parameter setup and the activation time of each state when state machine transition. Simulation experiments illustrate that compared with the prevailing terminal energy management methods, eRRC can realize an average energy conservation of 8.26%. Also, its lightweight implementation is suitable for other Internet of Things devices.

articleTitle: Dual-polarized RF Tags for Orientation Estimation of Underground Pipelines
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Ground Penetrating Radar (GPR) is a non-destructive technique widely used to detect objects such as underground pipelines and cables. The hyperbolic features observed in radar images are commonly used to estimate cylindrical objects' depth and radius. However, generating standard hyperbola requires that the GPR scanning direction be perpendicular to the pipeline's orientation, which is challenging to guarantee in practical field measurements. In this study, we integrate GPR with radio frequency identification (RFID) to estimate the orientation of underground pipelines. We designed a dual-polarized flexible RF tag, with the resonant frequencies depending on the polarization of the incident electromagnetic wave. The tags were tested in both simulation and field experiments to show that they can generate strong resonance in horizontal and vertical polarizations. Subsequently, we analyzed the different structures of tags that affect the resonant frequencies in horizontal and vertical polarizations and thereby can effectively control the resonant frequencies in different polarizations. This innovative approach has potential for applications such as pipeline orientation estimation, offering new solutions in the realm of underground environmental monitoring.

articleTitle: A Flexible Ultra-Wideband Bandpass Filter Based on Stepped Impedance Multi-Mode Resonator
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Microwave filters play an important role in the RF telecommunication system. With the wide application of UWB wireless communication technology, the demand for flexible UWB microwave filters is increasing rapidly. In this paper, a flexible ultra-wideband bandpass filter is proposed based on the step- impedance multi-mode resonance structure, with a pair of parallel open-circuit stubs loaded to suppress the high-order harmonic and a set of U-shaped gaps etched to improve the in-band return loss. By comparing the simulation results in the flat and bend state, the proposed filter is demonstrated that it has an ultra-wide passband from 2.93 to 10.86 GHz, with the insertion loss less than 0.89 dB and the reflection loss better than 12 dB, and good suppression of parasitic passband is obtained. Good filtering performance and out-of-band suppression can still be maintained in the case of bending deformation.

articleTitle: Development and Application of Multi-Source Data Governance Platform Based on Medical Research System
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: With the development of medical technology, the scale and complexity of medical research data have increased significantly. To meet the challenges of integrating and analyzing heterogeneous data from multiple sources, this paper designs a medical research-assisted multi-source data governance platform. The platform covers five modules: data access, processing, quality control, computation and output, and is able to efficiently handle structured and semi-structured data sources. By integrating Apache NiFi, Kafka, Flink, Spark and other technologies, the platform realizes real-time data processing, batch analysis and visualization display to support researchers' research and decision-making. In the future, the platform will further optimize the performance of real-time data processing and enhance intelligent analysis and data mining capabilities to promote the progress of medical research.

articleTitle: Design and Development of a Web Application for Childcare Assistance Using AI-Code Generation
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: This study addresses the growing demand for effective childcare support amid increasing challenges dual-income households face. We propose a mobile application designed to alleviate parental burdens by transforming routine tasks, such as dressing, tidying, and meal times, into engaging activities for children. Our goal is to foster children's independence and self-reliance by making these tasks enjoyable through game-like interfaces, thereby reducing parental stress and workload. The application will leverage cutting-edge artificial intelligence to balance automated processes with human input, ensuring a user-friendly experience for parents and children. Through this dual approach, the application aims to enhance family quality of life by facilitating efficient, enjoyable childcare experiences. Our research explores the innovative integration of AI within childcare solutions, highlighting its strengths and compensating for its limitations to achieve a balanced, effective platform.

articleTitle: ELPG: End-to-End Latency Prediction for Deep-Learning Model Inference on Edge Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: The demand for running deep learning models on edge devices is increasing. In order to achieve lower latency and higher accuracy on edge devices, many studies have custom-designed deep learning models for edge devices, among which hardware-aware neural architecture search (HW - NAS) is the most successful. HW-NAS require measuring the model's in-ference latency on real edge devices to guide the design of model structures. Directly measuring inference latency on edge devices is prohibitively expensive, leading many works to predict model inference latency using various methods. In this paper, we propose ELPG, an end-to-end inference latency predictor based on Graph Neural Networks and Gate Recurrent Unit. ELPG represents a model as a kernel sequence, and use this sequence as input to predict the model's inference latency. ELPG has no restrictions on the structure of the model and can predict the inference latency of the current advanced CNNs and their variants. Experimental results indicate that ELPG achieves higher prediction accuracy compared to existing methods, and with only 100 latency data, ELPG achieves 82.15% accuracy on Jetson Nano.

articleTitle: Accelerating the Commissioning Process of Wi-SUN FAN Nodes
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Wireless Smart Utility Network Field Area Networks (Wi-SUN FAN) provide a communications infrastructure for very large-scale outdoor networks. In this way, a Wi-SUN FAN lets industrial devices such as smart meters and streetlights interconnect onto one common network. Wireless network commissioning is the first step to establish and configure the Wi-SUN FAN. However, existing commissioning speed is slow and not stable. In this paper, detailed analysis is performed for commissioning process and a dynamic trickle time control method according to network size and density is proposed to accelerate the commissioning process. Experiment results validate the commissioning improvement.

articleTitle: Enhancing Web Service Composition Security with Formal Methods
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to enhance Web service composition through the Web Service Interaction Model (IWSN). The IWSN aims to ensure accurate interaction between Web services, improve composition scalability, resolve behavioral compatibility issues during interaction, and facilitate broader adoption of service composition technologies. Based on the Kahn Process Network (KPN) for its foundation in parallel computing via data streams and channels, the proposed model establishes formal semantics using Calculus of Communication Systems. The model's properties are explored, and its application is illustrated through a case study that demonstrates its effectiveness in web service composition and interaction.

articleTitle: Sparse Multiuser Signatures for Massive Grant-Free Transmissions
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a design of sparse multiuser signatures to increase the capacity of grant-free high-overloading transmissions for massive machine-type-communication (mMTC). The proposed sparse signature is composed of a short spreading sequence and a sparse pattern. The design not only lowers the correlation between the signatures but also brings in additional randomness and sparsity to the sequences. Therefore, it benefits from less-interfered symbol streams to present geometric characteristics of the modulation constellation at the receiving end, which enables blind multiuser detection even if the number of active users is large. The design method can also be applied to highly-correlated spreading sequences, and the correlation is lowered and more users can be supported. Numerical results are provided in terms of block error rate, which demonstrates that the proposed sparse signature has a similar error performance to the optimized schemes while the number of active users is increased sianificantly.

articleTitle: Trajectory Planning of Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor Based on Improved Bidirectional Long Short Term Memory Network
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Because the operation cycle of the CNC system is much longer than the control cycle of the permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM), it is necessary to do high-precision interpolation of the rotation Angle of the PMSM rotor on the position instruction sequence given by the CNC system. At the same time, to ensure the smooth transition of PMSM acceleration, this paper proposes a Bi-LSTM based on attention mechanism (Bi-LSTM-Att) interpolation model. The model introduces the attention mechanism optimization interpolation process, and uses the bidirectional long short-term memory network to analyze the time series data from the front and back directions with the global trend. The evaluation indexes of model verification results and simulation results show that Bi-LSTM-Att has smaller interpolation errors, higher interpolation accuracy and more stable control effect than other interpolation models.

articleTitle: A Color Image Encryption Algorithm Based on Chaos Theory for R, G, B Cross Layer Uniform Shuffle
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Chaotic maps, known for their sensitivity to initial conditions and unpredictability, are widely applied in fields such as secure encryption and communication transmission. This paper introduces a novel two-dimensional chaotic map based on the Singer map from chaos theory and the sine trigonometric function(2D-Sinsinger). Compared to some existing two-dimensional chaotic maps, 2D-Sinsinger exhibits superior ergodicity, hyper-chaotic properties, and unpredictability. Building upon 2D-Sinsinger, this paper designs a color image encryption algorithm (SinsingerIE). SinsingerIE is a novel encryption algorithm tailored for color images, distinct from previous methods involving confusion and diffusion processes. SinsingerIE employs two processes: R, G, B cross-layer shuffling and diffusion. The R, G, B cross-layer shuffling process further comprises two sub-processes: bit-plane-based R, G, B simple pixel shuffling and R, G, B cross-layer regional shuffling. The shuffling algorithm ensures uniformity in the mixing of three channels, significantly reducing the risk of leaking substantial valuable information due to the compromise of a single channel. In subsequent validation experiments, SinsingerIE demonstrates considerable advantages in encrypting large-scale color images, exhibiting excellent security performance compared to other encryption algorithms.

articleTitle: Low Complexity PAPR Reduction Algorithm of OTFS Signal for Integrated Sensing and Communications Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: With the advancement of integrated sensing and communications technology, Orthogonal Time Frequency Space (OTFS) modulation has emerged as an attractive technique in this field due to its superior performance in high-speed mobile environments. However, the high Peak-to-Average Power Ratio (PAPR) of OTFS signals can significantly degrade communication quality, severely limiting their widespread application in practical communication systems. To address this issue, we propose a low-complexity ZCT-TCPTS-ITR algorithm adopting Zadoff-Chu (ZC) sequence precoding, Threshold-Clipping-PTS(TCPTS) algorithm, and Iterative Tone Reservation (ITR) algorithm. Through simulation experiments, we have verified that this algorithm significantly reduces PAPR while maintaining a computational complexity of only 7.38% of the traditional PTS algorithm, with minimal impact on the signal's Bit Error Rate (BER) performance. The results of this study provide an effective solution to the PAPR issue of OTFS modulation technology in integrated sensing and communications systems.

articleTitle: Infrared Small Object Detection Based on Spatial Distribution Fusion and Multi-Scale Upsampling
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Detecting small infrared objects is a challenging task due to the inherent limitations of infrared images, such as insufficient texture information and low spatial resolution. To enhance detection accuracy, we propose an Original Image Attention Module(OIAM), which captures the spatial distribution patterns of objects within the dataset, and integrates the learned spatial distributions with the original image through a spatial attention mechanism. The output of OIAM is fed to the backbone of YOLOv8 to obtain efficient features for object detection. Additionally, we introduce a Multi-Scale Upsampling Module(MSUM) that fuses low- and high-level features during the upsampling phase, further enhancing the features of small infrared objects without increasing computational complexity. Experimental results on the FLIR dataset demonstrate that our method effectively improves the detection accuracy of small infrared objects, achieving a 3% increase in overall mAP@0.5 and a 7.2% improvement in mAP@0.5 for bicycles, which primarily consist of small objects.

articleTitle: Enhancing YOLOv8 with Attention Task Alignment Head for Prohibited Item Detection in Complex X-Ray Images
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Detecting prohibited items in X-ray images is challenging due to the complex backgrounds often encountered in security inspection scenarios. When prohibited items overlap with other objects, the inherent conflict between regression and classification tasks becomes more pronounced. To address this issue, we propose an Attention Task Alignment Head (ATAH) to enhance the YOLOv8 model. ATAH dynamically aligns regression and classification tasks by restructuring the network's extracted features and distributing them across the classification and regression branches. Each branch incorporates a Layer Attention Block (LAB) to adjust weights based on task-specific requirements. Additionally, the regression branch is designed to handle complex spatial variations in the images by utilizing Deformable Convolution (DCN). We also introduce Slide Loss to focus the model's learning on challenging samples. Experimental results on the PIDRay dataset demonstrate that our approach significantly outperforms the YOLOv8 benchmark.

articleTitle: Adaptive Topology Construction for Heterogeneous UAV Clusters in Dynamic Localization Tasks
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) technology is evolving from single-unit autonomy to complex swarm coordination. In highly heterogeneous scenarios, to address the challenges of cooperative localization and maintaining wireless sensor network connectivity, an adaptive clustering algorithm for localization tasks is proposed. This method integrates sensor task types with mobility trend similarities, while also considering key network stability factors such as topology duration, throughput, and end-to-end latency. During the clustering and cluster head selection process, the algorithm ensures that each sub-cluster meets localization requirements. Simulations demonstrate that, compared to the K-means and Group Trend Similarity-based Double-Head Clustering (GTSC) algorithms, the proposed method significantly improves topology duration, localization accuracy, and delay, particularly in large-scale swarms.

articleTitle: Modeling the Dynamic Network for Determined Communication of UAV Swarm
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: With the rapid advancements in communication technology and the evolving dynamics of the modern battlefield, the deployment of UAV swarms in combat scenarios has become increasingly prevalent. The execution of combat missions by UAV swarms requires deterministic communication to ensure multi- UAV coordination. However, wireless networks are significantly influenced by environmental factors and the dynamic changes in network topology during UAV swarm flight present considerable challenges in maintaining deterministic communication for combat missions. To verify whether UAV swarm scenarios can support deterministic communication for combat missions, this paper analyzes and models the dynamic network characteristics of UAV swarms and develops an evaluation model for deterministic communication in dynamic networks. First, the paper analyzes the cluster control and network topology conditions required to achieve deterministic communication in UAV swarm scenarios. It then models the channel quality of the wireless environment and the queuing of UAV node traffic, capturing the boundary effects of dynamic topology changes on end-to-end deterministic transmission. Subsequently, the model is used to evaluate the end-to-end communication performance of combat missions within the UAV swarm. Finally, a simulation experiment scenario is constructed using STK (Satellite Tool Kit) and Exata. The simulation results show that the proposed deterministic communication model effectively constrains the dynamics of the UAV swarm to meet the end-to-end deterministic transmission requirements of combat missions, thereby validating the feasibility of achieving end-to-end deterministic communication within UAV swarms.

articleTitle: A Radio Frequency Fingerprint Identification Method for Wireless Devices Based on Multi-Feature Fusion
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Radio frequency fingerprint identification can be used for device authentication, network access management, malicious device tracking and identity spoofing attacks. Current research on Radio Frequency Fingerprint Identification (RFFI) mostly relies on single signal features, using deep learning algorithms for feature representation and pattern recognition to improve identification capabilities, but there is a problem of low recognition accuracy. Aiming at the problem of wireless device RF fingerprint identification, this article presents a wireless device RF fingerprint recognition method based on multi-feature fusion. This method fuses three signal features with high time-frequency resolution: Short Time Fractional Fourier Transfer (STFRFT), Down Sampling of Short Time Fourier Transfer (DS-STFT) and Smoothed Pseudo Wigner-Ville Distribution (SPWVD) as fingerprints. These are then fed into a deep residual network (ResNet34) for device classification. Simulation experiments show that a series of experiments based on Bluetooth device datasets have verified that the proposed method is superior to single-feature methods in terms of accuracy and robustness. At the same time, even under conditions where a certain signal-to-noise ratio causes signal fluctuations to overwhelm device features, this method can still effectively classify transmitting devices.

articleTitle: Intelligent Hierarchical Neighbor Cell Planning Based on Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In order to improve the timeliness of communication network neighbor planning, solve neighbor omission, enhance planning accuracy, and effectively deal with challenges such as excessive neighbors, this paper proposes an intelligent hierarchical neighbor cell planning method based on neural networks. This method fully utilizes the engineering parameters of communication base stations, existing network indicator data, and existing network neighbor configuration data. Different from traditional planning methods that only consider distance and azimuth, it innovatively introduces factors such as Delaunay triangulation, distance multiple, overlapping coverage area coefficient, and neighbor hierarchy. By using a neural network model, the existing network experience is deeply learned, and new base station neighbors in the communication network are planned intelligently. This method introduces new planning factors, greatly improving the accuracy and timeliness of neighbor planning, and better coping with the evolving communication network environment.

articleTitle: TCP Pacing Without Clock-Based Timing Control for Data Segment Transmission
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: The rate based segment transmission control becomes important along with the increasing bandwidth of communication links. However, most of the pacing procedures for sending data segments in a fixed rate are supported by clock-based timing control, and the clock based software pacing requires heavy processing cost in commodity computers. There are some proposals which do not rely on clocks, but they assume a specific network interfaces. This paper proposes a new TCP pacing scheme which does not use any clock-based timing control, and which does not assume any specific network interfaces. It uses the ACK reception timings even in the slow start phase and expands the data transmission interval by waiting for multiple ACK reception. The performance evaluation through the network simulator shows that our proposal avoids packet losses in a high bandwidth and long delay network.

articleTitle: Performance Enhancement for IRS-Aided NOMA Networks with Underlay D2D Communications*
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: The co-channel interferences inherent in the non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) networks with underlay D2D communications drastically degrade the system performance. Intelligent reflecting surface (IRS) is able to mitigate the co-channel interferences through designing its reflected signals. In this work, an IRS-aided downlink NOMA system with underlay D2D communications is investigated. The expression of the total throughput of NOMA users and D2D terminal is analysed under the consideration of the co-channel interferences.
