An optimization problem is formulated to maximize the total throughput by joint optimizing the phase shifts of IRS, the transmitting power of all links as well as the decoding orders of NOMA users, under the minimum SINRs requirements. A novel dynamic programming approach based on Lagrange duality and genetic algorithm is developed to solve the problem. Finally, the simulation results demonstrate that the total throughput is significantly improved by utilizing IRS with a larger number of reflected elements.

articleTitle: Model Division-Based SeComm: Energy Consumption Minimization by Exploring Semantic Information Similarities
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In semantic communication (SeComm), semantic information (SI) extraction plays a vital part. However, existing research on SeComm did not delve into the inherent similarities of SI, resulting in more energy consumption when transmitting SI from different users. To address this issue, we propose a model division-based SeComm framework. In the framework, the BS divides the users into groups by the similarity of their SI after SI extraction. Then the SI of the users in the same user group is divided into shared and personalized information, which is the process of model division performed by the BS. To minimize energy consumption, we formulated an optimization problem where transmission power, bandwidth, SI extraction ratio, and shared information partition are jointly considered. Since the objective function and the constraints consist of separate terms, we propose an alternative optimization algorithm to solve the problem efficiently. The simulation results show that the proposed algorithm can achieve a minimum energy consumption reduction of 15% under bandwidth-limited conditions, and a minimum energy consumption reduction of 24% under total transmit power-limited conditions compared with reference themes. Moreover, the additional simulation results indicate that the proposed framework exhibits lower latency, making it promising in delay-sensitive communication scenarios.

articleTitle: DMT Airborne Cloud Particle Image Shape Recognition and its Application
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Airborne cloud particle detection equipment is the most direct and effective means to obtain the microphysical characteristics of cloud particles. A number of domestic units have introduced the U.S. DMT (Droplet Measurement Technologies) company's cloud imaging probe CIP (cloud imaging probe). Because its supporting software cannot output detailed information about particles one by one, it limits the indepth mining and analysis of cloud particle image detection data. Firstly, the quality control of particle image data is carried out based on the original data of the particle image. Then the particle shapes are divided into 8 categories according to the geometric characteristics of particle shapes. The gray CIP (cloud imaging probe) detection data obtained from three winter aerial surveys in Henan Province from December 2018 to March 2019 is used to conduct characteristic statistics on the shape of cloud particles and the area of each shape particle. We also compare the mass-scale relationships of different particles with the hydrometeor content, which is calculated by treating the particles as spherical droplets, and find that the latter exceeds the former by about an order of magnitude.

articleTitle: QoS-Aware Routing Algorithm for SDN-Based Integrated Heterogeneous Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In this paper, we design a three-layer architecture under software-defined network (SDN) control in order to solve the problem of communication between heterogeneous networks. In this architecture, we design an optimization problem that varies from different requirements of quality of service (QoS). Afterward, an approach for calculating weights is used in the optimizing objective to find a balance of multiple parameters. Based on solving optimization problems, we propose a mission-classified weighting optimization routing algorithm (MCWO-RA), which makes pertinent improvements in network performance. Simulation results show that MCWO-RA can bring optimization in delay, rate, packet loss rate of mission and meet the requirement of heterogeneous networks.

articleTitle: Efficient Range Search for Hamming Distance Using Function Secret Sharing
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In high-dimensional binary spaces, range search based on Hamming distance remains a crucial tool for ad-vancing research and applications across various fields due to its balance of simplicity, speed, and scalability. This paper presents a range search scheme for Hamming distance based on Function Secret Sharing (FSS), a novel cryptographic primitive that enables secure computation with low communication and computational costs. Additionally, we design a secure Hamming distance computation protocol that eliminates the need for third-party negotiation, allowing the query key to be generated by the querying party, which is more suitable for real-world applications and helps reduce communication overhead and computational costs. Finally, we provide a formal security proof of the proposed protocol and evaluate its performance through experiments, exploring the impact of different parameters. We conducted experiments on three real datasets, adjusting <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$r$</tex> to achieve optimal search rates, and demonstrated the effectiveness and efficiency of the protocol. Compared to existing work, our scheme reduces communication overhead.

articleTitle: A DRL Agent for Federated Learning Resource Allocation in the Internet of Things
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In the Internet of Things (IoT), federated learning aims to facilitate collaborative learning among distributed IoT devices. However, device heterogeneity poses a key challenge for resource allocation in federated learning. Deep reinforcement learning (DRL) has emerged as a promising technique to address the dynamic resource allocation problem. However, existing DRL methods suffer from slow and unstable training during the training process. This paper proposes a federated learning enhanced deep deterministic policy gradient (FL-EDDPG) framework. Firstly, an actor network is designed, combining long short-term memory layers with one-dimensional convolutional layers, to effectively represent states, learn device network states, and address long-term dependencies for rational allocation of computational and communication resources for IoT devices. Secondly, an enhanced dual critic network is introduced, with two independent critic networks fitting state-action value functions for different optimization objectives to reduce estimation errors and improve training stability. FL-EDDPG successfully overcomes issues of slow and unstable training, effectively coordinating computational and communication resources among IoT devices to achieve a balance between federated learning training time and IoT device energy consumption. Experimental results demonstrate that FL-EDDPG reduces the average system cost by 18.3% compared to other state-of-the-art methods.

articleTitle: Temporal-Difference Learning Aided Task Offloading in Air-Ground Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: The current exponential growth in the number of smart devices and the limited computing power of terminal devices make it difficult to solve some complex problems. This study proposes a deep reinforcement learning-based task offloading algorithm in which Temporal-Difference learning is aided to satisfy the demand for low latency and high mobility to improve the quality of service for users. Multi-UAVs are used as nodes for edge computing in an air-ground network, and a multi-intelligent deep deterministic policy gradient algorithm is used to optimize the trajectory of the UAVs as well as to reduce the delay of edge computing and the total energy consumption of the UAVs. Simulation results show that the energy consumption of the UAV is reduced by 14.65%, the average delay of task processing is reduced by 4.06%, and the rate of completing tasks increases by 3.16%-7.86%.

articleTitle: Cooperative NOMA Transmission Through Constellation Remapping on the Bilayer Graph
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel cooperative NOMA scheme named cooperative hierarchical constellation remapping (CHCR). Combining non-orthogonal transmission and relaying, the transmitted symbols utilize permuted modulation mappings on the resource elements from the relay to the destination. Simulated annealing algorithm is employed to optimize the remapping patterns with the objective to maximize the minimum Euclidean distance in the constellation. Two methods of optimization, same-search and diff-search, have been proposed. Leaving the source-destination link untouched, CHCR reduces the solution space and computational complexity required for optimization. Numerical results demonstrate that the minimum Euclidean distance and the bit error rate are significantly improves by our scheme.

articleTitle: New Entanglement-Assisted Concatenated Quantum Codes Exceed Quantum Gilbert-Varshamov Bound
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Quantum error-correction codes leverage encoding and redundancy to effectively detect and correct errors, thereby enhancing the reliability and accuracy of signal detection. Based on the scheme of entanglement-assisted concatenated quantum codes (EACQCs), we construct both new binary and non-binary EACQCs. Several of the new EACQCs achieve better parameters than the best-known standard entanglement-assisted quantum error-correction codes while maintaining the same code lengths and net transmissions. The quantum Gilbert-Varshamov (GV) bound serves as a crucial benchmark for evaluating quantum code parameters. As the code length increases, we construct binary and non-binary EACQCs that exceed the quantum GV bound. Index Terms-entanglement-assisted quantum error-correction code, entanglement-assisted concatenated quantum codes, quan-tum Gilbert-Varshamov bound

articleTitle: A Comparative Study of CNN, ViT, and ResNet50 for Pneumonia Detection in Medical Imaging
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Pneumonia is a common respiratory disease. Early recognition of pneumonia is crucial for treatment and prevention. We use Chest X-ray rays (CXR) to identify pneumonia. With the development of deep learning technology, its application in the field of medical image recognition is more and more extensive. This paper aims to explore the application of convolutional neural network (CNN), Visual Transformer (ViT) and ResNet50 in pneumonia recognition, and compare their performance. By using these methods, the Resnet50 model achieves the highest accuracy of 98.5%, within an average accuracy of 95.4%.

articleTitle: DRL-Based Joint Relay Selection and Power Allocation Strategy in Full-Duplex Eavesdropping Channels
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Full-duplex technology enables the simultaneous transmission of information on the same frequency, thereby theoretically enhancing spectrum efficiency and catering to the requirements of future secure communications. However, the inherent openness and broadcast nature of wireless communication systems significantly compromise the security of data transmission in the presence of eavesdroppers. In order to optimise the safety capacity of the channel and strengthen the safety and reliability of the full-duplex system, we propose a novel strategy that integrates relay selection and power allocation using deep reinforcement learning (DRL). In situations where multiple relay nodes are involved, DRL-based selection methodology is adopted to identify the most suitable relay node. Subsequently, under a joint power constraint, the power allocation scheme ensures optimal distribution of power between the source node and the selected relay node in pursuit of achieving the specified objectives.

articleTitle: Joint User Association and Resource Allocation for Communication-Efficient Hybrid Federated Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Federated Learning (FL) is an efficient distributed machine learning method that builds a shared global model by exchanging model parameters instead of local data, thus protecting user privacy. However, due to the heterogeneity and mobility of user devices, FL experiences high communication latency. To balance learning performance and communication latency, we construct a hybrid federated learning system (HFL) integrating FL and Federated Distillation Learning (FD) in a multi-base station scenario. We propose an optimization problem that jointly considers user mode selection, user association, and resource allocation to minimize communication latency per communication round. To solve this problem, we propose a convex optimization-assisted Double Deep Q-Network (CADDQN) algorithm. Simulation results show that the proposed algorithm outperforms state-of-the-art baselines.

articleTitle: Research on Federated Learning Algorithms for Marine Internet of Things
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Due to its ability to achieve efficient distributed machine learning with low communication overhead and data privacy protection, federated learning has gradually been applied in marine Internet of Things. However, due to the harsh marine environment, federated learning also faces challenges such as slow convergence of global models or even deviation from optimal solutions under heterogeneous data. To address these issues, this paper proposes a device-clustered federated online continuous learning algorithm (DC-FOCL). Specifically, in the device selection phase of DC-FOCL, the K-Means algorithm is used to group the participating devices based on the similarity of their feature maps, which helps mitigate model convergence oscillation issues caused by data heterogeneity. In the local training phase, it abstracts global shared parameters and localspecific parameters based on a parameter decomposition strategy to reduce the communication overhead of the model. Then, an Elastic Weight Consolidation (EWC) penalty is applied to the updates of the global shared parameters to address the catastrophic forgetting problem during the model training process. Comprehensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of DCFOCL in improving model performance.

articleTitle: A Spatio-Temporal Fusion Localization Scheme Based on Carrier Phase Tracking
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Existing carrier phase positioning (CPP) schemes primarily rely on phase difference of arrival (PDOA). However, without strict synchronization among base stations, the accuracy of PDOA-based positioning degrades significantly. To address this issue, we propose a novel CPP algorithm to reduce the need for synchronization and improve precision. We let each base station independently perform phase tracking on a moving target, exploiting the continuity of phase in the time domain. Simultaneously, the phase variations received by different bases should be spatially consistent. We jointly evaluate the phase properties in space-time to solve the problem of integer ambiguity, effectively reducing the need for clock synchronization. By analyzing these phase variation properties, we perform an asymptotic search to locate the target and obtain the best estimate. Simulation results prove the superiority of our algorithm.

articleTitle: A Receiver System for WiFi-6 Communication Using GaAs pHEMT Process
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: A receiver system that can be applied to wireless fidelity (WiFi) communication using the gallium arsenide (GaAs) pseudomorphic high electron mobility transistor (pHEMT) process is proposed in this paper. Based on the GaAs pHEMT process, the implementation approaches of the logic control and power regulator required for the WiFi receiver system are proposed in this paper. In addition, the necessary radio frequency (RF) modules, such as the low noise amplifier (LNA) and single pole double throw (SPDT) switch, are also implemented in the same chip. The final designed receiver system consumes a quiescent current of 17 mA with a chip area of 0.7 * 1.3 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The final simulated and test results show that this receiver system has good performance in all operating modes whose LNA path has a gain of 15 dB, a noise figure of 1.9 dB, and a P1dB of 15 dBm; the bypass path has a received signal attenuation of 8 dB; the transmission path has a power capacity of 31 dBm and an SPDT switch insertion loss of 0.6 dB; the power management module can digitally output a stable 3 V voltage with a load capacity of 20 mA.

articleTitle: Fusion-Based Automated Domain Ontology Construction Method
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Ontology is a crucial component of the Semantic Web, enabling knowledge sharing and reuse across data sources by organizing information into a knowledge network. Currently, domain ontologies are primarily constructed manually by domain experts. However, due to the typically unstructured or semi-structured nature of data sources, combined with large data volumes and the difficulty of content evaluation, the construction process is inefficient. Furthermore, relying on a single data source often fails to ensure the completeness of an ontology. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a fusion-based method for automated domain ontology construction. This approach integrates two types of data sources: relational databases and domain-specific texts (such as research papers and books). The method involves converting relational databases into domain ontology using the RDB2RDF standard, training a domain concept extraction model to identify concepts from texts, and employing pattern matching to extract relationships between concepts for ontology construction. Finally, ontology merging techniques are used to combine data from both sources, generating the final ontology. Using the field of electronic components as a case study, the proposed method was evaluated by domain experts, who confirmed the ontology's comprehensiveness and validated the approach's effectiveness.

articleTitle: Research and Implementation of Front-end Component Virtualization Asynchronous Rendering Method Based on Cache Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: With the increasing complexity of Web applications, front-end development faces great challenges in terms of performance optimization and user experience. Traditional front-end rendering methods often face problems such as long loading time, high memory usage and poor interaction fluency when dealing with large amounts of data and complex interfaces. This paper proposes a virtual asynchronous rendering method for front-end components based on cache mechanism, which aims to improve the rendering performance of large data sets and reduce unnecessary DOM operation and memory consumption. By managing component instances through object pooling, combined with virtualized rendering and caching mechanisms, the system renders only elements within the current viewport range, and manages the component lifecycle through reference counting mechanisms. Experiments show that this method can effectively improve page rendering efficiency, reduce memory consumption, and greatly improve user experience, especially when dealing with big data lists.

articleTitle: Lightweight Object Detection Method Based on Improved YOLOv8
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Although the existing object detection model has good performance, it is not suitable for deployment and operation on edge devices such as smart cars due to its many parameters, large amount of computation and complex model. In order to improve the detection accuracy of smart cars in the distribution process, a lightweight object detection method based on improved YOLOv8 is proposed, and partial convolution is replaced by AKConv convolution. Reduce the number of parameters in the model; The original loss function CloU is replaced by WloUv3 to reduce the influence of low-quality target samples on the results. To further reduce the size of the model, the detection Head is replaced with Adaptive Head. Experiments show that compared with YOLOv8n in VOC data set, mAP50, Recall and Precision of the proposed target detection method increase by 1 %, 1 % and 2.8% respectively, and the amount of computation and parameter number decrease by 13.6% and 12.9% respectively. Compared with YOLOv8n, the new model has the characteristics of fewer parameters and higher detection accuracy, which has greater advantages for deployment on edge devices such as intelligent vehicles.

articleTitle: Analysis and Optimization of Hierarchical ID-Based Encryption for MQTT
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: With the widespread adoption of Internet of Things (IoT), the number of IoT devices has increased significantly. To facilitate efficient data transmission on these devices, researchers have proposed numerous communication protocols. Among them, the Message Queueing Telemetry Transport (MQTT) protocol based on the publish/subscribe model is widely used. However, by default, the data transmissions with MQTT are plaintext. The MQTT specification recommends using TLS protocol to encrypt the MQTT packet. Due to the high computation cost of TLS, Fan et al. [1] propose a data protection scheme based on hierarchical ID-based encryption utilizing the topic hierarchy in MQTT. In this paper, we conduct a detailed analysis of their subscription algorithm with a multi-level wildcard and identify a security issue related to the leakage of the secret key in their scheme. Also, we present three possible solutions to address this problem.

articleTitle: Investigations on Disk Performance Indices and Their Statistical Learning for Storage Cluster Disk Fail-Slow Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Disks are critical components of data center storage systems, and their health directly affects system stability. However, when a disk enters a fail-slow state, it continues to function but experiences significant performance degradation, leading to slower response time and negatively affecting business service quality. Being different from disk failure, the fail-slow state is hard to be detected by using traditional disk failure detection methods. The scenario of fail-slow is very complex, therefore a flexible fail-slow processing framework is required, and the detection must be carried out on the premise of ensuring the reliability and high availability of the storage system. To address this challenge, we propose a non-invasive and adaptive method for fail-slow disk detection in storage clusters in this paper. Firstly, a latency prediction model is proposed to intelligently correlate disk performance metrics from a database. Based on this, we propose a health index-based monitoring strategy for fail-slow disk states and cluster health assessment. After deployment in a real production environment, this method has monitored thousands of disks, effectively identifying dozens of fail-slow disks and mitigating business risks caused by hardware issues.

articleTitle: Athlete-LLMs: A Specialized Large Language Model for Athlete Psychology
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Although there are many large language models (LLMs) in the field of psychology, they typically focus on general psychological issues without specialized support for specific populations. Currently, no large models exist that focus on the mental health of a specific group to provide personalized psychological assistance. This paper introduces the first large language model specifically designed for athlete psychology, Athlete-LLM, aimed at helping athletes stabilize their mindset before and after competitions, as well as during regular training.

articleTitle: SecPro-INT: Secure Programmable In-Band Network Telemetry Method
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In-band network telemetry (INT) can monitor network status in real-time and with high precision. It has attracted more and more attention from academia and industry. However, traditional INT system uses plaintext to transmit telemetry data, and is vulnerable to network attacks. This paper focuses on the security issues and designs a customizable encryption method in INT. In order to effectively balance security and transmission performance, this paper propose a dynamic feedback scheduling mechanism based on “security level +performance loss” Based on this, SecPro-INT as a secure INT system is designed. The experimental results indicate that Secpro-INT can quickly switch encryption algorithms based on network conditions during working. It ensures both the safety of in band telemetry and the normal operation of the network

articleTitle: A Time-Frequency Synchronization for Ka-band Inter Satellite Link of the Navigation Satellite System
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Satellite navigation systems provide global coverage, offering continuous worldwide navigation, positioning, and timing functions. These satellites are equipped with Ka-band inter-satellite links, which enable distance measurement and information transmission, thereby providing emergency tracking and control functions for overseas spacecraft. Due to these links being the only means of measurement and emergency communication when ground measurement and control stations are unable to reach, an increasing number of overseas spacecrafts are attempting to connect to these Ka-band inter-satellite link<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sup>. The extended users such as space stations, satellites, and other spacecraft, constrained by weight and power limitations, are unable to carry atomic clocks for high-precision time-frequency references, therefore they can't connect to Ka-band inter-satellite links using traditional time-frequency synchronization methods. This paper proposes a novel time-frequency synchronization method for non-atomic clock spacecraft with low time-frequency accuracy connecting to the Ka-band inter-satellite links of navigation satellites, which is proposed for the first time in China. After completing pointing calculations and one-way capture tracking with limited time slot, the extended users collect one-way ranging data between navigation satellites, construct a clock estimation model, calculate clock offset parameters, and compensate for time and frequency, which can increase the accuracy of time and frequency by 20 times. In the case of limited time slot resources for Ka-band inter-satellite links, this technology solves the problem of high-precision time-frequency synchronization between non atomic clock extended users and navigation satel-lites, and realizes the low-time-frequency accuracy extended users connecting to the navigation inter-satellite link for the first time in our country, greatly improving the availability of Ka-band inter-satellite links. The technology has been applied in orbit and the ranging accuracy has reached 0.5 meters, which is at the leading level in China. It also enables overseas satellites and spacecraft to connect to Ka-band inter-satellite links, providing emergency tracking and control functions for overseas spacecraft, improving survivability of spacecraft and achieving significant social and political benefits.

articleTitle: Low-Complexity Equalization for STBC-OCDM System Under Doubly Dispersive Channels
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Orthogonal chirp division multiplexing (OCDM) is a promising multi-carrier scheme that efficiently leverages multipath diversity through the use of chirp spread spectrum. In this paper, a novel Alamouti space–time block coded OCDM system is proposed to achieve significant diversity gains at low complexity. Subsequently, two frequency domain equalizers for compensation of channel dispersion are investigated, and the banded structure of the equivalent channel matrix is utilized to reduce complexity. Moreover, we propose a low-complexity iterative detection method based on reliable region which estimates reliable symbols by LSMR and then performs interference cancellation. Numerical results demonstrate the advantage of the proposed low-complexity scheme under doubly dispersive channels in bit error rate (BER) performances compared to the classical orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) scheme.

articleTitle: Intelligent Framework for Multi-UAV-Enabled Joint Offloading Service and Trajectory Planning in MEC
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) have a pivotal role in mobile edge computing (MEC) applications. In a UAV-based MEC framework, data generated by user equipments (UEs) on the ground can be offloaded to servers carried by the UAVs for expedited processing. Nonetheless, the diversity of computational tasks leads to uneven data distribution across UEs. Additionally, the energy consumption of UAVs for hovering and movement must be carefully managed to ensure sustainable flight and effective data analysis and processing. In this work, we tackle the NP-hard problem associated with integer service association in MEC systems by developing a potential game-based model that efficiently resolves the service association between UAVs and UEs. Building on this strategy, we develop a Grey Wolf Optimization (GWO) based trajectory planning method to explore the flight paths of the UAVs. This intelligent framework ensures a balanced and efficient operation of the MEC system, addressing key challenges in service association during task offloading and UAV trajectory planning. Simulation results demonstrate that our proposed MUJST not only ensures efficient convergence but also minimizes the offloading time for UEs and reduces UAV energy consumption.

articleTitle: Multi-UPF Traffic Prediction of 5G Core Network With Multi-Task Learning and Multi-core Parallel Computing
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Traffic prediction has become a key aspect of 5G core network management. However, predicting traffic for multiple User Plane Functions (Multi-UPF) has received limited attention. To achieve effective and efficient forecasting for Multi-UPF traffic with machine learning, this study proposes a framework combining multi-task learning and multi-core parallel computing. Firstly, the time-series traffic data of Multi-UPF is concatenated to form the input feature. Then, Random Forest algorithm is used as the backbone of the multi-task learning-based prediction model, which is able to predict the traffic of each UPF simultaneously. Finally, the computation of the multi-task learning model is further accelerated through multi-core parallel processing. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed multi-task learning approach outperforms single-task learning method in the accuracy of each UPF traffic prediction. Furthermore, the use of multi-core parallel computing enhances the prediction speed significantly.

articleTitle: GLMLog: Log Anomaly Detection Method Based on ChatGLM
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: The massive scale of logs makes manual analysis of logs impractical. The log anomaly detection scheme based on deep learning also faces many challenges, including the diversification of log types and the rapid increase size of log data. The recent emergence of large language Models provides a new solution for log anomaly detection. Therefore, this paper proposes a novel log anomaly detection scheme based on ChatGLM2-6B, and we call it as GLMLog. We develop GLMLog on ChatGLM2-6B which is pretraininged. Furthermore, ChatGLM2-6B is fine tuned through LoRA fine-tuning using publicly available log data according to the needs of log anomaly detection. In order to more accurately detect the anomaly, GLMLog implements log anomaly detection from content sequences and event sequences. We completed validation testing using the logs provided by LogHub as the dataset. Experimental result shows that after a small number of rounds of fine-tuning, GLMLog can achieve log anomaly detection and its F1-score is basically consistent with Deeplog.

articleTitle: Lightweight U-Net Image Dehazing Network for Remote Airport Tower Control
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Image dehazing is a significant part of low-level vision tasks in the area of airport traffic surveillance. However, the existing image dehazing methods based on deep learning suffer from the limitation on both model generalization and computational cost. A lightweight U-Net dehazing network based on improved inverted residual block (IIRB) and adaptive detail enhancement (ADE) module is proposed for remote airport tower control. Firstly, the low and mid-frequency feature was extracted with IIRB module from image smooth regions. Secondly, the high- frequency details and textures were extracted with ADE module, which further led to the enhancement of the network's expression in sky regions and detail features. Finally, the model was trained combining L1 loss and contrastive loss, which aimed to improve the model's generalization. To evaluate the effectiveness and practicality of the proposed method, the experiments were conducted both on SOTS dataset and real samples of airport hazy images. The experimental results show that, compared to lightweight AOD and weakly supervised RefineD, the proposed method achieves a balance between visual quality and real-time performance.

articleTitle: Channel Measurement and Comparative Analysis of 6.8 GHz and 13 GHz in Outdoor Scenarios
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: The extensive rollout of next-generation wireless communication systems demands additional spectrum resources, with mid-frequency electromagnetic waves showing significant potential for application. To comprehend the signal characteristics within this frequency band, this paper presents channel measurements at 6.8 GHz and 13 GHz conducted in an outdoor campus setting, including both line-of-sight (LoS) and non-line-of-sight (NLoS) scenarios. The analysis and comparison cover channel power delay profile (PDP), path loss, delay spread, and azimuth angle Spread of Arrival (ASA). The path loss for both frequency bands aligns well with the path loss model specified by the Third Generation Partnership Project (3GPP) TR 38.901. When compared to the 13 GHz channel, the 6.8 GHz channel shows more pronounced multipath effects, exhibiting higher delay spread and angular spread values. However, the observed angular spread is lower than the reference values provided by 3GPP. These research findings offer valuable insights for applying new frequency bands in 6G massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems.

articleTitle: GMSEflow: Learning Optical Flow Through Global Matching with Squeeze-and-Excitation Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Estimating optical flow is crucial for numerous computer vision tasks, including autonomous vehicles, object tracking, and image frame interpolation. Yet, the challenge of improving optical flow estimation precision while managing the complexity of computational structures remains formidable. This study presents GMSEflow, an innovative model for optical flow estimation that incorporates a global multi-scale attention mechanism. We have refined the SENet architecture to allow the network to capture fine details across different scales in intricate images more effectively. The enhancements to the GMflow framework are tailored to optimize the optical flow learning process. Extensive experiments using the Sintel dataset confirm that our method outperforms other techniques in terms of accuracy. These findings represent a significant step forward in optical flow research, offering theoretical insights and practical implications for technological progress in associated domains.

articleTitle: On Channel Coverage of MIMO Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Coverage is an important issue addressed in cell planning for mobile communication systems. In conventional single-input single-output (SISO) systems, cell coverage is mainly determined by path loss or the strength of the received signal at cell edge. However, with the introduction of multiple-input and multiple-output (MIMO) technique, it is not appropriate to use only the path loss to estimate coverage any more. Apparently, more factors, such as the number of antennas and channel capacity, should also be considered. In this paper, on the basis of Shannon capacity, we propose a new concept of so-called channel coverage for MIMO systems. When the channel state information (CSI) is not available at transmitter, we derive its lower and upper bounds which are the random variables related to channel matrix. By using random matrix theory, the exact close-form expressions for their mean and variance are then derived, which are observed to coincide well with the simulation results.

articleTitle: An On-Chip Temperature Sensor and its Application in Millimeter-Wave Low Noise Amplifier
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Based on 130nm BiCMOS technology., an on-chip temperature sensor and its application in a K band Low Noise Amplifier (LNA) with low temperature-dependent gain variation is introduced in this paper. The proposed temperature sensor consists of a temperature detector and hysteresis comparators., and provides a 3-bit digital output for gain calibration. With the help of the temperature sensor., the proposed LNA achieves excellent temperature-dependent gain variation performance., with 1.4 dB gain variation from -45°C to 85°C in measurement.

articleTitle: DB-YOLOv8 Model: Object Detection in Complex Scenarios
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: The improved DB-YOLOv8 model aims to address the issues of missed detection and false detection that are prone to occur in object detection tasks under complex scenarios, particu-larly in the case of overlapping objects and multiple identical ob-jects. It targets the limitations of the YOLO backbone network caused by fixed kernels that lead to restricted receptive fields and insufficient multi-scale feature learning capabilities due to the in-ability of the spatial and channel attention fusion mechanism to adapt to the input data feature distribution. The DB- YOLOv8 model introduces the deformable convolution C2f (D _ C2f) module in the backbone network to achieve adaptive adjustment of the network's receptive field. Additionally, the BiFPN structure is in-troduced in the Neck network, allowing information to propagate bi-directionally between different resolution levels, thereby better fusing multi-scale information. Experimental results demonstrate the outstanding performance of the DB-YOLOv8 model on the VOC and COCO datasets. Validation confirms that its mAP50 and mAP50-95 metrics are improved by 3.3% and 4.7% compared to the YOLOv8 model, respectively.

articleTitle: Joint Optimization of Scalable Encoding Setting and Resource Allocation for Wireless Video Multicast
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Dynamically reconfiguring video encoding parame-ters provides more flexibility to accommodate the diverse and time-varying user's channel conditions to improve the overall service quality of wireless scalable video multicast, which has yet been well addressed in the literature. In this paper, we propose a cross-layer optimization strategy that combines encoding settings configuration, radio blocks allocation as well as modulation and coding scheme assignment for wireless scalable video multicast. The joint optimization problem to maximize the system utility of multicast group is formulated as integer programming. To solve the formulated NP-hard problem to meet the demands of online real-time computing and optimization, a heuristic greed algorithm with slight computational burden is developed. Comparative simulation results show the effectiveness of the proposed strategy.

articleTitle: Micro Frequency Hopping Spread Spectrum Modulation and Encryption Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: By combining traditional frequency hopping ideas with the concepts of subcarriers and sampling points in OFDM baseband systems, this paper proposes a frequency hopping technology within the baseband, termed micro frequency hopping. Based on the concept of micro frequency hopping, this paper proposes a micro frequency hopping spread spectrum modulation and demodulation method based on cyclic frequency shift and cyclic time shift, as well as a micro frequency hopping encryption method based on phase scrambling of baseband signals. Especially, this paper reveals a kind of linear micro frequency hopping symbol with good auto-correlation and cross-correlation feature in both time domain and frequency domain. Linear micro frequency hopping symbols with different roots R have good cross-correlation feature, which can be used in multi-user communication at the same time and the same frequency. Moreover, there is a linear relationship between the time delay and frequency offset in this linear micro frequency hopping symbol, making it suitable for time delay and frequency offset estimation, also for ranging and speed measurement. The author believes that micro frequency hopping technology will be widely used in fields such as the Internet of Things, military communication, satellite communication, satellite positioning, and radar etc.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Comparative Analysis of Metaheuristic Algorithms Rooted in Mathematical Principles
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In recent years, there has been a burgeoning development of swarm intelligence-based metaheuristic algorithms, with those integrating mathematical principles and stochastic search strategies particularly capturing attention. These algorithms, through their unique mechanisms, effectively reconcile the contradiction between exploration and exploitation in traditional single/multi-population evolutionary algorithms, paving new avenues for individual optimization. To aid in future algorithm selection and application, this paper systematically evaluates the performance of eight recently developed math-inspired metaheuristic algorithms on the CEC 2022 benchmark suite, which encompasses complex problems of 20 dimensions. The robustness of the assessment results was ensured through the implementation of Wilcoxon rank-sum tests and Friedman rank tests. The experimental data reveal that, under 20 dimensions, the Geometric Mean Optimizer (GMO) algorithm demonstrated the most outstanding performance in addressing the 12 tests of CEC 2022, with the Gradient-Based Optimizer (GBO) and Exponential Distribution Optimizer (EDO) algorithms following closely, forming a competitive tier. While the Runge-Kutta Optimizer (RUN), PID-based Search Algorithm (PSA), Sine Cosine Optimizer (SCHO), Newton-Raphson-Based Optimizer (NRBO), and Arithmetic Optimization Algorithm (AOA) each have their distinctive features, they overall rank slightly lower, with their own applicable scenarios and limitations.

articleTitle: EEGTCW: Electroencephalogram-based Chinese Words Decoding
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: With the evolution of artificial intelligence technology and the exploration of brain science, more and more researchers are committed to the decoding of brain signals, and the application of brain-computer interface(BCI) is constantly updated. Electroencephalogram(EEG) signals are non-invasive signals that have attracted increasing attention due to their non-transplantability and high temporal resolution. This paper focuses on the decoding of EEG signals to Chinese words, and proposes a novel framework, EEGTCW, which is based on the BiGRU-Attention-CNN classification model and data augmentation method to decode EEG signals into categories corresponding to Chinese words on a self-built dataset. The classification accuracy reaches 0.88, while exploring the gener-alization performance of the model under different batches of a single subject and generalization performance across subjects. It has certain reference value for the improvement of BCI assistant system for speech disorder people.

articleTitle: Research on a Clinical Data Classification Model Based on BERT, Bi-LSTM, and Attention Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In the field of medical diagnosis, patients' clinical data encompass information such as their primary symptoms, current disease progression, past treatment experiences, and examination results, which are crucial for physicians to accurately grasp the condition and formulate treatment plans. Clinical data from patients are typically recorded in the form of long-text documents. Therefore, to better analyze clinical long-text data and enhance the accuracy and efficiency of clinical diagnosis, this paper proposes a clinical long-text classification model that integrates the BERT model, named L-A-BERT. The L-A-BERT model combines the deep bidirectional representation capabilities of BERT, the long and short-term memory characteristics of the Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory network (LSTM), and attention mechanisms to better understand and analyze clinical long-text data. The study employed real patient data for experimental analysis, and the results demonstrated that the L-A-BERT model performs exceptionally well in clinical long-text classification tasks, with the effectiveness of each component within the model further validated through ablation experiments.

articleTitle: Polling Resource Scheduling for Internet of Vehicles Based on U-Net Semantic Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: With the continuous development of Internet of vehicles (IoV) and intelligent transportation system (ITS), infor-mation interaction and resource sharing between vehicles have become increasingly important. However, the resource scheduling problem in IoV has been the main bottleneck restricting its fur-ther development. This paper proposes a semantic segmentation method based on U-Net deep learning architecture and applies it to the polling scheduling problem in the IoV environment to achieve the optimal allocation of resources. The simulation results show that compared with the traditional polling scheduling method, the semantic segmentation method combined with U-Net can significantly save bandwidth resources and reduce image transmission delay. Specifically, our algorithm achieves a 97 % bandwidth savings and a 90% reduction in image transmission delay. In the corresponding semantic segmentation algorithm, the U - Net algorithm also outperforms the SegNet algorithm model in real-time transmission of Internet of Vehicles image resources, which verifies its potential in resource scheduling optimization.

articleTitle: Multi-Step Online Scheduling to Improve Schedulability for In-Vehicle Time-Sensitive Networking
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: With the rapid development of intelligent vehicles, traditional in-vehicle networks struggle to provide real-time communication capacity. Time-Sensitive Networking (TSN) enables intelligent vehicles with high bandwidth, ultra-low latency and deterministic communications. One of the key mechanisms is the Time-Aware Shaper (TAS), which schedules real-time flows by a system-wide table to guarantee low latency and bounded jitter. Different from factory scenarios, the scheduling process of flows in vehicle networks needs to be online and make low disturbance to the system considering the safety-critical applications. Besides, with the large amount of flows involved in vehicle systems, the high schedulability demand of the scheduling algorithm is significantly arising. In this paper, we propose a multi-step online scheduling method, trying to reschedule flows selected by a metric, measuring the disturbance, when there is no feasible schedule for the new arriving flow. Evaluation shows that our method can improve 10% of schedulability in large-scale dynamic networks such as modern Intelligent vehicles.

articleTitle: YOLO v8_CAT: Enhancing Small Object Detection in Traffic Light Recognition with Combined Attention Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: This paper introduces YOLO v8_CAT, an advanced object detection model designed to improve the accuracy of small and challenging object detection in traffic light recognition tasks. Traditional object detection models, including earlier YOLO versions, often struggle with accurately detecting small objects and differentiating traffic light states (GREEN, RED, YELLOW, and OFF) due to limited feature refinement capabilities. YOLO v8_CAT enhances the baseline YOLOvS model by incorporating a Combined Attention Mechanism (CAT), which integrates channel and spatial attention paths to prioritize critical features. The channel attention path focuses on essential feature channels, while the spatial attention path emphasizes important regions, allowing YOLO v8_CAT to handle small and complex objects more effectively. Evaluated on the Bosch Small Traffic Lights Dataset, YOLO v8_CAT demonstrates significant performance improvements, achieving 84.5% accuracy for GREEN, 63.8% for RED, 21.5% for YELLOW, and 25.8% for OFF, outperforming YOLOv8 by notable margins. In particular, YOLO v8_CAT shows a 12.4% increase in accuracy for GREEN and an 8% improvement for RED detection. Additionally, YOLO v8_CAT maintains the high real-time processing speed of YOLOv8 at 1010 FPS. These results establish YOLO v8_CAT as a superior model for traffic light detection in autonomous driving, enhancing both detection precision and robustness without compromising computational efficiency.

articleTitle: Accelerating Transformer Architectures for Automatic Modulation Classification via Gated Activation Patch Selection
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to Automatic Modulation Classification (AMC) that leverages a Gated Activation Patch Selection (GAPS) mechanism to enhance the efficiency of Transformer architectures. Our method addresses the computational challenges associated with Transformer-based AMC models by filtering out less informative signal patches before processing. The GAPS module utilizes convolutional layers to extract key features from the input signal and quantifies the importance of each patch through adaptive aggregation. By employing a Transformer encoder, the selected critical patches are transformed into embeddings, facilitating self-attention computations. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method not only maintains competitive classification performance but also significantly reduces computational complexity, resulting in faster training and lower inference latency. Notably, our method achieves a 17.94% FLOPs reduction without any loss in performance, along with a similar degree of training acceleration, while the model's accuracy decreases by only 1.50% when the input signal length is reduced by 50%.

articleTitle: A Novel Code Update Method for FPGA Based on PCIe Slots
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: The code update of the FPGA board in real-time simulator on the market mostly utilizes JTAG cables. Due to the large size of binary files and slow download speed, updating codes on multiple boards take a lot of time with frequent insertion and removal of JTAG connector, which is not conducive to later maintenance. This article proposes a method for updating FPGA codes based on PCIe slots, which can achieve a parallel process of code update in multiple FPGA boards through the PCIe interface of the real-time HIL simulator, without the need of redundant devices. Firstly, the paper establishes the receiving and flashing mechanism of the binary update file based on XDMA IP core. Secondly, accomplishes the function of scanning PCIe devices and controlling the code update process separately based on Qt software. Finally, the experiment captures the waveform and verifies the correctness of the method by comparing the downloaded file with the read back file. The method proposed in this article improves the download speed of the update file, reduces the difficulty of operation, and does not require additional chips, thereby saving development costs.

articleTitle: Waveform Design for Integrated Sensing and Communication Based on Hybrid Beamforming
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: This paper presents a waveform design method for integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) system based on hybrid beamforming. The directional pattern forms several different beams in the space domain, which point to the communication direction and the radar perception direction respectively. It can detect the radar target and send modulated information to the communication user using the direction modulation (DM) technology. The detection performance was optimized by maximizing the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of radar echo signal under the constraints on user communication quality and transmitter power. The resulting beam response and phase response both demonstrate the effectiveness of the design.

articleTitle: Secrecy Rate Maximization for a MISO-ISAC System with Multiple Eavesdropping Targets
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: This work investigates an integrated sensing and communication system with multiple eavesdropping targets and communication legitimate users. To ensure the security of transmitted information and sensing multiple eavesdropping targets, we strive to maximize the sum secrecy rate by designing transmit beamforming and artificial noise matrices under constraints on beampattern similarity and transmit power budget. We reformulate the underlying problem is reformulated into a quadratically constrained quadratic programming problem using a lower linearization approach and solve it via a semidefinite program approach to obtain the optimum solutions. Furthermore, a robust design is further proposed to counteract to the effects of inevitable channel imperfections of eavesdropping targets. Simulation results validate the effectiveness of the proposed design in secrecy transmission and target sensing, as well as the robustness against channel imperfection of eavesdropping targets.

articleTitle: Modulation Order Identification of CPM Signals Based on Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: The modulation order is a crucial parameter of continuous phase modulation (CPM) signals. Its accurate identification is a fundamental prerequisite for achieving blind demodulation of CPM signals in non-collaborative communication. By exploring the inherent characteristics of CPM signals and the correlations among their parameters, this paper proposes a deep learning approach for modulation order identification of CPM signals based on exponential adjustment. Specifically, the instantaneous frequency derived from signal preprocessing serves as the input to the deep learning model, and a modulation index estimator is employed to approximate the modulation index of the signal. Subsequently, the estimated modulation index is utilized to adjust the instantaneous frequency of the signal, which is then fed into a recognition neural network for feature extraction and classification. The experimental results demonstrate that the method is applicable to a wide range of CPM signals, with superior recognition accuracy and noise immunity compared to traditional algorithms.

articleTitle: DDQN Based Adaptive Multi-Channel MAC Protocol for UAV Ad-Hoc Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicle ad-hoc networks (UANETs) are widely used in military and civilian applications. This paper introduces a double deep Q-Networks (DDQN) based adaptive multi-channel media access control protocol (DAM-MAC) for UANETs. The proposed protocol enables each node to maintain an available channel table to select suitable channels and sets different contention windows for each channel through the DDQN algorithm, dynamically adjusting based on historical information and current network conditions. A multi-channel simulation model on the OMNeT++ platform is employed to emulate the complex communication environment in UANETs. The simulation result shows that DAM-MAC significantly improves network performance such as packet loss, latency and throughput compared to the Q-Learning MAC protocol.

articleTitle: Intergrated Sensing and Communications (ISAC) in 5G-Advanced for High-Precison Localization and Tracking of Vessels at Sea
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Integrated Sensing and Communication (ISAC) is one of the key technologies in 5G-A. The core idea is to integrate communication and awareness functions in the same system, use the same radio resources to improve resource utilisation, and enhance the performance of each of the communication and awareness subsystems. The application scenarios of ISAC are very rich, such as high-precision positioning and tracking, simultaneous imaging, map building and positioning, human sensory enhancement and gesture and expression recognition. However, most of the applications and technologies are limited to the theoretical level, and there are few practical application cases on the ground. In this paper, we experiment with the high-precision localisation and tracking applications in the theory of ISAC using a group network built according to practical needs. The 128TR self-transmitting and self-receiving 5G-A sensing integration base station we set up in a sea area successfully carries out high-precision positioning and area alerts for a ship's sea mission. Our experimental results indicate that the longest coverage distance can be up to about 21km, and a long detection distance can be guaranteed regardless of whether the vessel is travelling at a low speed (e.g. 4.5m/s) or a high speed (e.g. 8.3m/s). Finally, we also analyse the technical difficulties and future development directions in the field of ISAC.

articleTitle: Joint Opportunistic Scheduling and Power Optimization for Covert Satellite Terrestrial Integrated Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In this research, we explore covert communications in a representative satellite terrestrial integrated network (STIN) which is made up of several potential relays and the public users. To ensure the covertness of downlink transmissions, partial users are used as cooperative jammers. It is proved that our proposed opportunistic scheduling scheme can significantly improve covert performance of the STIN. Specifically, the downlink from satellite to users with the highest signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio is chosen for covert transmission. On this foundation, the analytical expression of detection error probability at a warden is derived. Moreover, we further derive the effective covert rate, which is the important factor to indicate the efficiency of the considered covert network. Then, to further enhance system's covert performance, the transmit power of the satellite and the jammer are optimized, respectively. Finally, some simulations are presented to show the effectiveness of our proposed scheme, and prove that there exists one best power setting for the covert STIN.

articleTitle: YOLv5s-DDC: A Rapid Detection Network for Strip Steel Surface Defects Based on Deformable Convolution with Coordinate Attention and Distribution Shifting Convolution
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Surface defect detection in strip steel is essential for improving product quality. Current methods using machine vision and image processing struggle with multiscale variations, irregular distributions, and complex shapes. This paper proposes the YOLOv5s-DDC algorithm based on deformable convolution, distribution shifting convolution, and attention mechanism. To tackle complex shapes and small targets in strip surface defects, this paper introduces the C3-DC in the backbone, which integrates deformable convolution and coordinate attention mechanisms. This module can adapt to changes in the shape and size of strip surface defects. Additionally, this paper introduces the C3-DSConv in the neck, integrating YOLOv5s's C3 with distribution shifting convolution. C3-DSConv improves strip surface defect detection without increasing parameters and computations. Experimental results show that YOLOv5s-DDC reaches an mAP@0.5 of 80.4% on the NEU-DET dataset, improving by 4.2% over the original YOLOv5s. The algorithm has a fast convergence speed and meets the needs of the metallurgical industry.

articleTitle: A Hierarchical Network-Based Security Posture Assessment Method for Power Monitoring System
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Aiming at the problem of network security posture assessment in the existing attack classification system of electric power monitoring system, this paper researches the security posture assessment method of electric power monitoring system based on hierarchical analysis network. This research analyzes the security posture of the system from the device layer and the network layer, and designs the assessment index system based on the grey clustering analysis method, and optimizes the index weights by combining with the gravitational search algorithm, and finally obtains the network security posture perception model. The model presents the overall network state through hierarchical analysis, and simulation experiments show that the proposed method can obtain accurate and detailed network security situation information.

articleTitle: Research on Academic and Career Planning Model Based on Graph Neural Network and Transfer Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: This paper presents an academic and career planning model based on Graph Neural Networks (GNN) and Transfer Learning, aimed at addressing the challenges of major selection and career planning in the context of college entrance exam recommendations. The proposed model utilizes GNN to model the relationships between students' subject choices and career inclinations, effectively capturing complex relational information. To mitigate the challenges posed by few-shot dataset, Transfer Learning is introduced by incorporating pre-trained models, which enhance the generalization capability of the GNN. Additionally, the SMOTE algorithm is employed to handle the class imbalance in the dataset, further improving the classification performance of the model. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed model performs exceptionally well on imbalanced datasets, providing more scientifically sound and personalized recommendations for students' major selection. The model offers enhanced guidance for students' academic and career planning, ensuring more accurate and tailored advice.

articleTitle: Design of Coaxial Cable Transmission System in Complex Environment Based on FPGA
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: This paper designs and implements a coaxial cable communication system based on FPGA, and studies the influence of damage to the shielding layer or outer conductor of the coaxial cable on the transmission performance. The paper includes overall system design requirements, hardware design, transmission line model research, and software design. After multiple tests, the communication system is stable, with a low packet loss rate, which is of reference significance for data transmission of baseband coaxial cables.

articleTitle: A Research on Gas Safety Knowledge Graph and Retrieval-Augmented Generation Mechanism Based on Large Language Model
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Along with the advancement of modernization, gas safety has become more and more an area of concern. However, there is a lack of research on the mechanism of applying large language models(LLM) in the emergency handling of various types of gas safety events and the popularization of safety knowledge. In this paper, we construct a scheme for generating gas safety knowledge graph and retrieval-augmented generation based on big language model. Specifically, firstly, a knowledge graph is constructed by extracting entities from the dataset using LLM and prompt word engineering. Then, evaluation metrics and measurement methods are designed for this scheme. Finally, the feasibility of the proposed method is verified by experiments.

articleTitle: The Hyers-Ulam Stability for High-Order Linear Differential Equations with Constant Coefficients
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: There are many problems in engineering can be reflected by linear ordinary differential equation with constant coefficients. If a differential equation has the Hyers-Ulam stability, then it can guarantee that an approximate solution is close to an accurate solution. So it is important to consider the the Hyers-Ulam stability of differential equations in numerical solution of differential equations. Up to now, the discussion of the Hyers-Ulam stability for high-order differential equations is very few. This paper concerns with the Hyers-Ulam stability of high-order linear differential equations with constant coefficients. We get a necessary and sufficient condition such that a class of differential inequalities hold. Using this necessary and sufficient condition, the formula of general solution and roots of the characteristic equation for linear ordinary differential equation with constant coefficients, we discuss the Hyers-Ulam stability of high-order linear differential equations with constant coefficients. The conclusions show that some third-order and nth-order linear differential equations with constant coefficients have the Hyers-Ulam stability.

articleTitle: The A TG Interference Source Localization based on Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: The extensive deployment of Air-to-Ground (ATG) system significantly exacerbates interference issues with terrestrial 5G NR system, thereby elevating the importance of localization interference originating from A TG system. While existing method can locate interference sources to a certain extent, they predominantly require additional hardware installations or infrastructure modifications, escalating both costs and complexity. Addressing this challenge, this research introduces an innovative framework that utilizes Signal-to-Interference-plus-Noise Ratio (SINR) measurements collected from operational networks. These SINR values are geographically encoded, and ResN et is used to extract features from these encoded maps and locate the interference sources. Furthermore, the study examines the impact of varying the number of sensing base stations on the accuracy of interference source localization. Experimental results demonstrate that this approach substantially enhances the accuracy and reliability of interference source localization, offering significant practical benefits for intelligent interference management and 5G network optimization.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of a Propagation Counteraction Model in Social Media Information
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In the dissemination of social media information, it is common that there are two opposing viewpoints on the same topic, which we call social media information propagation counteraction. In this paper, based on the classical infectious disease model SIR, we propose a Propagation Counteraction Model SInIR in Social Media Information, and use Python to write programs to simulate the implementation of the model in a Facebook dataset, which provides a new perspective for analyzing the propagation of positive and counteractant information.

articleTitle: KDA-UNet: A Deep Learning Framework for Segmentation in Medical Imaging
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Medical imaging plays a crucial role in the diagnosis, treatment, and assessment of diseases. Accurate segmentation of bones and muscles in medical images is of significant practical importance for assisting physicians in diagnosis. However, the low contrast between bones and muscles in medical images, coupled with substantial variations in the edges and shapes of different bones, presents considerable challenges. To address these issues, this paper proposes a segmentation network based on the U-Net architecture, incorporating KAN convolution and a dual attention mechanism, referred to as KDA-UNet. The KAN convolution effectively captures local spatial information in images, compensating for the limitations of standard convolutional layers in modeling spatial features. The dual attention mechanism helps the network focus on the most critical regions and channels within the image, significantly enhancing the feature extraction performance and capability of the segmentation network.

articleTitle: ViScheduler: Visualized Seed Scheduling Based on Runtime Features
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Fuzzing is a popular technique for software vulnerability detection. Modern fuzzing uses feedback from the program under test (PUT) to prioritize test cases, but existing seed scheduling methods do not provide an interface for expert intervention. We propose a method to visualize seed features using neural networks trained with runtime seed features. This allows human experts to visualize fuzzing progress and intervene in seed scheduling. Current challenges include building labeled machine learning datasets using runtime features and visualizing high-dimensional seed embeddings. We address these issues by proposing a Transformer neural network trained using an approximation task (bug test case embedding extraction). The feature embeddings are then visualized in 3D space using dimensionality reduction methods. We also introduce four seed scheduling strategies based on seed embeddings to facilitate human intervention. This approach bridges the gap between seed scheduling and human expertise and experimental results show that it can lead to more effective fuzzing.

articleTitle: A Novel Channel Estimation Method for RIS Assisted Wireless Communication Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Channel estimation (CE) can be challenging in reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-assisted wireless communication systems. On the one hand, the dimensionality of the cascaded base station-RIS-user equipment (BS-RIS-UE) channel is exceedingly large. On the other hand, the currently available RIS hardware cannot arbitrarily switch between the active (reflection with configurable phase) and deactivate (absorption) modes, thereby resulting in a perpetual coupling between the BS-RIS-UE channel and BS-UE channel. To address the challenges above, we introduce a novel CE method that leverages the spatial modulation capabilities of RIS. The proposed CE strategy is bifurcated into two distinct phases: the BS-UE CE and the RIS-UE CE. In the BS-UE CE phase, the RIS is strategically configured to steer the incoming signals from the UEs away from the BS. This maneuver significantly suppresses the signal through the cascaded BS-RIS-UE channel, allowing it to be effectively disregarded. Consequently, this facilitates a separate BS-UE CE process using the conventional least squares (LS) algorithm. Armed with the estimated BS-UE channels, the RIS-UE channels can then be readily estimated. Simulation results show that, compared to the existing CE schemes, the proposed CE method can improve the estimation accuracy and reduce the computational complexity.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of the Performance of Recent Optimization Algorithms in Solving Engineering Problems
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Intelligent optimization algorithms are currently the mainstream methods for solving engineering design problems. This paper conducts a comprehensive analysis of the performance of five recent intelligent optimization algorithms in solving eight engineering design problems. The simulation results, along with the Wilcoxon Signed-Rank Test (WSRT), Friedman Test (FT), and the results of the boxplot, indicate that the APO algorithm has significant advantages in solving this types of problems.

articleTitle: Loss-Convergence- Driven Federated Learning with Energy Optimization: A Stackelberg Game Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In Federated Learning (FL), the accuracy of each client model directly impacts the performance of the aggregated global model. Increasing the number of local training rounds can improve the accuracy of the aggregated model, thereby reducing the number of global training rounds and minimizing communication overhead. However, existing methods need help in incentivizing clients for training, particularly in evaluating their contributions. To address these issues, the paper introduces a Stackelberg game-based incentive mechanism that focuses on loss convergence and power optimization. By leveraging the Monte Carlo algorithm to solve the game equilibrium, we optimize the training strategy to accelerate the FL process and reduce energy consumption effectively. Experimental results demonstrate that, while maintaining the same level of global model accuracy, our approach reduces energy consumption by up to 33% and shortens the number of global iterations by 27 %.

articleTitle: A Novel Decentralized Federated Split Learning Framework in 6G Edge Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Federated learning (FL) and split learning (SL) are two popular distributed machine learning approaches. As a paradigm of FL, decentralized federated learning (DFL) architecture enables edge devices to collaboratively train a shared machine learning model without a central parameter server. Meanwile, SL can reduce computing load of edge devices by model splitting and assignment. In this paper, we propose a distributed federated split learning (DFSL) framework. In terms of framework design, DFSL combines the advantages of SL and DFL, enabling resource-constrained edge devices to participate in the training of complex models while reducing the risks of network bottlenecks and single points of failure during training. In terms of model training, DFSL enhances the model testing accuracy compared to DFL and significantly reduces the training time compared to SL. We conduct detailed performance analysis of the proposed DFSL algorithm, demonstrating its efficiency and convergence in training. Numerical results validate the superiority of DFSL over DFL and SL in model training.

articleTitle: Cloud Auditing with Efficiently Updatable Designated Verifier
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Cloud auditing provides a convenient way for users to remotely check the integrity of data stored in the cloud. Public cloud auditing allows any cloud user to perform verification. However, in most real cases, the data owner expects its trusted designated verifier to perform the auditing task. Meanwhile, there are many cases that require updating the verifier, such as contract expiration and auditing costs etc. In traditional auditing scenarios, the CSP recalculates the tags to update the verifier. In order to improve the efficiency, we propose a cloud auditing scheme that can efficiently update the designated verifier based on the trapped collision property of the chameleon hash functions, and illustrate the security and feasibility of the scheme through a proof of security reduction.

articleTitle: A Packet Detection Method with Wide CFO Range Coverage for Bluetooth Low Energy 1M PHY Signal
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
