articleTitle: Predictive Performance of Kriging and the Long Short-Term Memory for Spatio-Temporal Data
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Spatio-temporal data arise in many studies across agriculture, environmental, and climate sciences, where forecasting and prediction are often key objectives. The best linear unbiased prediction method, Kriging, is widely used in these fields. However, the large covariance matrix involved in Kriging poses significant computational challenges. Moreover, Kriging of-ten depends on model assumptions such as stationarity. Machine learning methods offer an alternative approach. In this work, we compare the predictive performance of a particular deep learning model-the Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network-with Kriging. Using two environmental datasets, we demonstrate that the LSTM has the potential to outperform Kriging, likely due to the fewer assumptions required by the LSTM model

articleTitle: Joint Latency-Energy Cost Optimization for Asynchronous UAV-Assisted Mobile Edge Computing in Cognitive Emergency Network
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In the emergency scenario, we propose cognitive based and unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) assisted mobile edge computing (MEC) network (cognitive UAVMN) to solve the problem of insufficient spectral and computing resources. In the cognitive UAVMN, the effect of sensing duration is considered to balance the tradeoff between sensing, transmitting and computing for cognitive users and MEC servers. Based on this, an optimization problem is formulated to minimize the total system cost by jointly optimizing the position of UAV, transmitting power of ground users, spectrum sensing duration, computing frequency of ground device and UAV and offloading probability. We also analyze effect of spectrum sensing performance to the system cost in task transmitting and computing. The simulation results indicate that the proposed cognitive UAVMN decreases system cost with limited resource when compared to other schemes.

articleTitle: Stacked HRDGL: A Fast Hybrid Model for Real-Time Network Intrusion Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: The increasing sophistication of network attacks, such as Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) and darknet traffic anomalies, necessitates more efficient real-time network intrusion detection systems (NIDS). XGBoost has become a popular baseline for intrusion detection due to its high accuracy, but its latency often falls short of real-time requirements. In this work, we introduce Stacked HRDGL, a novel dynamic hybrid ensemble model that optimizes both detection accuracy and latency by leveraging a diverse set of base learners and an innovative stacking mechanism. The model combines Logistic Regression, Naive Bayes, Decision Tree, and Random Forest, selected for their complementary strengths in handling linearity, probabilistic inference, and decision boundaries, which collectively improve classification robustness. The novelty of Stacked HRDGL lies in its optimized stacking structure, which minimizes inter-model redundancy and enhances meta-learner decision-making, resulting in superior detection speed without compromising accuracy. Evaluated on the CICIDS2017 and CICDarknet2020 datasets for DDoS and darknet anomaly detection, Stacked HRDGL achieves competitive accuracy (99.98% on CICIDS2017 and 94.03% on CICDarknet2020), while significantly reducing latency by up to 15x compared to XGBoost, as measured on a standard multicore system. Although tested primarily on these two datasets, Stacked HRDGL's flexible architecture suggests scalability across diverse network traffic types and evolving threats. The model's low resource footprint and efficient execution make it particularly suited for real-time deployment in high-traffic environments. This paper contributes a practical, scalable solution to the NIDS field, bridging the gap between accuracy and real-time performance with an innovative ensemble approach.

articleTitle: SoftINA: A Softwarized In-Network Aggregator for Distributed Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Given that in-network aggregation (INA) has become a promising and generic performance acceleration solution for various distributed applications, in this paper, we explore the possibility of implementing aggregators in software with a case study. We not only identify the necessity and advantages of providing software-based INA for distributed applications but we also prototype SoftINA, an efficient softwarized in-network aggregator built upon the open-source virtual switch platform of BESS, together with a flexible packet format design. Testbed-based evaluations show the high efficiency of SoftINA-It achieves an aggregation throughput of about 3.4 ~ 16.3 Gbps for several flat-vector streams by only using a single CPU core.

articleTitle: Detecting Deletions and Insertions for Binary Segmented Channels
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: An insdel refers to an insertion or a deletion. In this paper, we consider the problem of constructing error-detecting codes for segmented single-insertion/-insdel channel, where the channel's input bit stream is partitioned into segments of length <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex>. The value of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex> is known to the receiver but the segment boundaries of the receiving string are not. We propose a structure where prefixes and suffixes are the sole additions. In this way, we are able to construct new codes that can detect segmented single-insertion/-insdel errors with redundancy 4 bits and 8 bits per segment, respectively. Moreover, our codes have linear-time encoding/detecting algorithms.

articleTitle: Intelligent Early Warning and Monitoring Decision Model for Abnormal Vibration States of Motors and an Empirical Study
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In chemical reactors, motor failures like belt breakage can disrupt production. Traditional methods for detecting motor abnormalities, such as manual inspections and monitoring control room currents, lack effectiveness. This study introduces a T2-LSTM algorithm combined with motor vibration sensors to predict motor quality and establish an early warning system. Statistical Process Control (SPC) techniques determine warning thresholds, while the ISO 10816-1 standard categorizes motor states as Good, Satisfactory, Unsatisfactory, or Unacceptable. Tested with 150 data points in a real-world scenario, the system achieved a 98% prediction accuracy (147/150), with 146 predictions within the normal range and only one unsatisfactory point among the four that exceeded the threshold.

articleTitle: Adaptive Gateway Traffic Scheduling Algorithm Based on Multidimensional Information
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In this paper, an adaptive gateway traffic scheduling algorithm based on multi-dimensional information is proposed to solve the load balancing problem in high concurrency scenarios. The algorithm considers the three dimensions of server performance, network status and traffic prediction, and dynamically adjusts the performance load weight, service access weight and traffic prediction weight to realize more intelligent traffic scheduling. By monitoring load pressure index, network pressure index and traffic prediction difference index in real time, the algorithm can flexibly deal with different network environments and traffic fluctuations. Experimental results show that compared with traditional load balancing algorithms, the proposed algorithm has a remarkable performance improvement in system throughput and response time. Finally, this paper looks forward to future research directions in introducing more dimensional information, optimizing traffic prediction models, extending to distributed environments, and improving real-time algorithms.

articleTitle: Resource Allocation Strategy Based on the BCPF Algorithm for Visible Light Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: A novel bandwidth and channel priority fairness algorithm (BCPF) is proposed for heterogeneous networks combining WiFi and Visible Light Communication (VLC) technologies. Indoor network modeling and simulation experiments verify the algorithm's effectiveness in improving overall system performance. The results demonstrate significant improvements in system throughput, reduced latency, and enhanced user fairness, indicating the new algorithm's potential to optimize hybrid WiFi-VLC networks.

articleTitle: Keyword-Enhanced Semantic Retrieval and Multi-Dimensional Relevance Ranking in RAG
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In the task of generating medical hot topics, efficiently and accurately retrieving relevant information based on hot keywords and generating credible topics is a challenging problem. Addressing the limitations of existing retrieval and ranking methods in terms of accuracy and relevance, this paper proposes a RAG-based keyword-enhanced semantic retrieval and multi-dimensional relevance ranking approach. First, we construct keyword vectors using the BGE model and perform fast similarity searches to achieve preliminary retrieval. Then, we optimize the relevance of the retrieval results by setting a similarity threshold and applying a cluster and de-duplication strategy. Building on this, multi-dimensional similarity measurement is introduced, combining a cross-encoder model and feature extraction to implement reordering, further improving the accuracy of retrieval results. Experimental results show that this method significantly enhances RAG's performance in generating hot topics from medical news and information, providing an effective solution for complex information retrieval tasks.

articleTitle: Modulation Recognition of OTFS Signal for UAV Communication System
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: With the continuous expansion of drone application scenarios, the communication requirements and modes of drones have become more diversified and complex. However, high-speed information transmission has always been a focus of attention. To provide a guarantee for highly reliable communication of drones, Orthogonal Time Frequency Space (OTFS) technology overcomes the influence of multipath and Doppler effects in traditional communication systems in high-speed moving environments. At the same time, in the multipath channel of unmanned aerial vehicle communication systems, traditional methods for identifying OTFS signal subcarrier modulation methods exist some problems such as low recognition accuracy and incomplete identification methods. Therefore, deep learning can be used to study the recognition of OTFS signal subcarrier modulation methods. The article uses Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), Long Short Term Memory (LSTM) Neural Network and LCDNN for modulation recognition. Meanwhile, Residual Network (Res Net) is used as the base model. The result of simulation experiment shows that the LCDNN has higher recognition accuracy, short training time for model and good network performance.

articleTitle: An Interference Detection Method Based on CNN and CNR for GNSS
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) signals are inherently weak and highly susceptible to jamming. Traditional signal analysis-based detection methods struggle with accurate identification in scenarios involving multipath propagation, weak interference, or complex interference types, leading in high missed detection rate (MDR). To solve these issues, a convolutional neural network (CNN) based interference detector by using carrier-to-noise density ratio (CNR) parameters from large-scale observation station is proposed in this paper. By learning the change principle in CNR features at lots of receiving stations under interference, a deep learning model is designed to effectively detect interference. In order to automatically extract the feature behind CNR data well, a CNN consisting of two convolutional layers, two max-pooling layers, and a fully connected dense block is built and trained. After preprocessing of normalization and dimensional transformation, the CNR observation data are fed into CNN to produce detection results. Simulation results demonstrate that a significant improvement in detection capabilities can be provided by the proposed method under both weak and complex interferences. Across the mixed dataset including 4 types of suppression jamming and 3 JSR values, an detection accuracy of 98.49% can be achieved by the CNN scheme, while only 95.12% is got by the baseline method, i.e RFA.

articleTitle: Blockchain-Based Intelligent E-Commerce Platform for Enhancing Customer Experience in Telecom Operators
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In the rapidly evolving landscape of e-commerce, the integration of blockchain technology and artificial intelligence (AI) presents unprecedented opportunities for enhancing customer experience, particularly within the telecommunications sector. This paper proposes a secure private blockchain-based intelligent e-commerce platform designed to streamline commercial and trade circulation while fostering trust and security. By leveraging the immutable nature of blockchain and implementing end-to-end encryption (E2EE), the platform ensures secure transactions and improves data privacy, addressing common pain points in digital commerce. Furthermore, the incorporation of large language models (LLMs) enhance user experience through personalized recommendation and efficient customer service. The synergy between blockchain and AI not only optimizes operational efficiency but also cultivates a more engaging and satisfying customer journey. Through empirical analysis and case studies, our proposed approach highlights its advantages over traditional platform in the perspective of customer experience.

articleTitle: R-LSTM Algorithm for Imputation of Air Quality Data Based on Sample Screening
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In the context of increasing societal concern for the natural environment, urban air quality monitoring has become a key component of environmental management. However, due to technical failures of monitoring equipment and data transmission problems, the lack of air quality data often affects the analysis and progress of downstream tasks. To solve this problem, this paper proposes an air quality data interpolation algorithm based on the Relevance Long Short Term Memory Network (R-LSTM). The algorithm significantly improves the accuracy of missing data interpolation by exploiting the intrinsic correlation between air quality indicators and combining it with a sample screening mechanism. In the experimental part, this paper uses air quality time series data from Shenyang City, Liaoning Province for testing. Under the set condition of 15 % random missing rate, this paper compares the performance of R-LSTM with other benchmark models using the mean absolute error (MAE) and mean relative error (MRE) as evaluation indices. The experimen-tal results show that R-LSTM has better results in interpolating the missing data of air quality.

articleTitle: Improving Urban Landscape Semantic Segmentation Using CBAM in DeepLabV3
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Semantic segmentation technology for urban landscapes plays an important role in various fields, such as improving autonomous driving, optimizing traffic control, and enhancing environmental monitoring. However, the complexity and variability of urban landscapes reduce segmentation accuracy. To overcome these challenges, this study proposes an improved DeepLabV3 model. Firstly, ResNet50 and a smaller stride are selected as the feature extraction backbone network, which improves the quality of feature extraction and segmentation accuracy while ensuring computational efficiency. Secondly, a Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM) is introduced after the feature extraction network to enhance the model's focus on important features in both channel and spatial dimensions. Finally, by increasing the dilation rate of the Atrous Spatial Pyramid Pooling (ASPP) module, the model not only captures a broader range of contextual information but also compensates for potentially overlooked detailed features during the feature extraction process. We conducted experimental verification on the CityScapes and GTA5 urban landscape datasets. Experimental results demonstrate that our method has improved the mIOU on the CityScapes test set from 81.3% to 82.8%, and achieved an mIOU of 81.6% on the GTA5 validation set. From the segmentation results, our model pays more attention to important features, and the precision has been enhanced in the segmentation of small objects. This demonstrates the robustness and adaptability of this method in complex urban streetscape segmentation tasks. This study not only enhances the performance of semantic segmentation technology but also provides new possibilities for its application in a broader range of urban scenarios in the future.

articleTitle: An Efficient Attention Mechanism Based Neural Network for CSI Feedback in Massive MIMO System
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In Frequency Division Duplex (FDD) systems, the quality and efficiency of Channel State Information (CSI) feedback enhancement are challenged by the large size of the CSI matrix in massive Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (MIMO) systems. A variety of machine learning techniques have been proposed to improve the accuracy of CSI feedback. However, most of these works achieved accuracy depending on the high computational complexity. To improve this situation, an efficient attention mechanism based neural network (EANet) for CSI feed-back is proposed in this paper. EANet reduces the computational complexity by simplifying the encoder and decoder network structure in the meantime it maintains the capabilities of feature extraction. Furthermore, a lightweight Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) module is integrated to improve the accuracy of CSI feedback by enhancing the ability to capture the channel features. Finally, experimental results demonstrate that EANet achieves higher feedback accuracy with a low computational complexity.

articleTitle: Technical Research on Missing Value Imputation for Atmospheric Quality Data Based on Improved GAIN
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: With the rapid development of China's economy, environmental issues have also become a key focus of attention. Environmental prediction can promptly detect potential pollution hazards and nip them in the bud. However, due to the interference of uncontrollable factors during the collection and storage of environmental data, data loss occurs. Addressing the issue of missing environmental data, this article makes various improvements to the existing GAIN filling network model. Finally, an improved GAIN network model is adopted, which uses dual generators to iteratively capture features and adds an attention module to obtain potential features. Compared with traditional filling models, the improved GAIN network model exhibits better performance in filling missing environmental data.

articleTitle: STSE-xLSTM: A Deep Learning Framework for Automated Seizure Detection in Long Video Sequences Using Spatio-Temporal and Attention Mechanisms
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: A detailed analysis of seizure semiology, the symptoms and signs that occur during a seizure, is crucial for the management of epilepsy patients. The inter-rater reliability of qualitative visual analysis is often low, highlighting the need for automatic and quantitative analysis of video-recorded seizures for objective assessment. To enhance evaluation accuracy and consistency, computer-aided video analysis of seizures has emerged as a natural direction of development. In the field of medical applications, deep learning and computer vision methods have driven significant advancements. However, analyzing video data presents challenges due to high dimensionality, variations in lighting, posture, and video quality. Additionally, the duration of seizures can range from seconds to minutes. To effectively extract features from seizures, we propose a novel deep learning model, STSE-xLSTM, designed to learn deep representations of arbitrarily long seizure videos. This model integrates a Spatio-Temporal Convolutional Network (STCNN) for feature extraction, a Squeeze-and-Excitation (SE) attention mechanism to enhance relevant features, and an extended Long Short-Term Memory network (xLSTM) to process long video sequences. The SE mechanism adaptively recalibrates channel weights, improving recognition of minority classes and reducing information redundancy. The xLSTM introduces scalar and matrix memory units, optimizing memory capacity and multi-scale feature extraction, thereby enhancing detection accuracy. When evaluated on the GESTURES dataset, our model outperformed state-of-the-art epilepsy detection methods in classification performance. Key contributions include the integration of STCNN, SE attention mechanism, and xLSTM to address data imbalance issues and improve the handling of complex sequential data in epilepsy detection.

articleTitle: Spatial Temporal Transpose Convolutional Networks for Action Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In recent years, the use of skeleton data for human action recognition has received increasing attention in fields such as intelligent monitoring, human-object interaction, and video retrieval. Among them, Modeling Human Skeleton as Spatial-Temporal Graph Convolutional Network (ST-GCN) has made significant progress. However, methods based on Graph Convolution (GCN) generally face two issues: on one hand, the receptive fields of the spatial and temporal graphs are not flexible enough, limiting their feature representation capabilities. On the other hand, the model is overly parameterized, leading to high computational costs. In this paper, we first propose a spatial-temporal transpose convolution module to overcome the inflexibility of the spatial-temporal graph receptive field. Secondly, we introduce 1 *1 convolutions and depth-wise separable convolution layers into the network model, effectively reducing the computational complexity of the model. On the two subsets of the large-scale skeleton action recognition dataset NTU RGB-D, experimental results show that the proposed method achieved Top1 accuracy metrics of 84.6% and 92.5% respectively, while the model size was reduced by 13.48 times compared to the classic ST-GCN method, and the computational complexity was reduced by approximately 17.18 times.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-Based Receiver for 4096-QAM Signal in IEEE 802.11be Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: As one of the latest wireless communication standard released by the IEEE 802.11be task group (TG), IEEE 802.11be firstly defines 4096 quadrature amplitude modulation (QAM) scheme which is helpful to high throughput and low latency. However, it brings new challenges in signal recovering, due to extremely high requirements on the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR). This paper proposes a deep learning-based receiver for 4096-QAM single-input single-output transmission in the IEEE 802.11be system. Simulation results show that the proposed receiver can achieve better detection performance than conventional methods and the bit error rate (BER) drops to 10–<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sup> when signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) is 40dB.

articleTitle: Microwave Nonlinear Mixing Properties of Graphene
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In this paper, a graphene harmonic mixer with low conversion loss and high isolation is proposed, which adopts an inductive capacitive resonator and a microstrip reflection stub. Due to the nonlinear properties of graphene, it is suitable for the development of a hybrid material. By simplifying the approximate conductivity of single-layer graphene and using the nonlinear model of graphene, the graphene SDD model was established. Compared with other nonlinear microwave mixing devices and similar graphene mixers, the CL of this mixer is significantly reduced, and the isolation between ports is also improved. When the local oscillator power is 15–17 dBm, the frequency is within 1.01-1.1GHz, the RF is −10dBm, and the frequency is within 2.31-2.41GHz, the output power of the mixer 400MHz is −28dBm, the minimum conversion loss CL is 17.7dB, and the isolation between the local oscillator end and the IF end is 28dB. near 2.3GHz RF frequency, the RF end The isolation degree of RF end and IF end is 32dB.

articleTitle: Energy Spreading Transform Based Iterative Equalization for Faster-Than-Nyquist Signaling
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Faster-Than-Nyquist signling,as a non-orthogonal signaling format,can effectively enhances the spectral efficiency of communication systems. However, it introduces significant Inter-Symbol Interference (ISI). ISI can lead to inferior receiver performance in transmission systems. Therefore,requires some competent equalization schemes as a key technology to overcome the key impediment to its use in future mobile communications.This paper aims to develop a high-performance Faster-Than-Nyquist(FTN) signaling system by utilizing an Iterative Decision Feedback Equalizer, which mitigates the impact of local errors through Energy Spreading Transform (EST). EST can extend the energy of an error symbol to the entire transmission frame, thereby minimizing their influence on surrounding symbols and improving overall system performance. In addition, we ensured that the SINR output at each iteration reaches its maximum during the iterative process.Simulation results demonstrate that this algorithm can have better ISI resistance while keeping the complexity low, and its performance improves with increasing iterations.

articleTitle: Leveraging CNN for Automated Lesion Detection in Stroke MRI Scans
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In recent years, more and more people have used neural network training to predict stroke lesions. In the field of images, the performance has been improved by using large models for training. Manual identification of stroke lesions may lead to inaccurate prediction and high error rate. By constructing basic CNN model, it can greatly help doctors to predict lesions. The aim of this study is to explore the influence of CNN model performance on focal image recognition.

articleTitle: Efficient FPGA Implementation of Phase Offset Estimation and Compensation for 5G Based LEO Satellite Communication System
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: The integration of 5G technology with Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite communication systems is crucial for the future of global wireless networks, offering extensive coverage and high data rates. In such systems, signals are susceptible to phase offsets due to factors like Doppler frequency shifts and phase noise, which necessitate the development of effective estimation and compensation algorithms. This paper presents an efficient FPGA-based phase offset estimation and compensation scheme for 5G LEO satellite communication systems. To address the challenges of Doppler frequency and phase noise in high-frequency band communications, a novel reference signal layout is devised, and circuit modules are realized using Verilog Hardware Description Language (HDL). The proposed scheme proficiently estimates and compensates for phase offsets, thereby enhancing system performance.

articleTitle: Path Planning and Oscillation Management in Unknown Environments Using an Improved D* Lite Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: This paper addresses the challenge of robotic pathfinding in scenarios characterized by mobility constraints and dynamic environments prone to causing oscillations, where the robot moves back and forth repeatedly. To mitigate this issue and enhance pathfinding efficiency, we introduce an innovative enhancement to the D* Lite algorithm. Our approach incor-porates a well-designed local oscillation detection mechanism that assesses the robot's state to promptly identify instances of oscillation and selects an optimal movement strategy accordingly. Furthermore, a local oscillation escape strategy tailored to swiftly extricate the robot from these oscillating patterns was devised, thereby minimizing the overall pathfinding time. Comparative experiments were conducted on 10*10 and 20*20 maps with varying environments and local oscillations. These experiments evaluated the algorithm's oscillation detection capability and path length. The results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm offers superior oscillation detection, reduced oscillation time, and shorter path lengths compared to the traditional D* Lite algorithm.

articleTitle: Improved Genetic Algorithm Based Task Allocation for AGV Warehousing and Logistics with Adjustable Load
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: With the rapid development of the e-commerce economy, the demand for enhanced logistics speed has become increasingly urgent. Among various logistics processes, the transition from factory to delivery is particularly critical. Consequently, the order picking system based on multi-load automatic guided vehicles (AGVs) has drawn significant attention. Compared with single-load AGV systems, scheduling a multi-load AGV system presents a more complex challenge. Addressing the optimization of automatic picking by multi-load AGVs to minimize costs and maximize efficiency is an urgent issue. In response, we propose a task scheduling model for a multi-load AGV system. Each AGV is capable of carrying multiple picking orders, with the sequence of orders for each AGV determined by minimizing the driving path, reducing the number of AGVs, and ensuring the timely submission of ordered goods. Simultaneously, an improved multi-link genetic algorithm is proposed, which employs a novel labeling method to address the issues of genetic algorithm encoding and decoding for multi-load AGVs. We compared the performance of the algorithm across different parameters and validated its efficacy in real-world scenarios. The results demonstrate that multi-load AGVs can complete designated order picking tasks more quickly and efficiently within the specified time constraints, using fewer driving paths and AGVs. Additionally, in scenarios involving a large number of AGVs and tasks, the algorithm continued to effectively optimize task submission.

articleTitle: Multi-UE Cooperative Time Synchronization Based on Proximity Services
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: With the advancement of mobile communication and industrial internet technologies, the demand for time syn-chronization in various scenarios has significantly increased. This paper investigates a multi-UE cooperative time synchronization scheme based on Proximity Services (ProSe). Leveraging ProSe's off-network operation and direct communication capabilities, the proposed method utilizes the Pairwise Broadcast Synchronization (PBS) protocol for time information transmission. This approach aims to achieve reliable time synchronization in emergency rescue scenarios, particularly where infrastructure may be compro-mised. The simulation results demonstrate that the proposed scheme improves synchronization accuracy and convergence speed compared to existing methods. Additionally, the incorpo-ration of Kalman filtering enhances the estimation precision. The findings indicate that this approach holds significant potential for applications in public safety, emergency rescue, and industrial automation, paving the way for more reliable and efficient time synchronization in critical scenarios.

articleTitle: Analyzing Effects of Time Series Data Characteristics on LSTM Performance
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: The use of deep learning techniques for time series forecasting has increased in recent years. Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) is a deep learning technique that has been shown to be effective for time series forecasting. This research proposes a methodology to study the relationship between LSTM performance and time series data characteristics, including trend, seasonality, skewness, kurtosis, chaotic behavior, and coefficient of variation. The methodology was applied to 48 stock price datasets. Three techniques, namely multiple linear regression, feature importance, and SHAP value, were used to compare LSTM performance across different data characteristics. The results show that coefficient of variation and chaotic behavior are the two most crucial characteristics affecting LSTM performance.

articleTitle: Remote Sensing Image Compression Using ResNet and SEBlock
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: This paper presents a remote sensing image compression method based on ResNet and the Squeeze-and-Excitation Block (SEBlock) to optimize bandwidth usage during satellite-to-ground transmission. By employing the ResNet model in the encoder and incorporating SEBlock to enhance feature representation, our model significantly reduces data size while preserving image quality. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves an excellent trade-off between compression efficiency and image quality, with PSNR reaching 38.02 dB and SSIM reaching 0.9851. We tested scenarios with 2 to 5 ResNet layers, showing consistent performance improvements, with fewer layers resulting in higher PSNR and SSIM values. This approach offers a novel solution for efficient transmission of remote sensing imagery, suitable for high-resolution and bandwidth-limited satellite communications.

articleTitle: Implementation of a Hip Fracture Classification Network Based on CT Tomography Scans
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Hip fractures is the most common hip clinical trauma. The majority of elderly patients experience a decrease in bone density due to osteoporosis, making them highly prone to various types of hip fractures. In this context, accurate diagnosis and classification of hip fractures are crucial for guiding clinical decision-making and ensuring the best possible patient outcomes. The BV C- N et proposed in this study is a two-stage model for the identification of hip fracture types, which is based on the integration of the V-Net and ConvNeXt architectures. First, deep learning segmentation model is trained to generate candidate fracture regions, and then, a deep learning classification model is trained in the second stage to classify the segmented local fracture regions according to the candidate fracture regions generated in the first stage to ascertain the type of fracture. The results show that the two-stage deep learning model proposed in this study enhances the accuracy of hip fracture type recognition and reduces the time required for manual classification, which can better assist doctors in fracture region recognition.

articleTitle: Design of Multipath Evacuation Method Based on Network Flow Model and Ripple Spreading Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: To solve the multipath planning with capacity-constrained problems (MPCCP), this paper proposes a solution based on the network flow model, utilizing the network flow-ripple spreading algorithm (NFRSA). Considering the dynamic nature of evacuated pedestrian flow during evacuation,-we have improved the ripple spreading algorithm by integrating it with the network flow model. The condition to generate a new ripple at the origin node is based on whether there are remaining pedestrians. The number of pedestrians assigned to the ripple is constrained by the link capacity transit operator. Then the arrival time of each pedestrian at nodes and the link capacity table for each time window are updated. NFRSA continues until there are no more pedestrians at the origin nodes. Finally, through experiments, we validated that NFRSA improves computational efficiency and ensures consistency of solutions compared to other algorithms. This establishes NFRSA as an effective solution for pedestrian evacuation in large-scale road networks.

articleTitle: Covert Cooperative Jamming Aided Secure Wireless Communication with Channel Inversion Power Control
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In this work, we explore the secure wireless communication with a covert cooperative jammer (CCJ) under the supervision of an intelligent eavesdropper. At first time, we construct the framework of the covert jamming hidden by the channel uncertainty brought by the channel inversion power control (CIPC) technology at the transmitter. Then, we characterize the jamming covertness and communication security by the detection error probability and the secrecy throughput (ST), respectively. At last, we optimize the CIPC constant and the jamming transmit power to maximize ST under the constraint of jamming covertness. Due to the additional channel uncertainty caused by CIPC, the numerical results show that the proposed CIPC scheme can achieve larger ST, compared with the conventional scheme with the constant transmit power (CTP).

articleTitle: Enhancing End-to-End Speech Emotion Recognition Using Dual-Stream with Multi-Task Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Since speech emotion is variable and continuous, and human-computer interaction scenarios such as voice assistants are increasingly appearing in life with the development of technology, it is both necessary and challenging to allow machines to accurately recognise emotion in speech. In this paper, we propose a new end-to-end speech emotion recognition (SER) model, using dual-stream and multitask learning. The dual-stream model is constructed based on the upper stream, used for learning spec features, and the lower stream, built through a pretrained Wav2Vec 2.0 block. In addition, We introduce two tasks, gender classification and the Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR), to form a multitask learning mechanism together with the main task of SER. Specifically, we pass the input audio to a pretrained model and a feature extractor so that the pretrained model learns potential hidden features in speech directly, while the feature extractor extracts speech as specific features and passes them to the subsequent model. On the IEMOCAP dataset, our model has UA of 79.6% and WA of 82.6%. Comparing with the latest end-to-end model, our model improves 2.5% on UA and 2.3% on WA. Compared with other models, our model outperforms existing methods by 0.5% UA and 1% WA.

articleTitle: An Efficient Verifiable Aggregation Scheme with Privacy-Enhanced in Federated Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Federated learning (FL) allows multiple clients to train a global model without sharing raw data. However, local gradient vectors are vulnerable to inference attacks, necessitating secure aggregation protocols to prevent the server from accessing information beyond aggregated results. A malicious server may fabricate results for personal gain, leading to inaccurate global models that negatively impact training. Therefore, verifying aggregation results is crucial for model reliability. Existing verifiable methods often use linear homomorphic hash (LHH) directly on gradient vectors, which can cause information leakage and inadequately address security concerns. To address this, we propose an efficient verifiable secure aggregation scheme. By combining a constant-length linear homomorphic hash with a commitment function and masking gradient vectors before hashing, our approach effectively prevents inference attacks, enhancing privacy. This scheme ensures the correctness of aggregation results while improving computation and communication efficiency. Experimental results demonstrate that our scheme outperforms state-of-the-art methods in accuracy, computation efficiency, and communication efficiency.

articleTitle: Enhanced Tuplet and Anchor Clustering For Distance-Based Recognition of Unknown Modulation Type Signals
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: With the rapid development of communication technology, the communication environment has become increasingly complex, and various modulation schemes are continuously emerging. In certain communication application scenarios, the receiver may encounter signals employing unknown modulation schemes. Therefore, effectively identifying these unknown modulation types has become a critical research topic in the field of modulation recognition. Currently, methods typically involve training models using Cross Entropy Loss and then distinguishing between known and unknown classes by calculating distances in the logical space. However, this approach does not ensure effective clustering in the logical space. To address this issue, this paper proposes an Enhanced Tuplet and Anchor Clustering (ETAC) method. This novel distance-based approach enables known classes to form tighter clusters around their respective class centers during the training process. Our experiments demonstrate that the ETAC method achieves superior AUROC performance in identifying unknown modulation types under various modulation schemes, signal oversampling factors, and different signal-to-noise ratio (dB) conditions compared to the traditional Cross Entropy Loss. Under high-quality signal conditions, our method achieves an AUROC above 0.960. Even with average signal quality, it maintains an AUROC around 0.9, demonstrating high effectiveness.

articleTitle: DNS Service Optimization Through In-Network Caching on Programmable Switches
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: The Domain Name System (DNS) plays a crucial role in contemporary internet infrastructure. Despite the geographical distance of public DNS servers posing a challenge in minimizing domain name resolution latency, there is an increasing reliance on these servers for resolving domain names. One effective approach to mitigate this challenge involves caching DNS query results at network nodes. The storage of cached results commonly employs hash tables due to the variable lengths of domain names. However, within network nodes, hash tables encounter limitations in capacity and susceptibility to hash collisions, potentially leading to inaccuracies in cached results. Current conventional caching strategies have not produced satisfactory storage outcomes. This research introduces a hash-based DNS caching mechanism to tackle these issues. The proposed mechanism presents a unique DNS storage structure on routers and suggests two implementation strategies that incorporate fingerprint verification and Bloom filters. Through analysis and extensive simulations utilizing real-world network topology, the results demonstrate that the hash-based DNS caching mechanism introduced in this study outperforms existing methods in cache hit rate and diminishes query latency.

articleTitle: CAAVM-TransUNet: Integrating Context Anchor Attention with Transformer U-Net for Single Image Dehazing
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Image dehazing has always been a challenging visual task. Most of the existing image dehazing algorithms are constructed based on convolutional neural networks, which perform very well in capturing local features and detail information, but fall short of the ability to capture remote contextual information. In this paper, we introduce a novel method called CAAVM-TransUNet. The method integrates Transformer into the traditional U -shaped architecture. Unlike earlier Transformer-based U-Net, CAA VM-TransUNet introduces the State Space Sequence Model (SSM) to enhance the ability of capturing remote dependencies, and adds Context Anchor Attention (CAA) to filter redundant features in the hopping connectivity layer prior to the encoder and decoder, so that the model can better focus on the key feature information and reduce the interference of irrelevant information, thus improving the effect of image dehazing. The results show that the dehazing effect of CAAVM-TransUNet on RESIDE dataset is better than the existing methods, especially the PSNR in the SOTS-outdoor dataset reaches 36.13 dB, which provides a new idea to solve the complex image dehazing problem.

articleTitle: A Quantitative 3D Reconstruction Evaluation Method Based on Blender
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Recently, image-based 3D reconstruction methods have made remarkable breakthroughs. However, the evaluation of 3D reconstruction is still limited to subjective judgment due to the unavailable 3D model data for ground truth. This paper proposes a quantitative evaluation method for 3D reconstruction based on the existing texture CAD models and rendering tools. To this end, we present a data simulator based on the Blender tool to generate multi-view images similar to that captured by a handheld device, i.e. a time-space continuous video of a target object. The data generated by Blender can not only be used to verify the 3D reconstruction algorithms, but also can ensure that the reconstructed geometry has the same coordinate system and scale as the CAD models through the limited camera parameters. Then, we can use the original CAD model to evaluate the reconstructed geometry and color. The experimental results show that our method can effectively evaluate the quality of 3D reconstruction.

articleTitle: Multi-View Fuzzy Clustering Based on Adaptive Local Neighbor Information
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Multi-view fuzzy clustering methods provide numerous solutions for clustering multi-view data. However, most existing fuzzy clustering methods primarily determine the membership of samples to different clusters based on the similarity between each sample and the cluster centers under various views, neglecting the similarity between samples and data within different clusters, and failing to effectively distinguish outliers. To address these issues, we propose an adaptive local neighbor information-based multi-view fuzzy clustering algorithm (ALN-MVFC). This algorithm considers the adaptive local neighbor information of each sample in different clusters, where the membership of a sample is determined by both its similarity to the cluster center and its similarity to several nearest neighbors from different clusters. Additionally, we introduce a novel outlier detection method and a way to identify the varying importance of different views. Experiments conducted on four widely-used datasets demonstrate the superiority of our algorithm.

articleTitle: Simulation Research on Link Handover Strategy and Link Characteristics of Satellite Constellations
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In response to the requirements of industry services for link quality or service access time, a link selection strategy that integrates satellite elevation angle and service time is designed. This strategy makes full use of the predictability of satellite trajectories. By adjusting parameters, a balance between average link delay, attenuation and service time can be achieved to meet the different needs of different industry services. The connection characteristics of high, medium and low orbit satellite links are calculated and discussed, providing a reference for differentiated selection of different services.

articleTitle: Joint Trajectory and Power Optimization for UAV-Assisted Communication Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: UAVs have become a key tool to assist communication networks in performing their tasks due to their mobility, flexibility and low cost. This study focuses on how to solve the problem of decreasing effective user coverage caused by increasing user data demand during data distribution of a single UAV-assisted communication network system, and proposes a method to jointly optimize the flight trajectory and transmission power of UAVs to minimize the decreasing trend of effective coverage. The problem is modeled as a mixed integer non-convex optimization problem. Therefore, a block coordinate descent algorithm based on continuous convex approximation (SCA) technique is proposed in this paper. The algorithm alternately optimizes the flight trajectory and transmission power of UAVs in each iteration, and uses SCA technology to deal with the non-convexity of trajectory and power, and transforms two non-convexity optimization problems into approximately convex optimization problems. In addition, the complexity of the algorithm is also analyzed. The experimental results show that compared with the existing benchmark scheme, the proposed scheme can effectively alleviate the problem that the effective coverage of user decreases due to the increase of user data demand.

articleTitle: Video Super-Resolution Based on Multi-Flow Guided Deformable Alignment and Temporal-Spatial Fusion
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Video super resolution aims to recover high resolution frames from multiple low resolution ones. Compared to single frame super resolution, the main challenge of video super resolution is how to effectively utilize the spatiotemporal information in video sequences. Due to inaccurate alignment of information between frames, the reconstruction results often suffer from motion blur and artifacts, which will accumulate during the propagation process and seriously affect the reconstruction quality and continuity of the video. To solve this issue, this paper proposes a Multi-Flow Guided Deformable Alignment module(MFGDA) based on a bidirectional propagation network. This module combines the multi-optical flow information of neighboring frames with deformable convolution, accurately aligns features through bidirectional information propagation, and eliminates artifacts. In addition, to better utilize spatiotemporal information, we also design a Temporal-Spatial Feature Fusion Module (TSFM) based on an attention mechanism. This module mines the spatiotemporal information of features at different time steps, eliminates the alignment errors that occur during long-term information propagation, and enhances the fusion of key features. The experimental results demonstrate that our proposed method achieves superior performance compared with state-of-the-art methods.

articleTitle: Classification of UAVs Utilizing STFT Features of RF Fingerprints and ASPConv-ResNet34 Network
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Classification of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) plays an important part in spectrum monitoring. This paper investigates the classification of UAVs from radio frequency (RF) fingerprints on the basis of using ResNet network. Firstly, we converts the RF signals captured from UAV controllers to Short-time Fourier transform (STFT) images. Then, we proposes an adaptively spatial parallel convolution (ASPConv) module to enable neurons to adaptively obtain the corresponding spatial information through multi-scale receptive fields, thereby improving the feature extraction ability. And ASPConv module replaces Conv1 in ResNet34 to form a new network called ASPConv-ResNet34, which applies Hardswith activation function. Using the proposed ASPConv- ResNet34, we classify a total of 17 different commercially available UAVs with an average testing accuracy of 99.97%, which significantly outperforms the existing approaches to our best knowledge.

articleTitle: Adversarial End-to-End Communication System: Dual Mechanisms for Anti-Interference and Anti-Eavesdropping
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Due to the broadcast characteristics of wireless channels, wireless communication systems not only encounter internal interference but also face the threat of eavesdropping. This paper proposes a multi-user symmetric encryption end-to-end (E2E) communication system that integrates both anti-interference and anti-jamming capabilities. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed system is robust to changes in interference conditions, maintaining secure communication for all users with very minimal performance degradation. Specifically, with 2 users, a modulation order of 16, achieving a symbol error rate (SER) of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−4</sup> requires only a 0.7 dB increase in the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR). In addition, the eavesdropper's SER is as high as 93.75%, which is equivalent to randomly guessing 16 symbols.

articleTitle: A Model for Large-Scale Fish Dataset Classification: SIM-CONV
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Image based aquatic organism recognition technology is one of the key technologies in the current field of aquatic ecology. By accurately identifying aquatic organisms, the structure and function of aquatic ecosystems can be better understood, providing scientific basis for the protection and management of aquatic organisms. However, current aquatic organism recognition methods have problems such as limited coverage of species and single classification methods. Based on this, this paper proposes a model SIM-CONV for fish classification in large-scale fish datasets. Due to the complexity of aquatic species, in order to provide more scientific classification results, this paper uses aquatic classification method to classify data at the phylum, genus, and species level, and classifies fish at the order and family classification levels. Common and rare samples are established for each classification level. The large-scale fish dataset FishNet is used as the experimental target, and the SIM-CONV model is obtained by introducing SIMAM attention mechanism to improve the architecture of ConvNext network and class balance training technology, which improves the accuracy of fish classification. The SIM-CONV model improved the classification accuracy of majority and rare classes at the order and family levels on the FishNet dataset by 0.83%, 2.27%, 6.45%, and 3.89%, respectively.

articleTitle: Hybrid Trusted Quantum Key Distribution Network Routing Scheme for Power Grid Environment
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: With the continuous development of quantum computing technology, Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) is an important means of secure communication in the post-quantum era. However, the high cost of trusted routing relays in QKD networks has hindered its widespread adoption in power systems. Reducing costs is the key to the popularization of QKD in large-scale data grid scenarios. Therefore, this paper proposes a routing scheme for QKD network in a hybrid trusted environment. Our scheme is based on SDN architecture, utilizing the characteristics of QKD network in hybrid trusted environment, through prioritizing the selection of trusted paths (composed entirely of trusted quantum nodes) and backup selection of hybrid trusted paths (composed of both trusted and semi-trusted quantum nodes), implementing a unified dynamic routing strategy to obtain the optimal quantum routing path. Furthermore, by collecting topology information and real-time link status of the power grid, a calculation method for the number of paths and link costs is proposed to maximize load balancing in the network. Finally, the simulation results demonstrate that our scheme outperforms routing schemes relying solely on trusted quantum nodes for key distribution, as well as other cooperative routing schemes involving semi-trusted quantum nodes, in terms of success rate of distribution and load balancing.

articleTitle: An Overview of Standardization Progress for Integrated Sensing and Communications: Use Cases, Channel Modeling and Potential Challenges
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) is a promising technique for 6G, which provides the possibility to enable smart manufacturing, smart transportation as well as smart city. Till now, 3GPP has initiated the study on ISAC in both Service & Systems Aspects (SA) and Radio Access Network (RAN) working group, aiming to identify the potential use cases, requirement and define the channel modeling details. In this paper, we provide a comprehensive overview about standardization progress of ISAC in 3GPP, including the use cases, deployment scenarios and channel modeling. In the end, the potential challenges for ISAC from operator's perspective are provided.

articleTitle: Video-Based Multi-Stage 3D Human Mesh Reconstruction
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Existing Model-based 3D human reconstruction provides a new perspective for generating realistic full-body meshes for 3D human pose estimation. However, many existing methods for reconstructing human meshes typically rely on neural networks to directly estimate the parameters of the SMPL model, subsequently utilizing the SMPL model to recover the human mesh. Despite significant progress in recent research, these methods still encounter several issues, including shape estimation overfitting, cumulative rotation errors, and rotational semantic ambiguities. Furthermore, these methods have not leveraged recent advancements in 2D and 3D pose estimation. To address these challenges, we propose a framework that decomposes the task of reconstructing 3D human meshes into three components: extracting 2D keypoints, a 2D-to-3D lifting network, and fitting the rotations of the keypoints. We decompose the rotation of the 3D keypoints into twist and swing components. In the 2D-to-3D network, we regress the 3D keypoint locations, shape parameters, and twist of the keypoints, while also introducing an optimization method for fitting the rotations. We conducted experiments on the Human3.6M dataset, achieving significant performance improvements.

articleTitle: Classification Performance Optimization Method Based on Semi-supervised Federated Learning and Dual-domain Knowledge Distillation
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Federated learning has emerged as a significant distributed learning paradigm, allowing devices to locally train models and transmit the updated parameters to a central server for aggregation, enabling collaborative model updates. However, data heterogeneity and catastrophic forgetting bring distinctive challenges. First, in non-lID (identically and independently distributed) data environments, model performance in other domains deteriorates significantly. Second, during local updates, models are optimized solely on local data, which leads to overfitting to the current data distribution and forgetting previously learned knowledge, resulting in catastrophic forgetting. Finally, traditional federated learning methods require the transmission of large model parameters, which results in high communication overhead. To address these challenges, we propose a classification performance optimization method based on semi-supervised federated learning and dual-domain knowledge distillation. For the data heterogeneity problem, we leverage unlabeled public data to enhance the model's generalization capability across different data distributions, thereby improving classifier performance. To mitigate catastrophic forgetting, we incorporate knowledge distillation in local updates, facilitating both inter and intra domain information sharing while preserving privacy. Experimental results demonstrate that, compared to typical federated learning methods, our method achieves better classification performance with lower communication overhead.

articleTitle: An Adaptive Self-Loading FxLMS with DOA Estimation Strategy by Circular Error Sensor Array for Active Noise Control of Indoor Environment
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Traditional active noise control (ANC) uses FxLMS (Filtered-x Least Mean Square) method to achieve fast noise attenuation. However, in sound zone construction process, the FxLMS may fail to distinguish between sounds that need to be heard and unwanted noise. Which may lead to unstable of sound zone. Thus, a new adaptive self-loading FxLMS (ASL-FxLMS) is proposed. The additional ASL filter will increase the ability to distinguish useful sounds from unwanted noise compared to FxLMS. Moreover, to distinguish useful sounds and unwanted noise, circular error sensor array (CESA) is also used instead of the single error sensor in single channel ANC. This will enhance direction recognition ability, thereby improving noise reduction capability. Furthermore, the updating equations is also influenced by the DOA (direction of arrival) strategy provided by the CESA. Theoretical instantaneous residual output error (IROE) analysis and attenuation simulations prove the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Skin Lesion Recognition and Classification Based on Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Skin cancer is one of the most common cancers in the world, characterized by rapid progression and high lethality. Early diagnosis of skin lesion types can significantly improve patient recovery rates. So, methods of automatic skin lesion recognition are proposed, struggling to achieve high accuracy. In recent years, deep learning has achieved significant results in various research fields. Existing methods for skin lesion classification primarily utilize convolutional neural networks and residual networks, but their accuracies and efficiencies still need improvement. Therefore, we propose a deep learning model that integrates the VIT and SEN et50 architectures for the automatic classification of seven different types of skin lesions. Experimental results demonstrate that the model achieves accuracy of 0.932.

articleTitle: Accurate Detection of Superspreaders on Multi-Pipeline Switches
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In various network monitoring tasks, the detection of superspreaders has become increasingly crucial. However, latest superspreader detection algorithms and data structures assume the target switch with a single pipeline, while state-of-the-art programmable switches actually comprise multiple independent pipelines. In current method for deploying super-spreader detection applications on multi-pipeline switches, a separate measurement data structure instance is employed for each pipeline. However, under multi-path routing, this simplistic approach leads to lower detection accuracy due to hash collisions. To address this issue, in this paper, we present PipelineAlloc, a HyperLogLog-based superspreader detection system designed for multi-pipeline switches. In order to reduce hash collisions in measurement data structures, PipelineAlloc assigns an egress pipeline as the monitor pipeline for each source IP address. PipelineAlloc introduces novel measurement data structures in the ingress pipelines for temporarily storing statistics of the source and destination IP addresses of packets, and uses packets to carry these measurement data to egress pipelines, which serve as the monitor pipelines. The HyperLogLog-based measurement data structures in egress pipelines are updated using data carried by packets. Experiments driven by real-world traffic traces show that PipelineAlloc outperforms existing solutions in terms of detection accuracy.

articleTitle: A Distributed Storage Method Based on Elasticsearch and MinIO Cluster Federation
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: This paper aims to propose a solution to address issues related to small file storage, data retrieval speed, and system resource consumption in existing technologies. The main approach involves federating Elasticsearch and MinIO clusters to form an efficient federated cluster. Based on this foundation, file upload operations and validity checks are implemented to ensure file effectiveness and security. Files that pass the checks are stored in the MinIO federated cluster to achieve efficient data storage and management. Simultaneously, the file addresses from the MinIO cluster are mapped, and the file information is synchronized with the Elasticsearch cluster to enable fast data retrieval and redundant storage. Finally, user access to files through applications is supported, ensuring that users can efficiently and conveniently obtain the required files. Through these measures, this approach not only improves the efficiency of small file storage and retrieval but also optimizes system resource usage, providing a reliable distributed storage solution. Experimental results demonstrate that this approach enables small file storage through Elasticsearch and MinIO.

articleTitle: Photovoltaic Power Prediction Based on Multi-Model Integration
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Photovoltaic (PV) power generation has been widely applied in recent years due to its renewable and environmentally friendly nature. However, the power output of PV generation is highly influenced by meteorological factors, resulting in significant randomness and volatility, which poses challenges to grid scheduling and energy management. Existing prediction methods, such as traditional statistical models and individual deep learning models, have limitations in handling complex nonlinear relationships and long-term dependencies. To address these issues, this paper proposes a photovoltaic power prediction method based on feature extraction and multi-model optimization integration. First, the importance of meteorological factors is evaluated using the XGBoost model to extract key features, and the feature set is further optimized using a weighted recursive feature elimination method. Then, an improved Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) model is used to capture long-term dependencies in the time series, while TimesNet is employed for efficient time feature extraction and modeling. Finally, a self-adaptive weighted fusion strategy is used to integrate the prediction results to maximize the performance of each model. Experimental results show that the proposed method outperforms existing individual models in terms of both accuracy and stability, demonstrating significant advantages.

articleTitle: Blockchain Technology Promoting Data Privacy Protection and Sharing in Communication Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Data privacy protection and sharing are key challenges in communication networks, and how to promote data resource sharing while protecting data security has always been a concern. This paper explores how to use blockchain technology to promote data privacy protection and sharing in communication networks. In this paper, we design a blockchain-based data privacy protection and sharing system architecture, which includes key modules such as user authentication, data encrypted storage, distributed access control, etc., aiming at realizing the full life cycle management of data. Meanwhile, this paper comprehensively evaluates the performance of blockchain technology in communication network data management. The experimental results show that the data privacy protection coverage of blockchain technology in communication network is significantly higher than that of traditional centralized technology, reaching 95.8 % on average, which reflects its advantages in distributed and encrypted aspects.

articleTitle: Max-Min Throughput Design for Wireless Body Area Network with Backscatter Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Recently, wireless body area network (WBAN) has become a prospective body monitoring system that can provide stable health services. In this paper, we propose a WBAN assisted by the backscatter communication (Backcom). In order to improve the throughput and ensure the fairness and quality of service (Qos) during the backscatter period, we investigate a throughput optimization problem based on the max-min fairness principle and introduce the robustness constraints. Because we jointly optimize the transmission power of access point (AP), backscattering coefficient, and backscattering time of the WBAN, making the optimization problem non-convex caused by the coupled variables. Therefore, we use the slack variable method and the successive convex approximation (SCA) method to convert the non-convex problem into convex. Simulation results show that compared to the traditional sum throughput algorithm and the linear energy harvested model, our proposed algorithm brings better fairness and robustness.

articleTitle: A Parameter Decoupling Approach in Personalized Federated Learning for Gastric Cancer Pathology Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Existing personalized federated learning methods face challenges when processing complex microscopic features, such as cellular morphology and tissue structure, in pathological images, often encountering difficulty in accurately capturing critical pathological features in participants' local models. The parameter decoupling-based personalized federated learning method can effectively address the aforementioned issues. However, different parameter decoupling settings can impact the model's ability to extract features from pathological images. This paper proposes a parameter decoupling strategy that divides the model into two core components: the classifier layer and the connecting layer. The connecting layer focuses on capturing and transmitting key information, ensuring effective feature transfer across different levels; the classifier layer is responsible for integrating features and generating the final task output, ensuring efficient aggregation of information during the decision-making process. Through this parameter decoupling strategy, information can flow efficiently across different levels, enabling the model to extract key information related to cellular lesions more effectively. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms other personalized federated learning approaches in the task of gastric cancer pathology image classification, achieving an accuracy improvement of % over the baseline, validating the effectiveness of the proposed framework and its corresponding parameter decoupling strategy.

articleTitle: Optimal Scheduling of Multi-Source Multi-Destination Links in Multi-UAV Assisted Ad Hoc Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) acting as relays provide new opportunities for assisted wireless communications. However, in a multi-UAV-assisted multi-source multi-destination communication network, there are many challenges in achieving parallel data transmission of multiple source-destination (S-D) pairs and maximizing the throughput of the entire network. To this end, this paper comprehensively considers the influence of interference and noise between source nodes and between relay UAVs, and proposes a source-to-UAV and UAV-to-destination joint link scheduling optimization problem to maximize the throughput of the entire communication network. To solve the optimization problem, this paper also proposes two optimization matching algorithms namely Global Optimal Precision Matching (GOPM) and Dual-order KM Optimized Matching (DKOM). Simulation results show that the two optimization matching algorithms effectively improve network throughput in scenarios with parallel transmission of multiple S-D pairs. In addition, with the increase of network scale, two algorithms show similar performance.

articleTitle: Enhanced Fusion of AMR Graph Representations for Event Argument Extraction
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Event Argument Extraction (EAE) is a key task in natural language processing that involves identifying and classifying events and their arguments in text. With advancements in language models, the quality of semantic representation is becoming more crucial for the success of EAE. Abstract Meaning Representation (AMR), as a graphical semantic representation form, effectively captures the semantic structures of complex sentences, providing valuable contextual information for the EAE task. Current research indicates that AMR plays an important role in EAE by offering detailed event and argument relationships, helping models better understand the semantic aspects of text. However, existing models often face inefficiencies in integrating AMR graph information, leading to subpar performance in extracting from complex texts. Additionally, many models fail to fully utilize multimodal information, limiting their performance improvements. Therefore, we propose EAGF, an Enhanced AMR Graph Fusion method, which aims to improve EAE effectiveness through enhanced AMR graph representation fusion. EAGF first conducts in-depth analysis of the AMR graph using Graph Attention Networks (GAT), extracting graph embeddings with rich context. Then, these embeddings undergo cross-modal attention fusion with the input text embeddings, and the fusion results are injected into the attention mechanism of the encoder in the generative model. Through this approach, EAGF effectively integrates information from different sources, improving the accuracy of event argument extraction. Experimental results show that EAGF achieves significant performance improvements across multiple benchmark datasets.

articleTitle: Adversarial Attacks Against Black-Box Network Intrusion Detection Based on Heuristic Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Machine learning has become an increasingly utilized approach for developing Network Intrusion Detection Systems (NIDS) for identifying anomalies associated with malicious network intrusions. Even in a black-box attack setting, where the attacker only has access to the output, machine learning-based classifiers are vulnerable to adversarial examples. This paper proposes a universal perturbation generation method based on a heuristic algorithm for generating adversarial examples to perform black-box attacks against different technology based NIDSs. The simulation results show that the adversarial examples generated by the proposed perturbation generation approach reduce the accuracy of multiple single and hybrid NIDS models.

articleTitle: MIMO and RIS-Assisted Localization Method in 6G Terahertz Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: 6G terahertz technology is regarded as a crucial component for future networks because of its comprehensive frequency range. Terahertz systems can achieve unprecedented data rates and precision sensing. We study the terahertz signal through one transmitter along with a RIS and under conditions where the line-of-sight path is blocked, we can derive expressions for the channel-dependent parameters. Drawing on that, we get a two-stage algorithm to estimate the position of the user. The algorithm estimates the channel parameters based on the orthogonal matching pursuit of vectors under multiple carriers and finally recovers the distance and the angle of arrival of the user. Using the signal from the base station, we find that the target user can be accurately located through the RIS under obstructed line-of-sight paths.

articleTitle: Generative Model for Joint Resource Management in Multi-Cell Multi-Carrier NOMA Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In this work, we design a generative artificial intelligence(GAI) -based framework for joint resource allocation, beamforming, and power allocation in multi-cell multi-carrier non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) networks. We formulate the proposed problem as sum rate maximization problem. Next, we design a novel multi-task transformer (MTT) framework to handle the problem in real-time. To provide the necessary training set, we consider simplified but powerful mathematical techniques from the literature. Then, we train and test the proposed MTT. We perform simulation to evaluate the efficiency of the proposed MTT and compare its performance with the mathematical baseline.

articleTitle: Deep Learning for Movable Antenna Precoding in 2D MISO Communication System
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
