abstract: The rapid advancement of wireless communication systems has spurred the exploration of innovative methods to significantly enhance signal transmission efficiency. Movable Antenna (MA) technology has emerged as a promising approach to improving the spatial characteristics of wireless channels. In flexible precoding systems, the positions of antennas at the trans-mitter can be dynamically adjusted to adapt to changing channel conditions. However, optimizing the positions of a large number of movable antennas in massive MIMO systems introduces substantial complexity, making real-time channel adaptation a critical challenge. By incorporating mobility into the antenna array, it becomes possible to design a more efficient and robust intelligent communication system. This paper proposes a CNN-based Flexible Precoding (CBFP) framework that leverages deep learning (DL) techniques to optimize both antenna positions and beamforming weights. Furthermore, we present the theoretical foundations and develop a two-dimensional (2D) antenna position search algorithm to identify the optimal configuration, while en-suring compliance with the minimum antenna spacing constraint. Extensive experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method significantly outperforms other optimization techniques, yielding notable improvements in both spectral efficiency and computational efficiency.

articleTitle: Cryptanalysis of Two Lightweight Authentication Protocols for IoT Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Internet of Things (IoT) play an increasingly important role in the field of smart-healthcare, intelligent industry, and smart city, etc. Authentication protocol is vital to ensure data security and user privacy. Recently, Guo and Guo put forward a lightweight authentication protocol for IoT environments. Zhang et al. presented a privacy-preserving authentication protocol for IoT-based e-health systems. Both these two schemes are designed to be rigorous, and preserve critical security properties. But after careful analysis, we found there are a few peccadilloes in their schemes. Specifically, Guo-Guo's scheme is vulnerable to multiple insider attacks, smart device captured attack, and violates forward secrecy. Zhang et al.'s scheme is susceptible to replay attack, and fails to preserve three-factor secrecy and forward secrecy.

articleTitle: Radio Frequency Fingerprinting Method Based on Empirical Modal Decomposition and Frequency Domain Phase Characterization
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Radio frequency (RF) fingerprinting is an RF signal identification method based on unintentional features of radio devices. In order to improve the accuracy of RF fingerprinting of autocorrelated surveillance broadcast (ADS-B) signals, a feature extraction method based on feature fusion of ADS-B signals is proposed. First, we employed empirical mode decomposition (EMD) and Fourier Transform to extract the intrinsic mode functions (IMFs) and frequency domain phases of pulse sequences. Subsequently, the extracted features were downscaled using principal component analysis (PCA) and the two downscaled features were fused into a single feature matrix using the operation of matrix fork product. Ultimately, we have designed an innovative residual neural network (ResNet) that incorporates an attention mechanism and integrates depthwise separable (DWS) convolution with an LSTM layer for training on feature matrices. The performance of the model was rigorously assessed on a validation set. Validation was carried out using pulse sequences extracted from the ADS-B signals of 43 civil aircraft. The results show a classification accuracy of 99.65%, thus affirming the validity of the method for real data, multi-category classification.

articleTitle: A Lyapunov Optimization Strategy with Deep Reinforcement Learning in Cloud-Edge Collaborative Service Offloading Scenarios
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Lyapunov optimization is a promising technology for stabilizing systems and reducing energy consumption in multi-edge-server collaborative computing scenarios. Existing studies have led to the instantaneous greedy issue, owing to the constant operation in the queue length calculation and local optimization. Therefore, this study tries to improve the Lyapunov optimization with deep reinforcement learning (DRL). First, the Lyapunov optimization framework was employed to build the queue model and derive the upper bound of the system objective function. Second, the system action and state space were constructed based on the queue model, and a Lyapunov optimization module was formulated to minimize the system energy consumption. Third, a reward function was created by integrating the reward discount factor. Finally, a soft actor-critic algorithm was used to train the adaptive cloud-edge service offloading strategy. Many experimental results show that the system does not need to obtain a local optimal solution in each time slot to ensure the stability of the queue and reduce energy consumption.

articleTitle: Research on Fabric Defect Detection Algorithm Based on Improved YOLOv8s
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Fabric defect detection plays a pivotal role in the textile industry. To tackle challenges like the wide range of fabric defect types, their small sizes, and the need for higher detection accuracy, we propose an enhanced YOLOv8s-based algorithm tailored for fabric defect detection. To boost the precision of detecting small defects, we've introduced a multi-scale feature fusion mechanism. This mechanism innovatively fuses CA (channel attention) and MSAM (multi-scale attention module) to create the CMSA (channel and multi-scale attention module). The CMSA is seamlessly integrated into the final layer of the YOLOv8s feature fusion network, addressing the issue of misalignment between classification and localization tasks. Additionally, it enriches contextual information for feature fusion, bolstering the model's multi-scale feature extraction capabilities and enhancing sensitivity to small targets. Experiments on the fabric defect dataset from the Alibaba Cloud Tianchi Competition reveal that our proposed algorithm outperforms the original YOLOv8s, achieving a 2.4% improvement in the map@0.5 metric.

articleTitle: ADRC Parameter Tuning of Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor Based on Improved CPO Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: At present, the control algorithm of permanent magnet synchronous motor(PMSM) is still dominated by the traditional proportional-integral-differential(PID) control mode, which has some problems such as easy to be affected by external disturbance, rapidity and irreconcilable overshoot. A second-order nonlinear active disturbance rejection controller(ADRC) is designed to replace the traditional PID controller, and a position control system based on vector control is constructed. Aiming at the problems that the ADRC involves many parameters, the tuning process depends heavily on the working experience of engineers, the process is complicated, and the debugging is complicated, an improved optimization algorithm is proposed to realize the parameter tuning of ADRC. Firstly, the good points set is used to optimize the individual location distribution of the population to make the population distribution more uniform and increase the global search ability and stability in the early stage. Secondly, the nonlinear dynamic weights are introduced to better balance the global search and local search. Finally, the adaptive t-distribution perturbation and variation are introduced to increase the development ability and avoid falling into the local optimal solution. Through simulation experiments, particle swarm optimization algorithm(PSO) algorithm, gray wolf optimization(GWO) algorithm and original crested porcupine optimization(CPO) algorithm are compared, and the results show that the proposed method performs better.

articleTitle: Performance Comparison Between HLS and HDL on Load Design of VTA Accelerator
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: The increasing complexity of DNN networks makes it harder to quickly design and deploy complete DNN accelerators in FPGA platforms. High-level-synthesis (HLS) is a common solution to simplify the design process and increase the abstraction level in system development. However, whether HLS compilation could make full use of hardware and timing resources is always needed to be considered. In this paper, a comparative study of HLS and HDL are presented focusing on load design of Versatile Tensor Accelerator (VTA). The design method of two development tools are introduced in detail. Through fine-grained instruction analysis, it can be determined that the AXI bus mechanism of HDL version is superior to HLS. Based on Xilinx ZCU104 development board, YOLOV3 are deployed and network performance evaluations are proposed. The results show that HDL design can greatly improve the load bandwidth compared with HLS, the resource utilization and power consumption are also better than HLS, which indicates limitations of HLS design in load data optimization.

articleTitle: Multi-Scale Feature Fusion for Low-light Image Enhancement in the RAW Domain
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: With advancements in technology, low-light image enhancement has become a popular research topic. Traditional methods are constrained by fixed processing windows or specific algorithm frameworks, making it challenging to fully capture and enhance global details in low-light images. Deep learning models based on self-attention mechanisms excel at capturing long-range dependencies but come with high computational costs and limited ability to enhance local details. To address these issues, we propose a Multi-scale Feature Fusion Network(MFFNet) that integrates self-attention mechanisms with convolutional neural networks(CNN). By employing local and global feature extraction modules, MFFNet effectively captures features at different semantic scales, enhancing global luminance distribution while preserving rich local details for more refined and comprehensive enhancement. To further enhance the quality of image recovery, we design the discriminator module to distinguish the generated image from the real image, thus providing additional supervisory signals. The discriminator is able to learn the subtle differences between the real image and the recovered image and guide the generative model to produce more natural and realistic enhanced images.

articleTitle: Wavelet Denoising Parameter Selection Method Based on Generalized Cross-Validation(GCV)
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: The wavelet threshold denoising method is fast and straightforward, widely applicable in various signal denoising scenarios. One of its critical aspects is the selection of the optimal wavelet basis and the determination of the best decomposition level. Addressing the challenge of unifying the wavelet basis and decomposition level when applying wavelet threshold denoising to noisy signals, a method based on the Generalized Cross-Validation (GCV) criterion for selecting optimal parameters is proposed. This algorithm defines an objective function based on the GCV criterion, aiming to minimize it to select the asymptotically optimal wavelet basis and the best decomposition level. To validate the rationale and effectiveness of this approach and to enhance the credibility and reliability of experimental results, we employ both hard thresholding (H) and soft thresholding (S) methods to handle different noisy signals. Furthermore, we evaluate the algorithm's performance using signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and mean square error (MSE). Experimental results demonstrate that this method can rapidly and accurately identify the optimal combination of wavelet basis and decomposition level. Applying this combination to wavelet threshold denoising yields higher SNR and lower MSE.

articleTitle: Construction of Audit Virtual Simulation Teaching and Training System Based on Unity 3D
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In recent years, with the continuous development of virtual simulation technology, its application in the field of education has become increasingly widespread. Traditional audit teaching lacks practice, and students can only learn in the form of theoretical courses without a deep understanding. The aim of this study is to design and implement an audit virtual simulation teaching and training system based on Unity 3D, to enhance students' understanding of audit courses. At the same time, the system will combine advanced virtual reality technology to provide students with an almost realistic auditing environment, allowing them to interact and experience immersive learning in a virtual scene that is close to reality, and complete the process of auditing verification. In the design process, at first, the Unity theoretical knowledge required for the design scenario is primarily analyzed. Then, the content of each learning stage in the audit course is described. Supported by Unity 3D, the advantages and technical system of the system are studied, and the process from scene modeling, scene interaction, UI design, data integration to testing the application is completed, proving the effectiveness of the system development. Finally, an explanation is provided on how to optimize the system from which aspects. This system provides strong support for improving the teaching level of auditing majors and promoting the application of virtual simulation technology in higher education.

articleTitle: Research on the Prediction Method of Remaining Tool Life Based on GASF-LSTM-Attention
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Accurate and reliable tool life prediction is important for improving machining reliability and reducing production costs. There are differences in the life degradation progress of different tools under the same working conditions. By analyzing the life curves, the tool life process can be divided into different stages. The Gramian Angular Summation Field (GASF) images of the sensor data exhibit consistent patterns in the same stages of different tools. Based on this, a high-precision tool life prediction framework that fuses deep feature extraction of GASF images with time series modeling is proposed. Firstly, a convolutional neural network is utilized to extract features from GASF images, while the features of the original time-series signals are fed into a long-short-term memory network to capture the dependencies in the time series. Based on this, the attention mechanism is added to enhance the model's focus on key features. Finally, the outputs of the modules are fused to perform lifetime prediction via a fully connected neural network. Experimental results show that the proposed method reduces the root mean square error by at least 0.3 %, which validates the effectiveness and feasibility of the model.

articleTitle: TimesKAN: A Generic Backbone Network for Time Series Prediction Based on Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: The field of time series analysis has significant applications in various domains, including physiological signals, weather prediction, and power systems. However, the intricate data patterns inherent in time series often lead to suboptimal performance of conventional models. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a novel multivariate time series prediction model called TimesKAN based on the Kolmogorov-Arnold network, drawing inspiration from the Kolmogorov-Arnold representation theorem. This model consists of two key components: (i) KAN layers constructed using B-splines as learnable activation function feature extractors instead of commonly used convolution and transformer structures in traditional time series models. B-splines are smooth piecewise polynomial functions capable of approximating complex shapes and patterns effectively, enabling the network to capture subtle changes in the data without being affected by abrupt changes or discontinuities; (ii) We introduce embedding multivariate channel independence for KAN layers where each channel contains a single univariate time series that utilizes independent KAN weights for each KAN input while sharing independent channel weights across all embeddings. This extension allows KAN layers to effectively handle complex data models. Experimental results demonstrate that TimesKAN outperforms many state-of-the-art frameworks for long-term predictions on 85% of datasets and short-term predictions on all datasets. The feature extraction method based on the Kolmogorov-Arnold representation theorem significantly enhances both long-term and short-term prediction accuracy. Furthermore, TimesKAN exhibits excellent performance when dealing with periodicity and trend within time series data while also adapting well to unstable changes within such sequences. The Kolmogorov-Arnold representation theorem provides a promising alternative, presenting opportunities for further enhancements to contemporary deep learning models that heavily rely on convolutional and transformer architectures.

articleTitle: Joint Routing and Scheduling for Deterministic Transmission in Drone Swarm Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: The coordination and flexibility of drone swarm networks play a critical role in future combat scenarios. Since the operational tasks and functions become more complex, the time-sensitive services, including control commands, real-time audio and video streams, requires higher transmission performance. In this paper, we propose a joint routing and scheduling scheme to satisfy the deterministic transmission requirements in drone swarm networks. This scheme integrates segmented source routing and time-division multiplexing to construct a joint routing and scheduling mechanism, to control the service transmission delay within the required range. First, we analyze the architecture and service flow characteristics of swarm network, to establish a three-layer cross-layer model of service flow - forwarding link - time slot. Subsequently, an optimal link selection and time-slot allocation scheme is designed based on an integrated ant colony tabu search algorithm. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed scheme outperforms traditional CSMA and TD-GPSR schemes in performance metrics such as end-to-end delay, packet loss rate, and scheduling success rate, particularly under high-load conditions.

articleTitle: An Automatic Tooth Position and Dental Disease Detection Algorithm Based on YOLOv8
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: With the development of digital dental imaging technology, panoramic tomographic images have become an effective tool for diagnosing dental diseases. However, due to the diversity and complexity of dental lesions, accurately identifying tooth positions and pathological conditions from these images remains challenging. To address the issue of low target detection accuracy caused by the high similarity and complex textures of teeth, this paper introduces YOLOv8-Teeth, an enhanced teeth detection algorithm designed for accurate identification of teeth positions and dental diseases from panoramic radiographs. Key innovations include integrating the C2f_ConvNeXtv2 module for improved feature extraction, employing the ASPP module for optimized multi-scale feature capture, and utilizing Focal-EloU Loss for refined bounding box regression. Experimental results on a custom dataset of 476 panoramic radiographs demonstrate significant performance gains, achieving a mean average precision (mAP) of 91.3%, precision of 93.6%, and recall of 88.7%. These improvements offer promising potential for early diagnosis and treatment planning in dental care.

articleTitle: Mixed Multi-Scale and Channel Attention Representations for Concealed Object Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Concealed object detection aims to identify and locate hard-to-detect targets, which are often challenging to discern due to their small size, high degree of integration with the environment, occlusions, or unfavorable lighting conditions. Despite significant advancements in this field, the majority of existing methods still fall short in fully utilizing information across various scales and channels, thereby limiting the indepth perception of the target's scale features and channel features. To address this limitation, this paper introduces a segmentation network based on mixed multi-scale and channel attention, named MMCANet, which encompasses two core modules: the Mixed Multi-Scale Attention Module (MMAM) and the Group-Reversal Attention with Channel Module (GRAC). Mixed Multi-Scale Attention Module (MMAM) aims to extract multi-scale and inter-scale relational information, while the GRAC module focuses on enhancing channel feature extraction through the synergy of group-reversal attention and channel attention, aiming for precise segmentation of concealed objects. The method proposed in this study was thoroughly evaluated on datasets such as CHAMELEON, CAMO-Test, and COD10KTest, demonstrating significant performance improvements over existing algorithms across various evaluation metrics. These experimental results not only validate the effectiveness of our algorithm in enhancing inter-scale and inter-channel information extraction capabilities but also underscore its practical value in the domain of concealed object detection.

articleTitle: A Novel Method for Data Aggregation in Internet of Things (IoT) Networks Using Colored Petri Net (CPN) Modeling and Reinforcement Learning (RL)
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel method for data aggregation in Internet of Things (IoT) networks, utilizing Colored Petri Net (CPN) modeling and Reinforcement Learning (RL) to outperform traditional data aggregation techniques in terms of energy consumption, end-to-end delay, and network lifetime. Experimental results indicate that the proposed method achieves a 20-25% reduction in energy consumption, 15-20% lower end-to-end delay, and a 20-25% increase in network lifetime. These findings provide scalability and improved quality of service for resource-constrained IoT applications. Potential challenges include computational overhead, convergence time, and security concerns, necessitating further research. Future research directions involve integrating the method with edge computing, real-world deployment testing, developing hybrid algorithms, exploring adaptive reward functions, and assessing the environmental impact.

articleTitle: Research on Anomaly Detection Method of Power Generation Data Based on Isolation Forest
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In the realm of power systems, anomaly detection techniques have proven instrumental, particularly in scrutinizing power generation datasets. Building upon this foundation, an innovative anomaly detection algorithm known as BPSO-iForest has been formulated. This novel approach enhances the conventional Isolated Forest algorithm by integrating Binary Particle Swarm Optimization (BPSO) to both refine its precision and augment execution speed. The BPSO-iForest algorithm addresses dual challenges inherent in traditional isolation forests: the algorithmic efficiency downturn and the potential detrimental impact of less discerning trees on the overall detection outcome.attest to the superior clustering capabilities and enhanced anomaly detectionproficiency of the proposed BPSO-iForest algorithm. Its efficacy transcends mere theoretical promise, demonstrating tangible benefits when deployed for the surveillance of abnormal power generation patterns within the energy sector. This cuttingedge methodology thus ensures a robust line of defense against anomalies in power generation data, fortifying the reliability and resilience of power grid operations.

articleTitle: Enhanced Differential Interaction Representation for Joint Entity-Relation Extraction
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Although significant advances in jointly extracting entities and relationships from text, challenges remain in enhancing semantic richness and effectively leveraging the intrinsic relationships between subtasks. Many recent approaches either share feature representations, leading to feature interference, or independently encode the two tasks but neglect their inherent interdependence. In cases where interaction exists, they often prioritize commonalities, overlooking the critical capture of distinguishing information. To overcome this limitation, this paper introduces a novel Cross-Attention Information Interaction Fusion (CAIF) module, which separates the tasks into two independent subtasks, achieving effective fusion of common information while capturing differential information. Specifically, CAIF consists of a Differential Information Extraction Module (DIEM) and a Similar Information Fusion Module (SIFM). DIEM facilitates cross-tasks differential feature extraction, while SIFM captures common information and integrates long dependencies. Extensive experiments conducted on four datasets have shown that our model outperforms other baseline models.

articleTitle: An Enhanced WSN Node Localization Approach in IoT
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: With the development of satellite communication technology, the integration of satellite communication into the satellite Internet of Things(Satellite IoT) is gradually becoming a key technology for achieving global coverage and seamless connectivity. Among these technologies, wireless sensor networks (WSN), as a core component of the satellite IoT, play an indispensable role in real-time data collection and processing. However, the positioning accuracy of WSN nodes still faces challenges such as complex environments and signal interference. To address the issue of low positioning accuracy of WSN nodes, this paper proposes an improved heterogeneous Ivy algorithm integrated with Kalman filtering (KF-HIvy). This approach, combined with the three-anchor centroid method and expected hop progress(EHP), aims to reduce WSN node positioning errors. The proposed method first uses the three-anchor centroid method and EHP to estimate the distance of unknown nodes, and then applies the KF-HIvy algorithm for node position estimation. Simulation experiments on WSN show that the KF-HIvy algorithm achieves low positioning errors under different WSN configurations, demonstrating strong adaptability in various scenarios, and significantly improving the stability and reliability of node positioning.

articleTitle: STRL: Writer-Independent Offline Signature Verification with Transformers and Self-Supervised Representation Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Handwritten signature verification is a commonly used method of identity authentication, but given its relatively lower fabrication difficulty compared to other biometric characteristics like facial recognition, designing algorithms for this purpose poses greater challenges. Existing handwritten signature verification algorithms mainly suffer from two drawbacks: firstly, due to the private and confidentiality of signatures, there is often a lack of substantial high-quality signature images for model training. Secondly, the majority of existing algorithms are implemented using convolutional architectures, where the localized neighborhood operations of CNNs limit the model's ability to capture the global interrelationships of signature strokes. To address these challenges, we introduce a self-supervised learning algorithm grounded in the Transformer framework. This approach incorporates convolutional cropping and grayscale inversion for the preprocessing of input images. Additionally, we integrate a convolutional image block encoding module into the network to supplement the network with local contextual information. The superiority of our proposed algorithm over current state-of-the-art self-supervised algorithms is validated through t-SNE visualization modeling and comparative ablation studies, demonstrating its feasibility.

articleTitle: Graphical Auto-Encoder Based Fault Cases Clustering with Multi-Feature Fusion
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Addressing the challenge of potential multiple and complex correlations between fault cases that are difficult to discern and thus fail to effectively guide similar fault handling, this study is dedicated to mining and analyzing the intrinsic connections between fault cases by employing advanced graph clustering techniques, and develops a highly efficient clustering model to improve the utilization of knowledge from historical fault cases. Firstly, a graph auto-encoder based on the characteristics of neighbor nodes is constructed, in which two GraphSAGE layers and an attention layer are introduced to fully integrate the neighbor information within two hops. Subsequently, a self-training clustering module is constructed, and the total objective function is defined through a joint optimization strategy to aggregate the cases with high similarity into the same cluster. Finally, comparative experiments are conducted to validate the model in the field of fault cases clustering effectiveness, and compared with the mainstream model, the accuracy (ACC), normalized mutual information (NMI) and adjusted Rand index (ARI) evaluation indexes are significantly improved.

articleTitle: AirSim-Based Multi-UAV Collaborative Exploration by Aggregating Actions
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) are increasingly employed in rescue, reconnaissance, and other critical fields due to their high mobility. However, most cluster algorithms based on multi-agent deep reinforcement learning (MADRL) remain confined to simulation, with a significant gap between simulation and reality. The AirSim 3D simulator offers highly realistic sim-ulation capabilities, bridging the gap to real-world deployment. This paper presents the AirSim-based MADRL training frame-work addressing the challenge of collaborative exploration under partial observation. We leverage the integration of MADRL with AirSim to avoid costly real-world testing and more efficiently validate the MADRL algorithm's feasibility. Successively we employ real-time imagery captured by UAVs, combined with the identification and relocalization algorithm, to accurately locate Points of Interest (PoIs) on the map. Unlike in 2D environments, UAV s in AirSim exhibit a tilted flight trajectory. This character-istic is leveraged to develop three distinct observation acquisition methods that enhance the field of view. Furthermore, we intro-duce the GAAC (Graph Attention Network Aggregating Actions by Actor-Critic) algorithm, which effectively aggregates action information to enhance the awareness of neighboring agents. The experimental results robustly confirm the feasibility of the proposed framework, demonstrating its practical effectiveness in multi-UAV collaborative exploration tasks. Additionally, GAAC demonstrates improvements over other mainstream algorithms, particularly in enhancing exploration efficiency.

articleTitle: An Embedded ZigBee Identification System Based on LMS Filter
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: ZigBee technology, which is widely used in low-power and low-data-rate applications, encounters challenges in accurate device recognition. This paper presents a deep learning-based approach for device identification utilizing the physical radio frequency fingerprint (RFF) of ZigBee devices. To enhance performance in cross-scenario identification, artificial noise and simulated channel impairments were introduced for data augmentation. A Least Mean Squares (LMS) filter was employed for estimating channel coefficients, specifically designed for channel impulse response simulation. The proposed methodology was implemented and validated on the cost-effective LPA3588 platform using a convolutional neural network (CNN) based on differential constellation trace figures (DCTF). Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach in improving the performance of deep learning models for device recognition under real-world conditions.

articleTitle: Optimization Scheme for Outage Probability of Long-Distance Data Transmission Based on Resonant-Motion Under Malicious Jamming
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) have been widely used in cooperative data transmission owing to its highly controllable maneuverability and scalability. Yet, when the distance is long, deployment density is low, and malicious jamming exists in the scenario, it becomes impossible for UAVs to deliver data as relaying in real-time. To resolve this challenge, we propose an innovative UAV cooperative end-to-end data transmission approach leveraging the resonant motion concept(here after we refer as RM), making it possible. Then, based on the channel scenario of the Rician fading model, the closed expression of the RM link outage probability is derived, and the influence of malicious jamming on the performance of the RM link is analyzed from the perspective of the outage probability. Finally, by comparing and analyzing the outage probability of the traditional relaying UAV and RM transmission mode, simulation results show that in the same scenario, the link outage probability of the UAV-based system with RM motion is lower and the antijamming performance is better.

articleTitle: Task Migration in LEO Satellite Networks: A Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Low Earth orbit satellite edge computing (LEO-SEC) networks, equipped with edge servers, provide computational and storage services to users globally, thereby reducing service latency. However, the stochastic nature of tasks and the heterogeneity of resources can result in load imbalances among satellites, adversely affecting user experience and system stability. Therefore, studying the issue of task migration in LEO-SEC networks is crucial. This paper investigates the task migration problem between LEO satellites, considering load imbalance and the dynamic nature of LEO-SEC networks. The problem is modeled as an integer programming (IP) problem. To solve it, we develop a multi-agent Markov decision process (MAMDP) and propose a migration approach based on the multi-agent proximal policy optimization (MAPPO) algorithm. Simulation results demonstrate the convergence performance of the proposed method and show that it outperforms baseline schemes in terms of efficiency and effectiveness.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Particle Swarm Optimization Algorithm for Multi-Objective UAV Swarm Topology Shaping
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: UAV swarm need to form specific topology shapes based on the requirements of various missions. Existing topology shaping methods adopting fixed topology shaping positions fail to optimize the total traveled distance for formation switching of UAV swarm. Moreover, the use of simplified energy models often leads to inaccurate shaping decisions. To cope with these drawbacks, this paper proposes a multi-objective optimization approach for UAV swarm topology shaping based on the Particle Swarm Optimization algorithm, while a practical energy consumption model is adopted. To handle the continuous and discrete solution spaces of topology shaping position and matching relationships, a hybrid Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Discrete Particle Swarm Optimization (DPSO) algorithm is introduced. This approach jointly optimizes the global energy consumption and standard deviation of flight distances, guiding the particle swarm updates to achieve multi-objective optimization. Our simulation results show that, in comparison to existing algorithms, the proposed method extends the working time of UAV swarm, reduces topology shaping time by 20%, and lowers the energy consumption of the most energy-demanding UAVs by 36.5%.

articleTitle: Beam Hopping and Power Allocation of LEO Multi-Satellite Communication Network Based on Multi-Agent DQN Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite communication systems have recently been considered the key point for achieving seamless coverage and high-speed Internet services, with beam hopping (BH) technology being one of the core to achieve this goal. However, the rapid movement of LEO satellites results in regional and time-varying traffic demands. How to meet the time-varying and differentiated needs of ground users with limited beam resources efficientlty is a critical issue that current LEO satellite communication systems face. Additionally, overlapping coverage areas among multiple LEO satellites often lead to significant intra-band interference due to the full-frequency reuse bandwidth allocation scheme commonly used in existing LEO communication systems. This paper proposes a multi-agent Deep Q Network (DQN) deep reinforcement learning algorithm based on interference avoidance, where each agent is responsible for only beam illumination or power allocation of a single beam. The agents collaborate by sharing global states and rewards to schedule beam resources while decreasing beam-to-beam interference. Simulation results indicate that the proposed method outperforms traditional BH algorithm by effectively increasing system throughput under interference isolation.

articleTitle: Earthquake Emergency Material Demand Prediction Based on SSA-BP Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Earthquake disasters occur frequently around the world and are extremely destructive. If the demand for emergency materials after an earthquake disaster can be accurately predicted, it will be significant for post-disaster rescue and reconstruction. This paper proposes a model for predicting the demand for emergency materials based on a back propagation neural network (BP). It optimizes the model using a swarm optimization method, the sparrow search algorithm (SSA). The SSA algorithm optimizes the weights and thresholds of the BP neural network by simulating the foraging and anti-predation behaviors of sparrows, thereby improving the accuracy and stability of the prediction model. In the experiment, the SSA-BP algorithm was verified using real earthquake disaster data, and compared with traditional BP neural networks and other common optimization algorithms such as particle swarm optimization (PSO) and genetic algorithm (GA). The results show that the SSA-BP algorithm is superior to traditional BP neural networks, PSO-BP, and GA-BP neural networks in terms of prediction accuracy and convergence speed. The SSA-BP model can quickly and accurately predict the number of casualties after an earthquake disaster, thereby indirectly estimating the demand for emergency materials in combination with the safety stock theory. The research results provide an effective decision support tool for earthquake disaster emergency management, which helps to improve the efficiency of rescue resource allocation and post-disaster recovery.

articleTitle: Data-Driven Highway Traffic Flow Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Aiming at the important problem of highway traffic flow analysis, this paper proposes a solution based on electronic toll collection (ETC) transaction data. Firstly, the data-driven elements including toll booth and ETC gantry transaction data are designed. By building a data-driven traffic flow analysis architecture, the data acquisition system and statistical analysis platform are designed and implemented. The platform provides rich statistical dimensions and visualization functions, and users can flexibly query and analyze traffic flow data in different time periods and regions. The backend adopts a microservice architecture to improve the maintainability and scalability of the system. Finally, through a specific case study, it is demonstrated how to use the platform to analyze highway traffic flow. Through the analysis of traffic flow change trends, traffic flow characteristics, and other aspects, it can provide a scientific decision-making basis for traffic management departments.

articleTitle: Hybrid Time-Triggered and Event-Triggered Flow Scheduling for Time-Sensitive Networking (TSN)
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Time-sensitive Networking (TSN) is an emerging technology that aims to solve the problem of precise network latency control in next generation industrial networks. In addition to conventional best-effort flows, TSN needs to deliver time critical flows, which are of high-priority. To ensure deterministic latency for time-critical flows, various scheduling models have been developed. However, those models are primarily designed for time-triggered (TT) critical flows, which are predictable and periodic. In realistic industrial scenarios, often there exist event-triggered (ET) critical flows, which are bursty and may have higher priority than time-triggered flows. In this paper, we design an enhanced TACQ model to meet the requirements of managing event-triggered flows, without affecting the deterministic transmission of time-triggered flows. On top of this model, we propose a corresponding event-triggered flows scheduling algorithm. Furthermore, to reduce the computation time of time-triggered flows scheduling, we propose a weighted sorting algorithm based on path optimization (WSPO). Simulations are conducted to evaluate the performance of our model and algorithms. Compared to traditional models and algorithms, the proposed methods can better handle hybrid critical flows.

articleTitle: A Microwave Oven Dish Recommendation System Based on Multi-Perspective Dialogue-Recommended Dual-Stream Contrast Fusion
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: When people are uncertain about choosing micro-wave oven dishes, an effective recommendation system with high commercial value is essential. However, existing systems typically provide recommendations from a single perspective based on users' historical data, which limits their ability to fully understand users' real needs and preferences for different items. To address this, we propose Dual-MDR, a microwave oven dish recommendation system based on Multi-perspective Dialogue-Recommended Dual-stream contrastive fusion. Dual-MDR integrates recommendation and dialogue modules, utilizing a Multi-perspective Dual-stream contrastive Fusion (MDF) strategy to improve recommendation accuracy. In the recommendation module, we introduce an Attention-based Latent Factor Model (LFMAtt) to distinguish users' preferences for different dishes and deliver more accurate recommendations. In the dialogue module, we incorporate the MSIM-SOG model to capture users' individual needs. The MDF strategy fuses users' specific preferences with their historical data through multi-perspective dual-stream information integration. Additionally, contrastive learning is employed to enhance accuracy. Through extensive experiments and real-world deployments, we evaluated the system's performance. Feedback from 257 users shows an impressive 87.16<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> satisfaction rate, demonstrating its practical value and strong user acceptance for continued use.

articleTitle: Machine Learning-Powered Anomaly Detection in Wireless Sensor Networks: A Survey
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: This survey provides a comprehensive review of machine learning-based anomaly detection methods in wireless sensor networks (WSNs). WSNs are integral in various applications, ranging from military surveillance to environmental monitoring, but their open nature makes them vulnerable to security threats. Traditional rule-based anomaly detection methods often fail due to the high-dimensional and dynamic nature of WSN data. Machine learning techniques, including supervised and unsupervised learning, offer promising solutions by automatically learning from data to detect anomalies. This paper reviews the state-of-the-art in machine learning for WSN anomaly detection, discusses the strengths and limitations of different methods, and highlights the challenges of implementing these systems in resource-constrained environments.

articleTitle: Quantifying the Effect of Path Stability on Multi-Path Routing in Cognitive Radio Ad Hoc Networks: A Markov Predictor Perspective
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Mobility generally may lead to the continual loss of data and link interruptions during the communications between secondary users (SUs) in distributed underlay cognitive radio ad hoc networks (CRANETs), which raises important concerns about the stability for routing design and maintenance. In this paper, we investigate the effect of path stability on multi-path routing in distributed underlay CRANET scenario. We firstly model the stability factor of the initial state of each path as the product of the stability coupling factor of the sorted link on this path. Then, we obtain the predicted stability of each path by using the risk level of link based on a second-order Markov predictor by taking into account the relative movement direction of SUs in the proposed Markov model. Particularly, we characterize the overall stability of each path on the basis of the predicted stability of this considered path. Moreover, an effective algorithm is presented to calculate the route stability of the path with the help of the Markov predictor. We also investigate the selection problem of the optimal path through the proposed optimal path selection algorithm. Numerical results are presented to demonstrate the effectiveness and practicality of our proposed algorithm, which achieves the evaluation of the overall stability for multi-path routing.

articleTitle: Joint Source-Channel Coding for Image Semantic Communications: A Parallel Processing Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Semantic communication is the focus of sixth generation (6G) wireless communication systems, emphasizing the efficient extraction and transmission of semantic information. However, existing image semantic communication systems face challenges in robustly recovering semantic content and mitigating channel noise. To this end, we propose a module based on a parallel processing approach, called STC, which uses feature segmentation to feed semantic information into the CNN and Transformer respectively in parallel. Through this approach, the local information extraction capability of CNN and the non-local information extraction capability of Transformer are efficiently combined, and an improved channel attention mechanism is introduced to incorporate the channel state information into the model training to reduce the unfavorable impact of the channel. Based on STC module, we propose a novel joint source channel coding (JSCC) model. The designed JSCC model improves gradient flow and information exchange through the hierarchical integration of STC and residual blocks. Compared with existing state-of-the-art models and traditional separated source-channel coding schemes, the proposed JSCC model demonstrates superior performance across datasets of varying resolutions.

articleTitle: Scene Graph Generation Based on Depth Information and Feature Enhancement
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: The objective of scene graph generation is to structure complex visual scenes into easily comprehensible graphical representations that facilitate a range of downstream visual tasks. However, existing work still exhibits the following shortcomings: firstly, an exclusive focus on the visual and semantic features of objects, with no consideration of depth information, which is also crucial for relationship prediction; secondly, the fusion of diverse modal features results in an excess of redundant object features and a lack of expressiveness; and lastly, there is a failure to mine contextual information between relationship pairs. In light of the aforementioned shortcomings, this paper proposes a scene graph generation method based on depth information and feature enhancement. This method enriches the depth geometric information of the object by mining depth features through the depth image and optimises the feature fusion process by using the Mamba algorithm, which removes the redundant information in multimodal features, enhancing their expressiveness. Additionally, a relationship pair feature enhancement method is proposed, which employs the Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM) to finely enhance the features of relationship pairs, providing a richer input for subsequent relationship inference. The efficacy of the proposed method was demonstrated through experimental validation on the Visual Genome (VG) dataset, wherein our method exhibited enhanced performance in the evaluation metrics of mR@20, mR@50, and mR@100. This evidence substantiates the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed method. The research presented in this paper not only advances the development of scene graph generation but also offers novel insights that can inform research in related fields.

articleTitle: Graph Attention Autoencoder Aided Unsupervised Community Detection for Relieving Alert Fatigue
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Intrusion detection system (IDS) is a security tool specifically designed to monitor and analyze network traffic to detect potential intrusions and attacks. However, due to volatile network traffic and imperfect rule signatures, IDS often generates high false positives, which overwhelms security analysts and reduces their efficiency. Therefore, reducing the false positives rate is critical to improving IDS performance. Traditionally, most of the methods for false alert rate reduction are based on supervised learning, but the effort of manually labeling alert data for large-scale network traffic datasets is really huge and costly. Therefore, unsupervised learning methods are potentially attractive in reducing the false alert rate because they do not require pre-labeled data. In this paper, we propose a novel framework GCRAF, an unsupervised approach designed to distinguish between normal alerts and false alerts. We introduce a community detection algorithm based on attribute network embedding considering topology and attribute information of attack nodes. In order to verify the validity of the proposed framework, we use two well-known datasets along with Snort as an intrusion detection system. The final results indicate that the GCRAF achieves satisfactory effectiveness and feasibility in eliminating false positives.

articleTitle: CL-MIL: Multi-Instance Learning on Whole-Slide Images with Self-Supervised Contrastive Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Histopathological examination of tissue slides is considered the gold standard for clinical cancer diagnosis. However, it heavily relies on pathologists' subjective judgment and involves substantial workload. Existing convolutional neural network (CNN)-based whole slide image (WSI) diagnostic methods suffer from high annotation costs and complex data acquisition processes. Therefore, this study proposes a weakly supervised multiple instance learning method based on self-supervised contrastive learning (CL-MIL) for WSI classification. By integrating self-supervised contrastive learning strategies, leveraging data augmentation through H&E stain separation, and introducing causal intervention via backdoor adjustment to mitigate dataset bias, our approach significantly enhances feature representation and classification performance in pathological images. Experimental results on the Camelyon16 and TCGA lung cancer datasets demonstrate that our method outperforms other comparable WSI classification models across various evaluation metrics, achieving higher diagnostic efficiency and accuracy. Additionally, our method exhibits good interpretability, enabling precise localization of pathological regions and providing robust technical support for clinical applications.

articleTitle: Sensing-Aided Channel Estimation in OTFS-ISAC Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Orthogonal time frequency space (OTFS) modulation has been considered as a promising waveform for the future sixth-generation (6G) communication. However, there exists fractional Doppler in practical scenarios, which leads to performance degradation of channel estimation. In this paper, a scheme which utilizes the sensing echoes from downlink signals is proposed to ensure the accuracy of uplink channel estimation. Specifically, we design a novel block-superimposed pilot scheme and a corresponding modified orthogonal matching pursuit (OMP) algorithm with low complexity. Furthermore, an iterative method which eliminates mutual interference between pilots and data is developed for accurate channel estimation. Simulation results show the necessity of considering fractional Doppler for OTFS communication, and our sensing-aided scheme outperforms that using only pilots for fractional Doppler channel estimation in terms of normalized mean square error (NMSE) and bit error rate (BER).

articleTitle: The Research and Implementation of NAS Signaling Decryption for 5G-R
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In network construction and operation, signaling monitoring is a crucial means of troubleshooting network issues and maintaining network stability. Given the extensive application of encryption algorithms in the 5th Generation Mobile Communication-Railways (5G-R), NAS signaling and data are processed with encryption, presenting certain challenges for signaling monitoring. Consequently, studying the testing and verification of NAS signaling encryption and decryption process becomes extremely important for signaling monitoring. At present, research on NAS signaling decryption for 5G-R remains unexplored. Therefore, this paper focuses on the encryption and decryption processes of NAS signaling during terminal access, designing a corresponding decryption and integrity verification scheme, and developing a decryption tool to address challenges such as as key acquisition and derivation, key updates during handover, and the association of signaling with terminals in multi-terminal access scenarios. By fully utilizing the laboratory network management system and the signaling capture and decoding capabilities of Wireshark, successful decryption testing and verification of NAS encrypted messages have been achieved. The final experimental results strongly demonstrate the feasibility of this scheme, enabling effective network state monitoring and analysis of the 5G-R communication system.

articleTitle: Spectrum Resource Allocation for Large-Scale UAV Clusters in Complex Electromagnetic Environments: An Improved Deep Reinforcement Learning Method
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: This paper proposes a spectrum resource allocation method based on distributional reinforcement learning (C51-SRAA) to optimize spectrum resource allocation for large-scale UAV swarms. It achieves joint allocation in both frequency and power domains to maximize spectrum resource utilization. Firstly, the method addresses dynamic communication traffic changes between ground stations and UAV clusters through an adaptive spectrum allocation scheme, enabling dynamic spectrum access and transmission power adjustment, significantly enhancing communication efficiency. Secondly, by representing the value of each action as a probability distribution rather than a single value, the method captures more comprehensive policy information, improving adaptability to environmental changes. Additionally, the method employs a loss function based on Kullback-Leibler divergence to enhance the learning capability of Q-value distributions, overcoming the limitations of traditional mean squared error (MSE) in handling probability distributions. The research results demonstrate the algorithm's superiority in spectrum resource utilization and communication delay.

articleTitle: Communication-Efficient Personalized Federated Learning for Traffic Flow Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: As an important component of intelligent transportation systems, accurate traffic flow prediction can improve road traffic efficiency. Traffic data is typically represented as graphs, but data from different regions is independently collected by various organizations (clients), resulting in the division of the complete graph structure into multiple subgraphs. Feder-ated learning enables the collaborative use of these independent datasets. However, limited communication bandwidth and computational resources result in high overhead in practical scenarios, hindering the application of federated learning. To address this, we introduce an efficient pruning-based federated learning algorithm (DPruneFL), which analyzes client differences and retains personalized model parts. Additionally, we developed the FedNe-DP system by integrating this with the personalized federated learning algorithm based on neighbor aggregation (FedNe), considering both the physical relationships among subgraph data and client personalization needs during aggregation. Experimental results on real datasets show that our approach not only improves prediction performance but also reduces communication costs, enhancing the efficiency of federated learning in actual traffic flow prediction.

articleTitle: A Practical Byzantine Fault Tolerance Algorithm Based on Reputation Scoring Mechanism and Dynamic Timeout Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Addressing the issues of random primary node selection, vulnerability to delay attacks, and sensitivity to network latency inherent in Practical Byzantine Fault Tolerance (PBFT), this paper proposes a Practical Byzantine Fault Tolerance Algorithm Based on Reputation scoring Mechanism and dynamic Timeout Mechanism algorithm (RT-PBFT). RT-PBFT, initiates by assigning reputation scores to nodes based on metrics including network stability, historical behavior, and contribution level, thereby quantifying node reliability. High-reputation nodes are then selected as primary nodes during view changes. Built upon the reputation scoring mechanism, RT-PBFT incorporates a dynamic timeout mechanism that allocates additional timeout periods to nodes dynamically based on their reputation scores. This design safeguards well-performing nodes from losing their primary status due to minor network fluctuations, reducing the consensus system's sensitivity to network delays. Simultaneously, nodes with lower reputation scores are allotted shorter timeouts, facilitating quicker view changes to replace nodes and evade delay attacks. The RT-PBFT algorithm, realized through these mechanisms, not only optimizes primary node selection but also mitigates delay attacks, tolerating delays for high-reputation nodes while promptly detecting faults in low-reputation ones. Experimental validation demonstrates that compared to PBFT, RT-PBFT significantly improves performance, marked by reduced consensus latency, communication overhead, and increased throughput under network volatility. These enhancements are pivotal for constructing large-scale, high-performance consortium blockchain systems, fulfilling the efficiency and security demands of scenarios such as Industrial IoT, finance, and supply chain management.

articleTitle: TS-PTLM: Enhancing General Time Series Analysis with Pre-Trained Language Models
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Pre-trained language models (PTLMs) have demonstrated adaptability to a wide range of natural language processing (NLP) tasks through methods such as prompting and fine-tuning. However, significant challenges persist in applying these models to time series analysis, largely due to the limited availability of time series data. As a result, the prevailing methodology often relies on the development of specialized models for specific tasks (e.g., forecasting, anomaly detection), which constrains the generalization capabilities of these models. Additionally, there are inherent differences between textual sequences and time series data. Directly inputting time series data into PTLMs frequently leads to suboptimal performance. To address these challenges, we propose a novel model, TS-PTLM, designed for time series analysis, capable of handling long-term forecasting, short-term forecasting, and anomaly detection. TS-PTLM employs a cross-modal knowledge transfer strategy to align textual sequences with time series data, leveraging both static and dynamic knowledge embedded in PTLMs to improve performance and generalization. Furthermore, the model incorporates frequency and temporal information from the time series data, with specialized adapters for fine-tuning, which further enhances its predictive accuracy. The effectiveness of TS-PTLM is demonstrated through extensive experiments conducted across three distinct time series tasks.

articleTitle: Joint Optimization of Node Selection and Resource Allocation for Sharded Blockchain
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: To enhance the scalability of sharded blockchain, we propose a joint optimization scheme for node selection and resource allocation. For transactions with varying computational demands, we use queuing theory to analyze the computation and sojourn time of transaction verifications. Based on this analysis, we construct an optimization model to maximize throughput and minimize latency, where the discrete node allocation and continuous resource allocation are separated and iterated using the Benders decomposition technique. These are further solved using the successive approximation approach and the branch-and-bound algorithm, respectively. Simulations show that the proposed scheme can significantly improve the throughput and reduce the latency of the blockchain system.

articleTitle: Covert Communication Against UAV Surveillance via Integrated Sensing and Communication System
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: This paper proposes a covert transmission scheme assisted by the integrated sensing and communication technique against the surveillance of a mobile unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV). Specifically, the transmitter attempts to transmit covert information to the legitimate receiver, while disturbing the detection of the warden UAV by sending artificial noise (AN). By utilizing the reflected AN, we track the UAV's position and velocity using the extended Kalman filter. To maximize the covert rate, we jointly design the beamforming vectors of AN and covert information signal while considering constraints on covertness, tracking mean squared error (MSE), and transmit power. Then, we solve the beamforming design problem by using the semidefinite relaxation and the Charnes-Cooper transform. Numerical results show that our proposed scheme can efficiently enhance the covert rate in comparison with the baseline schemes, demonstrating the superiority of integrating sensing into covert communications. Furthermore, we reveal the impacts of the covert coefficient and the maximum tracking MSE on the covert rate.

articleTitle: Response Time Analysis for Real-Time DAG Tasks Under Partitioned Scheduling
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Parallel task systems with real-time constraints are widely applied in various fields. Response time analysis is a necessary condition for online admission of applications in dynamic systems. This article focuses on the worst-case response time (WCRT) analysis of directed acyclic graph (DAG) tasks on multiprocessors under partitioned scheduling. We propose a new WCRT analysis algorithm, named the radiative-extended structure analysis (RESA) algorithm. We demonstrate that an-alyzing the radiative-extended structure (Res) helps to obtain more accurate analysis results. Compared with state-of-the-art algorithms, RESA achieves tighter upper bounds on self-interference and high-priority interference without increasing time and space complexity. RESA performs better by comparing the average response time observed in simulation experiments.

articleTitle: Towards Smarter Cities: An Adaptive AIoT Solution with Dynamic Sensor Group Selection for Real-Time Traffic Monitoring and Energy Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Efficient traffic monitoring and safety in smart cities demand real-time adaptability and energy-efficient operations. Static sensor configurations fall short in dynamic urban environments, leading to excessive energy use and delayed response times. This paper presents an adaptive Artificial Intelligence of Things (AIoT) framework with dynamic sensor group selection for intelligent traffic safety. Our system employs a context-aware sensor selection algorithm that activates only the most relevant sensors based on real-time conditions, including weather, traffic density, and time of day, thereby reducing unnecessary sensor usage and conserving energy. The framework's incorporation of weighted sensor prioritization and dynamic activation probabilities enhances its adaptability, achieving significant energy savings and accuracy improvements in real-time traffic monitoring scenarios. Energy management layer incorporates that dynamically adjusts power allocation and employs duty cycling to prioritize critical sensors while minimizing energy consumption. To address latency requirements, we leverage edge computing and vehicle-to-vehicle (V2V) communication, processing critical data locally and transmitting urgent alerts directly between vehicles. Additionally, low-latency communication protocols enable efficient data transfer for non-critical information to central servers. Experimental evaluations show that the proposed adaptive AIoT system reduces energy consumption by up to 30% and improves response times by 70% compared to non-adaptive configurations. These results demonstrate the potential of adaptive AIoT with dynamic sensor group selection to enhance urban traffic safety, providing a scalable, responsive solution for real-time smart city applications.

articleTitle: End-to-End Surface Roughness Prediction Method Driven by Multi-Source Information Fusion
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: To address the limitations of traditional data-driven surface roughness prediction approaches that rely on a single information source and require manual feature engineering, a deep learning-based surface roughness prediction model was proposed. The model used static processing parameters and raw signals from multi-sensors as inputs. Parallel convolutional neural networks were employed to extract multi-scale features from the signals, and a hybrid attention mechanism was introduced for feature enhancement to improve prediction accuracy. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method which integrates multi-source sensor signals may predict surface roughness effectively, outperforming other methods which are based on a single sensor signal or traditional machine learning models. It provides an effective approach to predict the surface quality of products in intelligent manufacturing rapidly and accurately.

articleTitle: Fusion of Transformer and Spatio-Temporal Graph Convolutional Networks in Grid Equipment Fault Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Grid equipment plays a crucial role in maintaining a stable power supply, and fault prediction is essential to guarantee the reliability of the power system. Traditional fault prediction methods are difficult to cope with the complex spatial and temporal dependencies in the operation of power grid equipment, and thus have limitations in terms of accuracy and applicability. To overcome these challenges, this paper proposes a novel hybrid model combining Transformer and Spatio-Temporal Graph Convolutional Networks (STGCN). The STGCN module is able to efficiently capture spatial dependencies among grid components, while the Transformer module is able to learn long-term temporal dependencies in equipment operation. This approach leverages the strengths of both models through a feature fusion strategy, resulting in more accurate fault prediction. We validate the effectiveness of the proposed model in several experiments, and the results show that the hybrid model significantly improves the prediction accuracy, robustness, and ability to handle complex time series compared to the traditional deep learning model. In addition, this study analyses the contribution of each module to the overall performance through ablation experiments, demonstrating the complementary nature of spatial and temporal modelling. The method demonstrates a wide range of applicability when dealing with fault prediction of power grid equipment, and can provide strong support for the efficient operation of smart grids.

articleTitle: CT-PBFT: A Comprehensive Trust-Based Practical Byzantine Consensus Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Blockchain technology has become a foundational component for constructing decentralized, secure, and immutable distributed systems. The consensus mechanism ensures that all nodes in a blockchain network reach agreement on a single version of truth, thereby maintaining data consistency across the distributed ledger. The earliest blockchain application, Bitcoin, adopts Proof of Work (PoW), which provides high security at the cost of substantial computational power and energy consumption. Ethereum employs Proof of Stake (PoS) to reduce energy consumption, though it introduces new challenges in the fairness of node selection. Practical Byzantine Fault Tolerance (PBFT) has gained significant attention for its ability to achieve more efficient consensus by reducing computational and energy demands. However, traditional PBFT still requires extensive message exchanges and voting among nodes, leading to significant communication overhead in large-scale networks. To address these limitations and further enhance the performance of PBFT, we propose the Comprehensive Trust-based PBFT (CTPBFT) algorithm. CT-PBFT reduces communication overhead by excluding nodes with low trust scores from the consensus process, thereby optimizing overall efficiency. We conducted a thorough analysis and simulation of CT-PBFT, and the results demonstrate that CT-PBFT outperforms traditional PBFT in terms of consensus latency and throughput. Moreover, CT-PBFT is more effective than other trust-based PBFT variants in swiftly eliminating Byzantine nodes, providing a robust and efficient solution for secure communication in distributed systems.

articleTitle: Lattice Based Double-Layer Traceable Aggregate Signature Scheme for Smart Grid
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Smart grid is characterized by complex network structures, decentralized deployment of terminal devices, and huge data processing demands. These place higher requirements on grid data collection and processing efficiency, and need to solve the difficult problem of tracing grid faults. Furthermore, the existing signature schemes fail to provide adequate security against quantum computing attacks. Signature aggregation technology, with its advantages of reducing signature storage overhead and improving verification efficiency, is well-suited for multi-terminal and high-data-volume scenarios in the smart grid. In this paper, we propose a lattice based double-layer traceable aggregate signature (DT-LAS) scheme by introducing an anonymous identity mechanism and ordered aggregate signature technology. DT -LAS enables efficient data aggregation at the edge layer of the smart grid, allows rapid fault node tracing, and safeguards the identities of terminal devices. Theoretical analysis and simulation experiments demonstrate that DT-LAS not only ensures correctness, unforgeability, and quantum-resistant security but also enhances aggregate signature efficiency and enables the tracing of faulty base stations, thus ensuring the safe and efficient operation of the smart grid.

articleTitle: Blind Classification of Linear Block Codes Based on Multi-Dimensional Features
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Linear Block Codes (LBCs) classification is a critical component of non-cooperative communication. Existing researches mainly rely on semi-blind classification techniques based on predefined candidate sets, while few research directed towards blind classification of new scheme LBCs widely used in modern communication systems. Therefore, this paper concentrates on classifying new scheme LBCs, including Polar code, Low Density Parity Check (LDPC) code, Bose-Chaudhuri-Hocquenghem (BCH) code, and Reed-Solomon (RS) code. Addressing the existing issues, this paper proposes an innovative method to classify key LBCs types based on multi-dimensional codeword features. To achieve better classification of new scheme LBCs types in error scenarios, a classification method based on multi-dimensional codeword features is proposed. This method utilizes four key features, including code length, frozen bits feature of Polar code, sparse parity check matrix feature of LDPC, and Galois Field Fourier Transform (GFFT) spectrum of RS and BCH codes. And the proposed method is not limited to the specific candidate sets. The experimental results have verified the effectiveness and practicality of the proposed method.

articleTitle: FRCS: Congestion Control in Datacenter Networks Based on Fair Rate Calculation by Switches
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Remote Direct Memory Access (RDMA) has been widely deployed in data centers to further reduce latency and CPU overhead. The line rate in data center networks (DCNs) is gradually growing from 40Gbps to 100Gbps and beyond, and more and more flows will be completed in a single round-trip time (RTT). Traditional congestion control mechanism cannot accurately regulate different flow transmission rates in such background, and it will produce an increase in the flow completion time (FCT) and a loss in throughput. In this paper, we propose FRCS, a congestion control algorithm based on direct fair rate computation that enables fast convergence and switch queue emptying. FRCS can also address the victim flow problem during multiple congestion points. To achieve this goal, FRCS adopts different control methods according to the lengths of flows, calculates the flow fair rate using programmable switches, and passes the information back to the sender via ACK. Simulation results show that FRCS, compared to HPCC, not only achieves a lower FCTSlowdown but also reduces the average queue length at switches by more than 50%.

articleTitle: Robust Adaptive Beamforming Based on Low Complexity Interference Plus Noise Covariance Matrix Reconstruction
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: The algorithms based on interference-plus-noise covariance matrix (INCM) reconstruction are regarded as a burgeoning robust adaptive beamforming (RAB) technique in recent years. However, the majority of INCM algorithms prioritize performance in various error scenarios while neglecting the computational complexity of the methods. Consequently, this paper addresses both the robustness and computational efficiency of the INCM algorithm. First, the Capon algorithm is used to estimate the steering vector (SV) and the robust Capon beamforming (RCB) algorithm is used to correct the SV, which improves the anti-error ability of the algorithm. Then, the eigenvalue decomposition is used to obtain the interference and noise power, and the proposed algorithm simplifies the interference power estimation of INCM reconstruction by using the largest eigenvalue, which effectively reduces the computational complexity of the algorithm. Finally, the simulation results show that the proposed INCM algorithm has excellent resistance to different types of errors, taking into account both computational complexity and performance.

Author Keywords: interference and noise covariance matrix (INCM) reconstruction

articleTitle: Analysis on Influencing Factors of Vehicle-Road-Cloud Time Synchronization Accuracy
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
