abstract: Based on the scenario of internet of vehicles, this paper analyzes in detail different influencing factors of vehicle-road-cloud time synchronization accuracy, such as communication mode, communication delay, time synchronization protocol, time synchronization algorithm, vehicle speed and other factors. The experiments of time synchronization based on 5G tested in Xi'an, Shaanxi Province, and Yizhuang, Beijing, confirm the feasibility of time synchronization based on 5G, proving that the time synchronization based on 5G is more accurate than that based on WiFi. Thus, we also design a comprehensive timing scheme by integrating 5G with the vehicle-road-cloud scenario, which is suitable for different vehicle-road-cloud scenarios, and can meet the requirements of high reliability, low delay and deterministic communication in the vehicle-road-cloud scenario, make the network connection more reliable and have lower delay, improve the accuracy and reliability of time synchronization, and improve the management and maintenance capability of the network.

articleTitle: Algorithm for Workpiece Recognition Under Complex Conditions Based on Enhanced YOLOv8
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In response to the issue of poor object recognition accuracy in existing deep learning-based object detection algorithms due to factors such as changes in light intensity, complexity of image environment, and movement of capturing devices, the study introduces an enhanced YOLOv8 object detection algorithm. The proposed modification incorporates a Triplet Attention Mechanism module, enabling the model to engage with more comprehensive dimensional feature information. In an innovative approach, the conventional UpSample module is substituted with a DySample module, facilitating an increment in accuracy without imposing additional computational costs. Moreover, the integration of Adaptive Spatial Feature Fusion (ASFF) empowers the algorithm to autonomously select optimal feature combinations, while the introduction of the WIoU loss function further refines detection efficacy. Experimental results show that the improved YOLOv8 algorithm achieves a detection accuracy of 92.7% (mAP) on the T-LESS datasets, which is 2.6% higher than the baseline model. The algorithm achieves higher detection accuracy without sacrificing much detection speed, effectively balancing the accuracy and speed of the algorithm.

articleTitle: Security-Enhanced Data Sharing Model for Cloud-Edge Collaborative Network
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Cloud-edge collaborative network is a promising paradigm for data sharing in Internet of Things (IoT). However, data services of the cloud server and edge nodes are provided by interest-oriented third parties, making it crucial to protect user privacy while sharing data. There are two main problems with existing schemes. On the one hand, most schemes focus on solving a certain aspect of issues and lack overall guidance on secure data sharing. On the other hand, terminal devices in cloud-edge collaborative network are susceptible to physical attacks, which may lead to the failure of traditional security schemes. To address the above issues, we present a security-enhanced data sharing model for cloud-edge collaborative network, which considers the security threats faced by main processes in cloud-edge data sharing as a whole. This model integrates mutual authentication mechanism, multi-dimensional access control mechanism, and ciphertext retrieval mechanism, and designs a physically secure key management scheme based on physical unclonable function (PUF) to provide protection against physical attacks. The proposed model can macroscopically solve the security issues faced by cloud-edge data sharing, which provides theoretical support for subsequent research.

articleTitle: Data-Driven Analysis of Skeet Shooting Training: Multi-Modal Data Collection and Lake-Warehouse Unified Architecture Design
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: As times evolve and technology advances, the speed and scale of data generation have increased dramatically, giving rise to new technologies for big data processing and analysis. The Bidirectional Skeet Shooting Analysis Project aims to enhance the training levels of skeet shooters. Traditional training methods primarily rely on coaches' experiences and lack systematic data analysis. To address this issue, this paper applies big data technologies by comprehensively collecting data from athletes' training processes and constructing a data warehouse based on a lake-warehouse architecture. This approach assists coaches in accurately understanding each athlete's training status while providing analysis and visualization capabilities. It promotes the shift of skeet shooting training towards a data-driven direction, thereby enhancing training effectiveness and offering significant theoretical and practical references for improving traditional training methods in skeet shooting.

articleTitle: Robust and Low-Complexity Secure Beamforming for Distributed RIS-Aided mmWave Systems with Limited Feedback
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: This paper presents a robust and low-complexity beamforming design to enhance physical layer security in mmWave systems with distributed RIS under imperfect CSI. This design jointly optimizes feedback bit allocation with active and passive beamforming to adapt to varying channel conditions. To address this complex and non-convex optimization, we propose an alternating optimization algorithm that decouples the problem into subproblems, applying appropriate methods iteratively at each level to obtain the optimal solution. Simulations demonstrate the robustness of the proposed algorithm in mitigating the effects of imperfect CSI, providing improved security performance and resource efficiency compared to benchmarks, particularly with limited feedback bit resources or in challenging spatial conditions.

articleTitle: Sexual Harassment in Social Virtual Reality: A Systematic Review
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: This paper investigates the phenomenon of sexual harassment within social virtual reality environments, focusing on its impact on various demographic groups, including women, children and teenagers, and LGBTQIA+ individuals. Through a systematic review of existing literature and case studies, the analysis highlights the unique challenges posed by the immersive and embodied nature of social virtual reality, which can intensify the experience of sexual harassment compared to traditional online interactions. The findings emphasize the need for targeted interventions, enhanced platform governance, and user education to mitigate these risks. Key recommendations include the implementation of more intuitive reporting mechanisms, safety-focused design features, and clear community guidelines. The paper also outlines future research directions to address the evolving dynamics of sexual harassment in social virtual reality, aiming to foster safer and more supportive virtual environments.

articleTitle: Quantum Generative Adversarial Network Enhancement Method Based on Quantum Principal Component Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Quantum machine learning (QML) has attracted increasing attention due to its excellent performance on clas-sification and identification tasks. In quantum machine learning methods, quantum generative adversarial networks (QGANs) are an extension of classical generative adversarial networks in the field of quantum computing. However, current quan-tum generation techniques are limited by quantum computing resources, these techniques are only validated on small-scale datasets, and the images generated by QGANs are of lower quality. To improve the image quality generated by QGANs, we introduce a new method to construct latent spaces based on quantum principal component analysis, to ensure high-quality data output of QGANs. In addition, we employ a parameterized quantum circuit instead of a sub module of quantum principal component analysis (Quantum Phase Estimation) to reduce the circuit depths and the number of gates. Experimental results indicate that our new method, which utilizes the new latent space as the input for QGANs, outperforms the original QGAN in terms of performance metrics Frechet Inception Distance and Cosine similarity. Specifically, our method achieves a 20 % lower Frechet Inception Distance score and 9 % higher cosine similarity compared to the original QGAN.

articleTitle: Effective Secrecy Throughput Maximization for WPT Enabled IoT in the FBL Regime
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: The inherent broadcast nature of wireless communication makes data transmissions vulnerable to eavesdropping, creating a critical need to balance communication reliability with security. This balance is especially important for applications where secure and dependable data transfer is essential. In this work, we consider a wireless power transfer (WPT) activated Internet of Things (IoT) including a passive legitimate sensor Alice, power transmitter and packet receiver Bob, as well as an eavesdropper Eve. To effectively balance the trade-off between communication reliability between legitimate users and security against eavesdropping, we characterize the effective secrecy throughput (EST) based on the concept of leakage-failure probability (LFP), and formulate a EST maximization problem by jointly optimizing the blocklengths of the energy harvesting (EH) phase and the wireless information transfer (WIT) phase. Nevertheless, the formulated problem is nonconvex and highly coupled in its variables. To address this issue, we first reformulate the original problem via successive convex approximation (SCA) and subsequently decompose it into two subproblems. An effective suboptimal solution is finally obtained via the alternating optimization (AO) algorithm. Numerical results demonstrate the efficiency and optimality of our design, as well as the performance advantage in achieving high effective secrecy throughput.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of a High-Performance Baseband Receiver Cache and Time Synchronization for Satellite Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: This thesis proposes an FPGA-based cache optimization and time synchronization implementation scheme for the high-performance baseband receiver side of the satellite communication system. First, an efficient DDR read/write control module is designed to accurately schedule the data cache through a state machine to ensure that the receiver end achieves low latency and high throughput in data transmission. Second, in the time synchronization module, the starting position of OFDM symbols is initially determined by cyclic prefix detection. Then, the starting point of subframes is further accurately located using the Primary Synchronization Sequence (PSS) stored in the FPGA ROM. The time synchronization module gradually outputs the precise subframe start address through the control of the multi-stage state machine. It feeds it back to the DDR module to ensure the correctness of data transmission. Simulation and hardware test results show that the design achieves a good balance of performance, resource utilization, and power consumption and is suitable for real-time baseband signal processing in high-performance communication systems.

articleTitle: Integrated Communications and Positioning System with Low Probability of Interception and Anti-Jamming Waveform
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: localization and communications are two fundamental requirements for unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) clusters. However, in certain severe environments, the satellite positioning and navigation service is unavailable. Moreover, the information exchange among UAV nodes also faces the risk of eavesdropping and jamming. How to realize relative positioning as well as low probability of interception (LPI) and reliable communications is an urgent issue. Inspired by the above considerations, this paper proposes an integrated communications and positioning protocol with LPI and anti-jamming waveform. We design a flexible frame structure that exploits pilots and the following data symbols for distance measurement and degree of arrival estimation. The data symbols are specially processed via the weighted fractional Fourier 4 transform (WFRFT). Compared to the traditional spread spectrum frequency communication and positioning integration technologies, the WFRFT-based LPI method not only realizes high-precision positioning but also has better security performance. In this way, secure transmission in complex electromagnetic conditions can be achieved and physical layer security can be further improved. Simulation and analysis results show that the low interception communication and positioning integration technology based on an array antenna provides a more secure and accurate solution for wireless communication and positioning, showing considerable potential for development.

articleTitle: Multi-Modal Task-Oriented Secure Semantic Communication: A Hide-and-Deceive Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a multi-modal task-oriented secure semantic communication (SemCom) framework. In this framework, the base station (BS) jointly transmits the semantic information, i.e., semantic vectors of multi-modal data, to the user for multi-modal downstream task such as visual question answering (VQA). A powerful eavesdropper intends to complete the same multi-modal task by the eavesdropped semantic information and the stolen downstream task model. To degrade the task performance of the eavesdropper, an invertible neural network based hide-and-deceive (INN-HD) method is proposed. This method can deceive the eavesdropper by generating a dummy semantic information of one modality while hiding the original semantic information of that modality into another modality. However the user can extract the hidden semantic information by invertible neural network (INN) and complete task normally. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method can reduce the eavesdropper's downstream task performance by up to 100%, while maintaining 96% of the user's task performance compared to directly transmitting the original semantic vectors.

articleTitle: Integrating Adaptive Reference Vectors with Differential Evolution Algorithm for Multi-Objective Service Composition
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Multi-objective service composition is increasingly crucial in distributed system engineering, especially in optimizing quality-of-service (QoS) attributes. This approach seeks to identify Pareto-optimal solutions regarding QoS attributes in distributed systems. As service requests increase, finding all Pareto-optimal solutions becomes excessively time-consuming. Although existing methods that approximate the Pareto-optimal set are scalable, they still require substantial enhancements in effectiveness. To overcome this challenge, this paper aims to refine the reference vectors to more uniformly guide the solutions towards the true Pareto-optimal set. Consequently, we propose a novel multi-objective differential evolution algorithm designed to efficiently identify solutions that demonstrate both proximity to and diversity within the Pareto-optimal set. This algorithm utilizes a reference vector-based cascade search to gather essential nondominated compositions efficiently. Additionally, it features an adaptive reference vector mechanism specifically designed to address the complexities of intricate multi-objective optimization problems. The robustness and effectiveness of our proposed algorithm have been rigorously validated using a real-world dataset, demonstrating its capability to improve service composition in distributed systems.

articleTitle: Research on Topology Management Methods for Large-Scale Satellite Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: The paper addresses the challenges and requirements of topology management in large-scale satellite constellation networks. It first examines the limitations of existing methods, which often rely on centralized topology planning characterized by limited autonomy and an absence of resilience. To overcome these shortcomings, the paper introduces two novel approaches for satellite network topology management: a multi-master centralized method and a masterless distributed method. Both methods are designed to enhance system reliability and reduce inter-satellite transmission data volume. Also, the paper provides a detailed explanation of the implementation and characteristics of these methods, followed by an analysis of their engineering design and experimental validation. A comparison with the traditional onboard centralized topology construction approach demonstrates that the proposed methods not only meet the design specifications but also improve the autonomous operation and reliability of space networks while in orbit. These findings underscore the potential of the proposed methods to advance the field of satellite network topology construction.

articleTitle: Multi-Agent Collaboration for Autonomous Systems Based on Implicit Strategy Prediction and Prioritization
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Collaborative multi-agent systems (MAS) have the potential to greatly enhance task performance by enabling agents to learn and adapt through interaction. However, traditional methods often face inefficiencies, particularly when agents encounter similar tasks repeatedly. To address these challenges, we propose a novel multi-agent collaboration scheme (MACS) based on deep reinforcement learning (DRL), aimed at improving interaction efficiency and reducing redundant learning. The proposed framework integrates two main components: the Implicit Strategy Prediction Algorithm (ISPA) and the Optimized Experience Prioritization Algorithm (OEPA). ISPA focuses on predicting agents' underlying strategies through their actions, ensuring that experience learning remains both unique and relevant. OEPA then prioritizes strategies based on their effectiveness, guiding agents to rapidly adapt and learn in downstream tasks by leveraging optimized strategies from long-term exploration. The framework's efficacy is demonstrated through simulations across multiple environments, where it achieves faster task completion and enhanced learning efficiency compared to traditional approaches.

articleTitle: Method for Real-Time Abnormal State Detection of Non-Cooperative Air Targets Based on Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: We propose a deep learning-based method for real-time abnormal state detection of non-cooperative air targets. Regarding the abnormal state detection task as a sequence labeling machine learning problem, the proposed method designs a deep temporal assessment network (DTAN). Firstly, DTAN integrates the target's trajectories and surveillance images as multimodal input time sequences, and employs MLP and ResNet separately to extract trajectory features and pose features at each time step. Secondly, a Transformer Encoder is incorporated to derive long-term target state features, followed by a CRF layer for temporal propagation constraints across time steps. Finally, the target's state (abnormal or normal) of each time step is predicted in real-time by the network. Besides, PolyLoss was employed to improve the training process of DTAN. Simulation experiments demonstrates that the proposed method surpasses conventional methods in accuracy, as well as reducing false alarm rate and decreasing assessment delay.

articleTitle: A C-SLAM Method Based on Improved Lightweight Feature Extractor
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Collaborative Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (C-SLAM) is an important solution to the problem that traditional single-robot SLAM systems are unable to efficiently accomplish tasks in large scenes and complex environments. In this paper, a distributed collaborative C-SLAM framework based on an improved lightweight feature extractor is proposed. The framework enables multiple mobile robots to collaboratively connect their respective local maps to enhance shared global understanding while efficiently utilizing computational resources. The system incorporates a lightweight feature extractor that significantly reduces computational resources and increases inference speed. We evaluated the performance of the proposed framework using the KITTI dataset and EuRoc dataset, and the results show an improvement in feature extraction efficiency compared to traditional feature extraction methods.

articleTitle: Multi-Path Routing Algorithm for WSN in Shipyard Based on MADRL
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In shipyards, the transmission reliability and efficiency of wireless sensor networks are significantly affected by routing algorithms. Traditional routing algorithms are inefficient and prone to congestion. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a multi-path routing algorithm based on multi-agent deep reinforcement learning. The algorithm first designs the shortest multi-path routing strategy to enhance the flexibility of path selection; secondly, the stability of the algorithm is improved through the multi-agent deep reinforcement learning method. Through the evaluation of the network topology of an actual shipyard, the experimental results show that the proposed algorithm outperforms the existing benchmark methods in terms of stability and service quality, verifying its effectiveness and feasibility in practical applications.

articleTitle: Privacy Protection for Image Sensors Using Convolutional Neural Network and Generative Adversarial Nets
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: An image privacy information protection method that does not damage the original image quality is proposed considering the risk of privacy information leakage due to the widespread use of image sensors and image sharing in social platforms. A convolutional neural network is used to detect the privacy information of the image. A generative adversarial network is then employed for the detected privacy content to protect image privacy by transforming the privacy information into non-privacy information without damaging the original image quality. Numerous studies have been conducted on real-world images., and results prove the efficiency and effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: VLSI Parasitic Capacitance Extraction Based on Pattern Matching Using Modified Machine Learning Methods
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: The increasing complexity in the process of IC design and verification has made the rule-based methods widely used by layout parasitic extraction (LPE) tools meet more and more challenges in precision, due to the increasingly severe parasitic effects resulting from the rapid growth in chip integration especially for Very Large-Scale Integration (VLSI). Based on the machine learning algorithms, a new pattern segmentation and combination method is proposed and a corresponding pattern library is established, which is more suitable for the two automatic classification models developed in this research. Two kinds of machine learning networks are trained for experiments and comparisons. For the CNN model, the number of network parameters at different depths and the effect of training layer depth on classification accuracy are compared. For the KNN algorithm, fuzzy distance pre-processing is performed on samples, and a KD-Tree model is established to store and retrieve the “distance” of point pairs. The classification accuracy of models on different training datasets is analyzed. For the labeled pattern datasets, the KNN classification model achieved a better result; Performance improvement is required only in certain mirror patterns. For a set of patterns that are not explicitly classified, the model can potentially be adapted into an unsupervised method to assist in building a pattern library. This method possesses the potential benefit of simplifying the introduction of new processes, preventing the occurrence of pattern mismatch, and saving costs when the computing resource is limited.

articleTitle: An Improved YOLOv10 Model with Ghost Mode for Camouflage Detection in Complex Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: This paper focuses on the detection of camouflaged targets in complex environments. Given the complexity of combat scenarios and climates, this paper has developed a various weather, multi-scenario dataset for camouflage targets. To address the challenge of limited resources in complex environments, this paper proposes a lightweight network structure based on an improved Ghost mode in YOLOv10n. The main improvements are the CBS module and C2f module based on the Ghost convolution. Through comparative experiments with different networks, it validates the high accuracy of the proposed network in detecting camouflage target, while maintaining a low number of model parameters and computational requirements. The trained network is capable of effectively adapting to the constraints of limited resources in complex environments.

articleTitle: Cloud P2P Video Conferencing for Enterprise Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In recent years, video conferencing has been a popular internet application in social life, and it also has been an essential tool for enterprise off-site meeting activities. Existed studies are designed for public Internet scenarios, and they assume that the underlying network is fully connected. Participants in video conferencing for large enterprises are spread across a wide geographical area. Some participants are on the intranet, and some are on the Internet outside the intranet. For the sake of network security, communication between the intranet and the internet has to come through certain gateways. Therefore, the underlying network of enterprise video conferencing is not fully connected just as the Internet. For this reason, this paper proposes an Enterprise-Oriented Cloud P2P video conferencing approach, referred to as EOCP. EOCP rents servers in the data centers as relay transmission nodes and utilizes the Peer-to-Peer(P2P) transmission mechanism between these nodes to improve the resource utilization rate. EOCP jointly optimizes P2P organization of the Internet and intranet and the selection of gateways to improve the service quality of video conferencing under cost constraints. Specifically, in EOCP, we build a network resource optimization model for enterprise video conferencing. Furthermore, we design a heuristic algorithm to solve the above model. The experimental results show that EOCP can significantly enhance the quality of service(QoS) in comparison with other solutions. The performance of the designed heuristic algorithm is close to the solution result of the optimal algorithm, and the calculation time is shortened from approximately 2 hours required by the optimal model to around 10 seconds.

articleTitle: Service Continuity Guarantee for Coordinated Optimization of Offloading and Migration in LEO Satellite Computing Power Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Low earth orbit (LEO) satellite computing power networks have become an important field of next-generation communication and computing technology due to their global coverage and low-latency characteristics. However, due to the high-speed movement of satellites, LEO satellite computing power networks face challenges such as service interruptions and fluctuations in communication delays. Traditional methods mostly focus on the single strategy of computing offloading or service migration, which is difficult to adapt to the highly dynamic scenarios of LEO satellite computing power networks. To this end, this paper proposes a dynamic decision-making mechanism driven by the collaboration of computing offloading and service migration, models the service continuity guarantee problem as a nonlinear integer programming problem, and uses an artificial electric field algorithm to solve the net utility of the three schemes of computing offloading, service migration, and continued service of the original node, and dynamically adjusts the computing offloading and service migration strategies. The simulation results show that this scheme effectively guarantees the continuity of user services under the LEO satellite computing power networks while improving service utility.

articleTitle: A Buffer-Aided Cooperative NOMA Scheme with Improved Physical Layer Security
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: A novel buffer-aided cooperative non-orthogonal multiple access (C-NOMA) scheme with improved physical layer security (PLS) is proposed and its performance is analysed. Assuming that both source and relay transmissions are vulnerable to the eavesdropper, a randomize-and-forward relaying protocol is employed to degrade the eavesdropping rate. Considering a proactive jamming (PJ) scheme and targeting the maximization of the average secrecy rate (ASR), an optimization problem is formulated by jointly taking into account the buffer stability, the quality of service (QoS) guarantee and the energy constraint of the nodes. As this is a non-convex mixed-integer problem, a dynamic recursion algorithm based on Lagrange duality and variable discretization is proposed as a low complexity solution which requires a polynomial time. Performance evaluation results have shown that, as compared to other equivalent C-NOMA schemes which do not employ buffering or PJ, the proposed scheme achieves higher PLS performance. They have also shown that by increasing the power of PJ, further improvements of the ASR are possible.

articleTitle: Day-Ahead Spot Electricity Price Prediction Based on Hybrid Model
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: The spot electricity price is crucial for maintaining the supply-demand balance in the electricity market, and accurate electricity price prediction holds significant importance for electricity producers and large consumers. This article proposes a hybrid model based on FEDformer and LSTM, which utilizes the advantages of both to predict day-ahead spot electricity prices. FEDformer excels in capturing long-term dependencies, utilizing frequency domain analysis to extract long-term trends and seasonal features, which can more accurately model the long-term trend of electricity prices. LSTM can capture short-term dependencies in sequence data and is suitable for handling sudden fluctuations and short-term changes in electricity price data. We use real data from the electricity market of a certain province from 2020 to 2022 for model training and evaluation, which includes various factors that affect electricity prices, such as temperature, humidity, load, new energy, etc. We compared the model with other models and our own basic model, and the experimental results showed that the model outperformed other models in different evaluation indicators, providing a new method for predicting day-ahead spot electricity prices for participants in the electricity market.

articleTitle: Path Planning for RIS-Assisted UAV: Phase Shift, Scheduling and Trajectory Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces (RIS) dynamically adjust the phase shifts of their reflective elements to optimize signal transmission paths, making them highly applicable in modern Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) communication systems to enhance communication quality and overall system performance. However, effectively integrating a RIS with a UAV and jointly optimizing both the UAV trajectory and RIS phase shifts presents a significant research challenge. This paper proposes a path planning method for a RIS-assisted UAV (RIS-UAV) based on alternating optimization, with a focus on achieving both green communication and fair communication. The proposed approach first employs a combination of continuous convex approximation and fractional programming to jointly optimize scheduling variables and the UAV trajectory, taking into account UAV speed, acceleration, and position. Subsequently, a Riemannian gradient-based manifold optimization algorithm is applied for the iterative optimization of RIS phase shifts. Numerical results demonstrate the proposed algorithm's superiority in enhancing both communication fairness and system performance.

Index Terms: Speed Of The Unmanned Aerial Vehicles

articleTitle: An Enhanced iTransformer-Based Model for Electricity Load Forecasting
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: With the rapid rise of new energy technologies and electric vehicles, the volatility and uncertainty of electricity load have increasingly intensified, making electricity load forecasting more important than ever. However, existing load forecasting models often face certain limitations when dealing with complex time series data. To overcome this bottleneck, this paper proposes a novel electricity load forecasting model called FTFformer. This model effectively combines a meticulously designed Frequency Feature Extract Block (FFEB) with the encoder of iTransformer, enabling the model to excellently capture both frequency and temporal features of the time series, thereby improving prediction accuracy. Experimental results demonstrate that FTFformer performs exceptionally well on actual electricity load datasets, significantly surpassing the predictive accuracy of mainstream existing models. This achievement not only substantially enhances the accuracy and reliability of electricity load forecasting but also provides strong support for the efficiency and stability of power systems.

articleTitle: Secure Transmission Method in Dual-Polarized Satellite Communication Based on Constellation Distortion
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Polarization state modulation(PM) It is known that satellite communication signals are easy to eavesdrop and how to realize secure transmission is the key problem. This paper proposes a secure transmission scheme based on the polarized constellation rotation and the weighted fractional Fourier transform. Firstly, the pseudo-random sequence is used to process the phase of the two components of polarization signals to make them change randomly, and the constellation points will randomly rotate around the horizontal polarization axis in the Poincare sphere. Then two polarization signals are processed by WFRFT with different orders separately to further distort the polarization constellation. In this manner, the constellation points will be randomly distributed in, on and outside the sphere improve the transmission security. In addition, with the proposed, it is difficult for the eavesdropper to accurately recover the WFRFT parameters and when there are errors in the cracked WFRFT parameters, self-interferences occur in the recovered signals, which causes a decrease in the SNR of the signals received by the eavesdropper. In this way, it also obtains a positive secrecy capacity to ensure the transmission security. Finally, the performance of the proposed scheme is verified from three aspects: polarization constellation distortion, security capacity and the bit error rate performance.

articleTitle: SF-DQN: A Cloud-Edge Collaborative Online Task Offloading Framework Based on SwiftFormer and Reinforcement Learning in Industrial Scenarios
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: With the rapid advancement of artificial intelligence, big data, and Internet of Things technologies, the global manufacturing industry is swiftly transitioning toward digitization and intelligentization. The novel cloud-edge collaborative industrial interconnect computing architecture effectively addresses the limitations of centralized cloud processing and distributed edge computing. However, its multi-layered design introduces challenges for efficient task collaboration, making computation offloading research crucial for enhancing system efficiency and optimizing performance. Existing computation offloading strategies typically focus on single optimization objectives, exhibit pro-longed decision-making times in large-scale edge architectures, and only consider current environmental conditions, thus failing to meet the demands of dynamic environments. To tackle these challenges, this paper proposes SF-DQN, a deep reinforcement learning-based serial task offloading algorithm tailored for a three-tier cloud-edge-end architecture. The approach includes a lightweight bandwidth prediction model based on SwiftFormer to provide proactive support for dynamic offloading decisions, the construction of a comprehensive objective function that accounts for resource competition, task latency, energy consumption, quality of service assurance, and link conditions, and the application of the Deep Q-Network (DQN) algorithm to define state space, action space, and reward function suited for serial tasks, thereby determining the optimal offloading strategy. Simulation experiments validate that the proposed algorithm significantly outperforms existing methods in terms of latency, energy consumption, and system resource utilization, demonstrating its superior performance in large-scale cloud-edge collaborative environments.

articleTitle: MJSCHED: A Moldable Job Scheduling Algorithm in Heterogeneous Resource Environment
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Moldable jobs have the ability to dynamically adjust their resource requirements before execution, offering greater flexibility compared to rigid jobs that allocate fixed resources. Currently, most resource management systems do not fully consider the resource requirements of moldable jobs, and few scheduling algorithms address the scheduling of such jobs, especially those requiring both CPU and GPU resources. In this paper, we propose a moldable job backfill algorithm(MJSched) that dynamically adjusts job resource allocation to reduce turnaround time. First, a resource allocation strategy that minimizes turnaround time is applied to jobs at the head of the waiting queue. We utilize a greedy algorithm and a genetic algorithm to construct the set of backfill jobs, determine the computational nodes, and allocate the number of tasks for these jobs. Furthermore, a profit-first remaining resource scheduling strategy is proposed. We implement the Slurm scheduling plug-in based on our moldable job scheduling algorithm to support moldable job scheduling in heterogeneous resource environments. Simulation experiments demonstrate that our MJSched-GA algorithm effectively reduces both average job turnaround time and average job waiting time by 15.7%-22% and 18.8%-26.2% respectively, while improving cluster resource utilization by 8%-14 %.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Orthogonal Chirp Division Multiplexing System with Zero-Forcing Receiver over Multi-Path Fading Channels
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: With multi-path propagation, the transmitted signal experiences varying degrees of fading, which greatly impacts the current 4G/5G communication system based on orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) modulation. In recent years, the orthogonal chirp division multiplexing (OCDM) modulation has emerged as an attractive alternative to the OFDM due to its increased resistance to fading channel impairments. Although numerous studies have been done on OCDM communication systems recently, a comprehensive statistical analysis of the post-detection signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) with zero-forcing (ZF) receiver is still lacking. In this paper, we investigate the statistical properties of the received symbol SNR in a multi-path propagation environment for a point-to-point OCDM communication system. We first derive the SNR expression for the demodulated symbol using ZF receiver. Then we analyze the distribution of the SNR, demonstrating that it depends on the joint distribution of the eigenvalues of channel matrix. Following this, we provide a comprehensive derivation of the probability distribution function (PDF) of the SNR for both single-path and two-ray propagation environment. The so-derived PDFs are utilized to provide key insights into the OCDM system in terms of the bit error rate. Finally, the accuracy of our analytical results have been validated with Monte Carlo simulations.

articleTitle: Monitoring Forest Changes in Yunnan Province Using Landsat 8 and Random Forest on GEE
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Protecting and sustain ably utilizing forest resources is of paramount importance for systematically monitoring and analyzing changes in forest cover across Yunnan Province. In this study, we employed the random forest classifier on the Google Earth Engine (GEE) platform, utilizing Landsat 8 images to monitor and analyze forest changes in Yunnan Province from 2013 to 2023. The primary objectives of this research are to assess alterations in forest cover by employing Random Forest (RF) algorithms that incorporate multispectral features, topographic features, and textural characteristics. The findings of the study reveal the following: (1) The Random Forest (RF) algorithm outperforms the Support Vector Machine (SVM) algorithm with respect to forest mapping accuracy. The overall average accuracy of the forest cover classification stands at 87.94%, accompanied by a Kappa coefficient of 0.76.(2) Between 2013 and 2023, the total area covered by forests in Yunnan Province expanded from 228,876.74 km<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> to 233,238.57 km ”, indicating an approximate average growth rate of about 1.91 % over this ten-year period. The maj ority of these forests are located in southwestern and northwestern regions of Yunnan, characterized by robust vegetation coverage.(3) Alterations in forest area have significant implications for the water cycle as they influence transpiration rates which subsequently affect precipitation patterns. A reduction in forested areas results in decreased precipitation levels. Furthermore, variations in surface temperature impact evapotranspiration processes along with precipitation outcomes—changes that invariably influence both forestration growth and spatial distribution. This study provides a scientific foundation for effective management practices regarding forestry resources within Yunnan Province while also serving as a vital reference point for leveraging remote sensing technology aimed at ecological monitoring initiatives.

articleTitle: QSAFL: A Quality-Based Semi-Asynchronous Federated Learning Strategy
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Federated learning (FL) addresses high data upload costs and privacy issues of centralized machine learning by en-abling distributed model training, which is a hot topic in wireless communication. Among FL strategies, synchronous strategy is subject to the slowest client, and asynchronous strategy faces challenges in global model convergence. Semi-asynchronous FL strategy balances client idle time and global accuracy. However, non-independent and identically distributed (Non-lID) samples among clients further complicates model aggregation. This paper introduces Quality-Based Semi-Asynchronous Federated Learning (QSAFL), a strategy mitigating two common issues in FL within the field of wireless communication: straggler effect and global accuracy problem caused by Non-lID samples. In QSAFL, the client requests a server connection immediately after finishing training. If the server is idle, it connects; otherwise, the client waits. Once connected, clients upload their models, after that, the server aggregates global model and distributes it back. The server then disconnects and becomes idle, ready for new connections. In the meantime, sample size and uniformity of distribution, evaluated by Gini index, are used to weight the client local model during aggregation. This ensures high-quality models predominate, enhancing global accuracy. According to the experiment results, QSAFL can reduce the overall time by 80 % and decrease clients' idle time by 83 % to reach the target global accuracy in Non-lID samples compared with traditional FedAvg. Within the same time frame, QSAFL's global accuracy is 10% higher than that of FedAvg.

articleTitle: Joint Communication and Computing Resource Allocation for Cell-Free-Enabled MEC Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: This paper investigates a cell-free massive multiple-input multiple-output (CF-mMIMO)-enabled mobile edge computing (MEC) network, aiming at satisfying stringent quality-of-service (QoS) requirements of computation-intensive services. We design a partial offloading strategy, where users execute local computing and simultaneously perform task offloading through reliable cell-free links. A joint communication and computing resource allocation (JCCRA) problem is formulated to maximize the sum computational bits of the system. The optimization approach jointly optimizes the transmit power, the local computing frequency, as well as the time allocation for local computing and computing offloading of each user. To tackle the non-convex problem, we develop an iterative algorithm based on fractional programming (FP) theory and block coordinate ascent (BCA) method. The original objective function is first reformulated using FP technique, and then it is decomposed into multiple sub-problems by BCA method. For each sub-problem, we derive the optimal closed-form solutions by leveraging Lagrangian dual transform and Karush-KuhnTucker (KKT) conditions. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed scheme outperforms other benchmark schemes in terms of improving the sum computational bits.

Author Keywords: joint communication and computing resource allocation

articleTitle: MetaFETC: Adaptive Few-Shot Encrypted Traffic Classification with Meta-Learning for Diverse Encryption Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Encrypted Traffic Classification (ETC) plays a pivotal role in managing network traffic and ensuring network security. Existing solutions often rely on training on large-scale traffic datasets to achieve good performance. However, due to the diversity of encryption technologies and application scenarios in the real world, collecting and labeling sufficient data for each ETC scenario often becomes impractical. To address this problem, we propose a novel adaptive few-shot ETC model named MetaFETC. MetaFETC extracts protocol-agnostic packet length sequences from encrypted traffic sessions as the input to learn the universal traffic representation and utilizes multi-task learning and meta-learning strategies to quickly adapt to new unknown ETC tasks in evolving network environments with only a small amount of new labeled data. Specifically, we utilize Temporal Convolution Network (TCN) model to capture the dependencies within the packet length sequences, which is essential for understanding the complex patterns present in encrypted traffic. Moreover, we introduce a multi-task meta-learning module to learn the optimal model initialization parameters via non-target task data of other encrypted scenarios, which can facilitate generalization and transferability across novel diverse ETC tasks. Experimental results show that the classfication accuracy of MetaFETC improves 10% in unknown few-shot encrypted scenario compared to traditional transfer method.

articleTitle: Near-Field Beamforming for Extremely Large-Scale Antenna Array
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Extremely large-scale arrays is a vital technology for enhancing the capacity in wireless communications. The employment of extremely large-scale arrays makes the near-field propagation become dominant, where the achievable rate is decreased owing to beam mismatch. However, the integration of angle and distance information must be investigated in the near-field beam domain, due to the spherical nature of electromagnetic wave propagation. Thus, in this paper, we propose a beamforming algorithm to mitigate the beam mismatch. We derive the phase profile of extremely large-scale uniform planar array under the spherical wave assumption, and design the visibility region strategy to capture the non-stationarity characteristics of extremely large-scale antenna arrays. Numerical results validate that the proposed algorithm is robust against the beam misfocus effect and performs with a higher achievable transmission rate.

articleTitle: Multi-Task Terminal Radio Frequency Fingerprint Feature Extraction Framework Based on Shuffle Network
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In the process of extracting and identifying wireless radio frequency signal fingerprints, the hardware differences between devices of the same type are too small to extract sufficiently distinct and effective features. To address this issue, this paper proposes a multi-task terminal radio frequency finger-print feature extraction framework based on a shuffle network, called RFFRe (Radio Frequency Fingerprint Re-identification). This framework can effectively capture the set of features corresponding to the subtle hardware differences from radio frequency signals. The framework employs a ResNet network model, removing the traditional fully connected layer and using the deep network model solely as a feature extractor for radio frequency signals. Additionally, it incorporates a shuffle network to apply additional perturbations to the extracted features, enhancing feature variability. Further, it performs multi-task learning on the perturbed feature space, using metric learning and representation learning to extract the distribution characteristics of feature vectors in the feature space. This compactly clusters intra-class features while improving inter-class discriminability. This model can complete the device registration process with a single training session when new devices are added and achieve quick identification through simple feature similarity comparison during device access. Experimental results show that RFFRe achieves a recognition Rank-1 accuracy of 99.4% on devices of the same type with minimal hardware differences, outperforming similar solutions.

articleTitle: Optimizing Real-Time Emotion Recognition: A YOLO v.8 Deep Learning Solution for Facial Expression Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Identifying emotional states from facial expressions is challenging and requires advanced technology. This paper introduces a YOLO (you only look once) based-deep learning facial expression recognition model. This rapid and precise object detection method improves facial recognition. The project aims to comprehend face recognition principles by assessing Yolo v.5, Yolo v.8s (Small), and Yolo v.8m (Medium) based models' facial expression recognition. Moreover, evaluate system performance using accuracy, recall, F1-score, precision, and robustness; measures Yolo v.8m is precise and efficient. The model is practical due to its accuracy and efficiency across several criteria. Yolo v.5 is weaker to other models but accurately catches face emotions with 91% and 0.87 macro-average F1-score. At 93% accuracy and 0.86, Yolo v.8s has good recall, precision, and macroaverage F1-score. Yolo v.8m balanced F1-score and 98% accuracy make it the best of three models. Its balanced macro-average F1-score i.e., 0.88. Potentially revolutionary, the suggested approach offers a solid fix for practical problems where traditional approaches fall short.

articleTitle: Foreign Object in Coal Belt Conveyor Detection and Tracking Based on Improved YOLOv9 and Bytetrack
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Conveyor belt transporting coal is an important scene in coal mining and transport operations. Once foreign objects are mixed in the conveyor belt, it will lead to damage of the conveyor belt and cause safety accidents in serious cases. However, the current mainstream algorithms have problems such as poor real-time performance, low recognition rate, frequent ID switching, and poor occlusion resistance, etc. To address the above problems, this paper proposes a tracking method based on the improved YOLOv9 algorithm and Bytetrack algorithm. The CEDNet module for acquiring multi-scale features is added, and the information representation of the features is enhanced by changing the loss of the main branch during the training process, which accelerates the convergence speed of the model. For long sequential information in the foreign object tracking process, the Vim module was introduced in the data association section, which uses global context modelling and positional embedding to better track and predict missing trajectory segments. ID switching due to occlusions was reduced. On the Belt Coal Foreign Dody Detection and Tracking dataset, MOTA and IDF1 achieve recognition rates of 91.2% and 92.5%, respectively, both of which are improved by 2.9%. The algorithm proposed in this paper not only identifies foreign objects in the conveyor belt coal transport scenario, but also tracks foreign objects accurately and stably in the dense occlusion scenario. The algorithm can also be applied to vehicle and pedestrian detection and tracking.

articleTitle: Fuzz Testing of Stateful Network Protocols Based on Multi-Armed Bandit Variant
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: As the foundation of network communication, the security of network protocols cannot be ignored. Therefore, it is crucial to discover their vulnerabilities in time. Fuzzing, an efficient software vulnerability discovery technique, has been widely used in the industry due to its high efficiency and low false positives. In recent years, several fuzzers for stateful network protocols have been proposed. But they are faced with the following challenges: (1) when evaluating and selecting states, there is a tendency to rely on information from a single dimension, such as code coverage, which can lead to a failure to identify critical test states; (2) the lack of an effective state selection algorithm leads to the possibility that the fuzzer may spend a significant amount of time testing meaningless states, thus reducing the efficiency of testing; (3) seed selection and retention rely too much on code coverage, while ignoring other state information, making it difficult to select and retain high-quality seeds. In this paper, we propose a gray-box fuzzing method for stateful network protocols, which guides the fuzzing process based on the information of path coverage, state coverage, and number of state transitions. We also introduce the AR-SMAB model to guide the state selection process. We implemented our testing tool and compared it with other stateful fuzzers. Our experiments show that our tool is more effective in discovering paths, improving by approximately 10% to 15% compared to other tools. Our tool also can find more crashes, improving by approximately 30% to 35% compared to other tools. In addition, our tool is similar to AFLNET in terms of execution efficiency, ensuring an efficient performance.

articleTitle: Covert Communications in Spectrum-Sharing Networks with Multi-Antenna Transmitter
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Covert communication aims to enhance communication security by hiding the existence of communication transmission behavior from the warden. This paper investigates covert communications in spectrum-sharing networks with a multi-antenna covert transmitter. The covert optimization design is proposed to maximize the achievable covert rate by optimizing the beamforming vectors with the covertness constraint, and the zero-forcing design is proposed for comparison. The multi-antenna covert transmitter and the warden are assumed to have the imperfect channel state information of the detection links in accordance with practical scenarios. For the proposed designs, the closed-form expressions of the warden's approximate minimum detection error probability are derived. The results show that the covert beamforming design performs better than the zero-forcing design when the covert constraint is weak or when the transmitter can obtain precise channel state information estimation about the warden, which indicates that the covert beamforming design can take full advantage of the degrees of freedom from antennas.

articleTitle: A Lattice-Based Dynamic Group Authenticated Key Exchange Protocol
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Group Authenticated Key Exchange (GAKE) protocol can achieve authentication among multiple users within a group and facilitates the agreement on a consistent group key, which ensures the security of the transmission of data within the group. Society is entering the post-quantum era with the development of quantum computers, and traditional cryptographic algorithms used in existing group authenticated key exchange protocols may not be able to resist quantum attacks. Using the lattice-based key encapsulation mechanism Kyber, we have developed a post-quantum secure group key exchange protocol. The protocol incorporates dynamic joining and leaving phases for group users to ensure scalability, while also utilizing passwords for user authentication. Finally, we formally prove the security of the protocol and compare it with other lattice-based group authenticated key exchange protocols through simulation experiments, the results demonstrate that our protocol is more efficient.

articleTitle: A Spatio-Temporal Trajectory Segmentation Framework Considering Vessel Anomaly Behaviors
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: As global trade and maritime shipping continue to expand, there is a growing focus on the safety and efficiency of sea transportation. The Automatic Identification System (AIS) offers a wealth of data, laying a robust foundation for the thorough analysis of ship movements and behaviors. However, due to the complexity of vessel behaviour, traditional trajectory segmentation methods based on vessel behaviour often fail to fully account for abnormal behaviour, which to some extent limits the effectiveness of their analysis. We propose an AIS trajectory segmentation method based on spatio-temporal and geometric features that integrates abnormal vessel behaviour. Based on the behavior of vessels, the AIS track data was segmented. We constructed a two-stage strategy for extracting and classifying stopping points. Building on the preliminary segmentation, we developed a detection approach that employs a sliding time window to identify vessel anomalies, including loitering and turning behaviors. The validity of this method has been confirmed through the analysis of actual historical AIS data obtained from the western seaboard of the United States. The results show that the classification accuracy for stop segmentation is 0.97. In comparison to existing method, the loitering detection accuracy has been enhanced by 1%. Furthermore, following the preliminary segmentation, the accuracy of loitering detection is increased by 7%, with high accuracy for turning anomalies.

articleTitle: Optimisation of Bandwidth Allocation in Backscatter Communication Based on Stackelberg Game and Dual Pricing
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: The combination of cognitive radio and backscatter communication can effectively improve spectrum utilization. However, the coexistence of multiple backscatter devices in this network introduces competition among secondary users (SUs) in licensed bands due to spectrum sharing, which cannot be ignored. This paper examines the Stackelberg game to facilitate mutually beneficial transmissions between primary users (PUs) and SUs in an interweave cognitive backscatter network, proposing a dual-bandwidth pricing mechanism. Multiple SUs are assigned to distinct non-overlapping sub-channels, utilizing frequency division multiple access for spectrum sharing. In each sub-channel, each SU pays a bandwidth fee to the PU proportionate to the allocated bandwidth, reflecting the cost of bandwidth sharing. An optimization algorithm for resource allocation based on Stackelberg game theory is developed to maximize PU's band-width revenue while optimizing SU's throughput utility function, considering both PU's total bandwidth constraints and SU's individual bandwidth constraints. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed pricing mechanism effectively increases PU's revenue and improves SU's throughput performance and utility.

articleTitle: Unknown DGAs Detection Based on TextCNN and Autoencoder
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Botnets pose a significant threat to Internet information systems, leveraging Domain Generation Algorithm (DGA) for malicious activities such as denial-of-service, spam, and malware distribution. Current research of DGA in machine learning and deep learning has primarily focused on binary classification of known DGAs, resulting in reduced accuracy when confronted with unknown DGAs due to the increasing diversity of DGAs. This paper addresses this challenge by proposing a novel approach utilizing a domain-specific tokenizer and the TextCNN for multi-classification of known DGAs, augmented by Autoencoder (AE) and extreme value theory (EVT) for accurate identification of unknown DGAs. Our method builds upon the insight that AE reconstruction errors are typically higher for unknown DGAs compared to known ones. To further enhance precision, we introduce an EVT-based algorithm to estimate confidence probabilities for recognition outcomes. Our approach aims to accurately identify unknown DGAs in addition to performing multi-class classification of known DGAs using deep learning methods (TextCNN and Autoencoder). Experimental results on real-world DGA datasets suggest improvements in recognition accuracy compared to conventional baseline methods.

articleTitle: Lightweight Attention Graph Convolutional Network for Two-Person Interaction Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Currently, significant advancements have been made in the field of two-person interaction recognition. However, many contemporary methods rely on deep neural networks, resulting in longer runtime and higher computational resource requirements, which limits their practicality and adaptability in various application scenarios. To address these issues, we introduce the lightweight graph convolutional network (LGCN) and the lightweight spatio-temporal Transformer (LST Transformer), as well as propose the lightweight attention graph convolutional network (LAGCN). The LGCN incorporates sparse matrices, low-rank approximation, and weight-sharing techniques to reduce the parameter count and computational complexity. The LST Transformer uses average pooling and spatial partial self-attention to further enhance efficiency. These innovations allow our model to maintain a competitive accuracy while drastically reducing the number of parameters and computational load. We evaluate our model on the interaction subsets of the NTU-RGB+D and NTU-RGB+D 120 datasets, achieving the lowest parameter count and computational effort compared to advanced methods, while preserving high accuracy.

articleTitle: Hybrid Beamforming Design for Multi-Functional RIS-Aided mmWave MIMO Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: This paper delves into the hybrid beamforming problem in a millimeter-wave (mmWave) multiple-input multiple-output network aided by a multi-functional reconfigurable intelligent surface (MF-RIS). The goal is to overcome the path loss and blockage issues in mmWave networks. Unlike conventional RISs, our MF-RIS can reflect, refract, and amplify signals at the same time. By jointly optimizing the transmit beamforming, MF-RIS coefficients, and hybrid precoding matrices, we propose an iterative algorithm to maximize downlink spectral efficiency (SE), leveraging sequential rank-one convex relaxation and least square methods. Simulation results show the superior performance of MF-RIS over conventional RIS under various parameter settings, highlighting its potential to significantly enhance mmWave network effectiveness.

articleTitle: SIE-GNN: A Link Prediction Algorithm Based on Semantic-Aware Graph Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In the field of knowledge graph link prediction, models based on Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) handle multi-faceted and diverse relationships, effectively capturing complex relationships and patterns between entities. However, these models face limitations in addressing complex interactions between entities. A novel link prediction model, SIE-GNN, is proposed to address this issue. This model combines Semantic Evidence-Aware Graph Neural Networks (SE-GNN) with the InteractE model that integrates a triple-attention mechanism. Evaluation results on public datasets indicate that the SIE-GNN model shows improvements in performance metrics compared to the SE-GNN model.

Author Keywords: semantic evidence aware graph neural network

articleTitle: Domain-Specific Load Balancing for Accelerating Gradient Synchronization Communication in Large Model Training
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: As the scale of GPU clusters expands in large model training scenarios, the mismatch between GPU computing speed and gradient data transmission speed within data centers becomes increasingly evident, resulting in gradient synchroni-zation communication becoming a major bottleneck constraining training efficiency. Despite efforts to mitigate this issue through gradient compression techniques for reducing communication volume and scheduling strategies for enhancing computation communication parallelism, these methods have overlooked the pivotal role of load balancing. The traffic patterns encountered during large model training significantly diverge from the typical long-tail distribution found in data centers. Specifically, they exhibit a few large flows in the spatial dimension and high burstiness in the temporal dimension, with the optimization objective focused on minimizing the tail flow completion time (Tail FCT). In response, this paper presents a domain-specific load balancing method tailored for large model training scenarios. This method leverages the Holt-Winters model to predict round-trip times (RTT), enabling anticipation and avoidance of potential congestion paths. Furthermore, it allocates bandwidth resources fairly based on the size of gradient synchronization flows, ensuring overall high synchronization performance. Additionally, the method employs proactive strategies to actively occupy idle paths and flexibly redirect congested flow, thereby adapting to dynamic network environ-ments. Simulation experiments validate that this method significantly outperforms current mainstream load balancing methods under various GPU cluster scales and congestion path percentages.

articleTitle: Cyber Resilience Based Threat Hunting for Electric Internet of Things
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Threat hunting for Electric Internet of Things (E-IoT) systems is crucial, as these systems are critical national infrastructures and have become primary targets for cyber attackers. However, traditional boundary-based threat hunting approaches cannot deal with internal or unknown threats. To address this problem, this paper introduces cyber resilience (CR) into threat hunting by designing several metrics focused on the actual performance of the E-IoT system. We propose a CR measurement framework called <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S^{3}$</tex> and further integrate it into the threat hunting process. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first CR-based threat hunting approach designed for E-IoT systems. Moreover, we design a reliability enhancement architecture via the proposed <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S^{3}$</tex> framework, in which dynamism, diversity, and redundancy are introduced. Experimental results demonstrate that our proposed <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S^{3}$</tex> framework effectively captures the system's encountered threat levels and aids in the threat hunting process. Additionally, our proposed reliability enhancement architecture is proven to boost the reliability of the E-IoT system.

articleTitle: An Improved DEC Algorithm for Time Series Clustering Task
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In recent years, global climate issues have escalated, driving a substantial increase in the total installed capacity of new energy sources worldwide over the past five years in order to replace fossil fuels and construct a cleaner electricity system. Consequently, the inherent fluctuations and intermittency of new energy sources have increasingly manifested negative impacts on the stable operation of power systems. Against this backdrop, energy storage technologies have garnered widespread attention for their ability to effectively mitigate the uncertainty of new energy output. However, the randomness of new energy output significantly increases the scale of power grid operation scenarios. It is not efficient to design storage solutions tailored for each day, and manually generating the most representative typical scenarios from long-term data is challenging. To address these issues, this paper proposes an improved DEC algorithm for time series clustering tasks. Through validation using actual regional data, the clustering performance of this algorithm surpasses that of the K-means algorithm, the original DEC algorithm, and the PCA+K-means algorithm, enabling the generation of more representative typical scenarios. This holds significant importance in reducing the complexity of optimizing storage configuration.

articleTitle: Question-Enhanced for Semantic Representation in Fine-Tuning Pre-Trained Encoding Models for Chinese Event Argument Extraction
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Event argument extraction is a crucial task in natural language processing, aimed at extracting structured information from unstructured textual data. In response to the challenges posed by limited resources, this study proposes a fine-tuning method for question-answering tasks based on a question-enhanced mechanism in pre-trained models. In practical scenarios where annotated data is scarce, this method demonstrates unique advantages through transfer learning of event types. By pre-training encoding using question templates, the method expands the feature representation of question-answer texts, exhibiting better performance when multiple roles are mentioned in events and these roles belong to the same entity type. Additionally, the method offers effective strategies for handling default arguments that may occur in events. The proposed model not only enhances the recognition and understanding of complex event structures but also improves performance under data scarcity conditions.

articleTitle: 5G Passive Positioning Based on Channel Decoding and Measurement
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In the fifth-generation (5G) private network radio monitoring scenarios, it is essential to monitor and locate 5G terminals that serve as interference sources. The 5G mobile communication system offers excellent coverage and flexibility, making it highly promising for positioning applications. We propose a passive, non-cooperative positioning framework based on a deep understanding of the 5G protocol, capable of achieving two-dimensional positioning of target user equipment (UE) using at least two receivers. This paper proposes the Joint Channel Decoding and Measurement Positioning Method (JCDMP), which obtains observation values through multi-receiver channel measurements of Synchronization Signal Block (SSB) and Physical Random Access Channel (PRACH). Additionally, it mitigates spurious points by utilizing Timing Advance (TA) information obtained from Random Access Response (RAR) decoding. To mitigate positioning errors caused by the complex wireless channel environment, this paper introduces a two-step weighted least squares algorithm based on elliptic curves to enhance positioning accuracy. Simulation results demonstrate that, compared to existing passive positioning methods based on Time Difference of Arrival (TDOA), the proposed framework and algorithm deliver superior positioning performance.

articleTitle: An Intrusion Detection System for the Internet of Vehicles Based on Multi-Level Hybrid Feature Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: The rapid advancement of Internet of Vehicles (IoV) technology has increasingly automated and intelligentized modern vehicles. The connection between vehicle networks and external networks has become much closer, significantly increasing the risks of intrusions and threats, making vehicle network security more critical. This paper propose an intrusion detection model based on multi-level hybrid feature analysis to identify intrusions and threats in the IoV. The model utilizes parallel Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), and One-Dimensional Convolution (Conv1D) to extract global and local features from input data separately and then merges these features to provide comprehensive and integrated hybrid features. It employs a multi-head attention mechanism to extract relationships at different positions in the sequence from multiple perspectives, and an improved emporal Convolutional Network (TCN) to further capture long-distance dependencies in the sequence, thereby extending the model's awareness of long-term dependencies. Finally, malicious traffic is identified through multi-classification. The proposed model was evaluated on two publicly available IoV security datasets, CICIoV2024 and CICIDS2017, achieving accuracy rates of 100% and 99.821 %, respectively. These findings underscore the effectiveness of our proposed model.

articleTitle: Vector Quantized Diffusion Model-Based Joint Source-Channel Coding for Task-Oriented Agent Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In this paper, a novel joint source-channel coding (JSCC) scheme based on the vector quantized diffusion model is proposed to enable task-oriented communication for multi-agent systems. To make the agent communication compatible with digital communication systems, the feature vectors encoded by the parameterized encoder are quantized using a learnable codebook. Furthermore, to improve the reliability of feature vector transmission, a discrete channel denoising diffusion model (DCDDM) is designed. The DCDDM can learn the distribution of the sender agent's feature vectors, and then utilize this learned knowledge to correct the receiver agent's received feature vector. Based on the corrected feature vectors, the parameterized decoder recovers task-related information for the receiver agent's subsequent decision making. Finally, the encoding process of the sender agent as well as the decoding process of the receiver agent are modelled as action policies. The multi-agent collaboration is modelled as a Markov decision process (MDP). The optimal encoder and decoder of the JSCC scheme are then obtained by solving the MDP using a reinforcement learning algorithm. Simulation results show that the proposed scheme can improve the robustness of multi-agent cooperation against channel noise with a reduction in the transmission overhead.

articleTitle: A LSTM-MSGNET Model for Remaining Useful Life of Lubricating Oil Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Lubricating oil plays a significant role in the operation of mechanical equipment, as it reduces wear and tear and maintains the effective lifespan of the equipment. In actual production processes, the frequency of oil changes is very important. If the interval between changes is too long, it can cause equipment damage; if it is too short, it leads to wastage of lubricating oil. However, due to the complexity of the working environment of mechanical equipment, the degradation of lubricating oil is irregular, making it difficult to determine an appropriate replacement interval. The degradation of lubricating oil is a long-term process accompanied by nonlinear changes in various parameter indicators.
