This study employs the LSTM-MSGNet time series prediction method to predict the remaining useful life based on various parameters of lubricating oil collected in the laboratory and test results. LSTM can effectively capture long-term dependencies, and MSGNet can analyze the changes in multi-variable, multi-scale data. Experiments have shown that the LSTM-MSGNet model can achieve good results in predicting the remaining useful life of lubricating oil and can be applied to subsequent online monitoring of lubricating oil quality.

articleTitle: Chinese Named Entity Recognition Based on Lexicon Information Enhancement and Adaptive Adversarial Training
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Aiming at the problem of insufficient accuracy enhancement of fused lexicon information in Chinese named entity recognition, this paper proposes a Chinese named entity recognition based on lexical information enhancement and adaptive adversarial training. The model directly integrates external lexicon knowledge into the BERT layer through the lexicon adapter. In addition, we also propose an adversarial training method. During the training process, this method dynamically adds perturbations to the network variables, aiming to enhance the robustness and generalization ability of the model. The model has experimented on two benchmark Chinese NER datasets, Resume and Weibo, and the experimental results show the effectiveness of the model.

articleTitle: TRAINS: Train and Passenger Real-Time Analytics and Integration Network System Using NeuRaiSya with BhaiCha Algorithm and PINNs Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Current Philippine railway systems face significant challenges in real-time monitoring and effective management of both train movements and passenger flow. These challenges often lead to inefficiencies, safety concerns, and financial losses due to outdated monitoring systems and a lack of predictive capabilities. Addressing these issues, the NeuRaiSya System was developed to enhance the oversight and management of trains and passenger movements. The system assists engineers and operators by providing tools for real-time tracking and prediction of train movements, thereby preventing potential issues and optimizing passenger flow to improve train traffic and maximize railway revenue. The system achieves these goals by gathering sensor data, including accelerometer, gyroscopic, and tilt angle measurements, which are simulated and analyzed using the PINNs application for train anomaly detection and prediction. This BhaiCha algorithm employs a coding matrix to convert sensor data into actionable insights about the train's status and passenger distribution. The system's graphical user interface (GUI) supports real-time monitoring by visualizing train movements and conditions. Simulation results demonstrate that the BhaiCha algorithm effectively generates signal codes that accurately reflect the status of trains and passenger flow, addressing the critical needs of modern railway systems. The implementation of this system shows significant potential to improve safety, efficiency, and financial management in railway operations.

articleTitle: Identification and Analysis of Risky Driving Behaviors at Intersections Based on Vehicle Trajectories
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Intersections are bottlenecks that limit traffic efficiency and safety, with risky driving behaviors at intersections being key factors affecting both. By leveraging real-time vehicle trajectory data collected in an intelligent connected environment, we design threshold judgment methods for risky driving behaviors such as rapid acceleration, rapid deceleration, and sharp turns across different vehicle types and speed ranges. On this basis, three evaluation indicators-average time of rapid acceleration, rapid deceleration, and sharp turns—are used. The entropy weight method and TOPSIS are applied to analyze risky driving behaviors at ten intersections. The identification results show that the occurrence frequency of rapid acceleration and deceleration is related to the degree of traffic weaving, while the frequency of sharp turns is related to intersection saturation. The comprehensive analysis of risky driving behaviors indicates a significant variance in risk levels across intersections, with the TOPSIS scores ranging from 0.191 to 0.943.

articleTitle: The Hierarchical Learning for Energy Saving of Base Stations
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: With the rapid advancement of 5G technology, there has been a significant increase in the number of 5G base stations (BSs), leading to a substantial rise in power consumption. Traditional artificial intelligence (AI) and deep reinforcement learning (DRL) methods face challenges related to decision cycles and exhibit suboptimal performance. To address these issues, this paper proposes a hierarchical learning framework that integrates an outer Binary Particle Swarm Optimization (BPSO) algorithm with an inner Multi-Agent Proximal Policy Optimization (MAPPO) algorithm, thereby significantly enhancing the convergence speed of the learning process. Moreover, this hierarchical framework effectively partitions and addresses different modules within the base station-specifically, the Remote Radio Unit (RRU) module and Building Baseband Unit (BBU) module. In comparison to existing algorithms, our proposed outer layer achieves a reduction in power consumption by 54.19%, while the inner layer further decreases power consumption by an additional 56.16%.

articleTitle: MRLRO: Meta-Reinforcement Learning Based Segment Routing Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Segment Routing over IPv6 (SRv6) has been considered as a promising and efficient traffic engineering (TE) technology. However, traditional SR-TE solutions primarily fo-cus on improving the performance of long-term optimization strategies, while neglecting adaptability to dynamic environments. Some solutions place greater emphasis on the ability to adjust routing strategies in real-time for practical applications, but they suffer from slow adjustment speeds and high data col-lection costs. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a meta-reinforcement learning based SRv6 routing optimization algorithm (MRLRO). During the pre-training phase, MRLRO leverages multi-task training and Kullback-Leibler divergence to enhance the ability of agent to quickly learn and adapt to new tasks. With the fine-tuning operations of the agent, MRLRO can interact rapidly with the environment and adjust routing strategies under traffic bursts. Once the network stabilizes, the agent utilizes the experience accumulated during the pre-training phase to make routing strategies. Additionally, MRLRO involves the generalization of graph neural networks to improve its robust-ness. Simulation results demonstrate that MRLRO significantly outperforms existing reinforcement learning algorithms under dynamic traffic matrices with traffic bursts.

articleTitle: Hybrid Cross Modality Feature Fusion
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: This paper presents a novel RGB-D saliency object detection model, which utilizes the MAE model for RGB feature extraction and the ViT model for depth feature extraction. By employing our Hybrid Cross Modality Feature Fusion module, the model effectively integrates RGB and depth features. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed module significantly enhances detection performance across various public datasets, especially on datasets with lower-quality depth images. Additionally, the superiority of the proposed model is further validated by comparing it with multiple feature fusion schemes.

articleTitle: A Model Based on LSTM and Data Augmentation for Network Traffic Prediction with Few Samples
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Utilizing artificial intelligence technologies, particularly deep learning models, for modeling and predicting time series has demonstrated significant efficacy and potential across various fields. In the domain of network traffic, models can predict future trends by leveraging features of learned traffic patterns, thereby facilitating rational allocation of network resources as well as assessing network security and preventing cyber threats. However, deep learning models often require large amounts of high-quality time series data for training, and network traffic data, being somewhat private, is generally not easily accessible. In the real world, effective modeling is often hindered by the lack of sufficient data. In this paper, we propose a method Transfer Data Augmentation(TransDA) for augmenting few samples of network traffic data based on network traffic characteristics and the concept of transfer learning. Additionally, we have combined Long Short-Term Memory(LSTM) with the newly proposed Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks(KAN), replacing the original Multi-Layer Perceptron(MLP), to better capture the nonlinear relationships between sequential data points. Experimental results indicate that our proposed model achieves better performance on few-sample network traffic datasets compared to the standard models.

articleTitle: A Joint Graph Neural Model for Chinese Domain Event and Relation Extraction with Character-Word Fusion
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: One of the most difficult problems in Chinese event extraction is the lack of interaction between characters and words, which is more prominent in domain-specific event extraction tasks. Previous studies focus on event detection and lack a joint model for Chinese event and intra-event relation extraction. This paper proposes a character-word fusion method based on a graph convolutional neural network model, which fully associates characters with related entities and greatly improves the information interaction between characters and words. At the same time, the relation extraction task is combined with the recognition and classification task of event trigger words and arguments, forming an end-to-end method for transforming text into an event graph. Experimental results on the ACE Chinese data set and Chinese domain data set DGRE demonstrate the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed method. At the same time, through the analysis of strategy analysis, ablation experiment, parameter analysis, and other analysis work, each module's role and the model's scalability are verified.

articleTitle: Matrix Optimization Algorithm for WebGL-Based 3D Visualization Construction Models
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: 3D visualization has been widely used in various fields, from scientific computing to data analysis and virtual reality, etc., with increasingly demanding performance and quality requirements. WebGL-based 3D rendering technology brings powerful graphics processing capabilities to the Web platform, however, complex 3D models require efficient matrix operations to handle transformations, projections and view switching, etc. Traditional algorithms are difficult to strike a balance between performance and effect. In this paper, we propose an algorithm based on matrix optimization, which is specifically used to improve the computational efficiency and rendering quality of WebGL 3D visualization construction. Based on the analysis of existing algorithms, this paper proposes a strategy combining matrix decomposition and parallel optimization, and experimentally verifies its significant performance improvement in complex 3D scenes. Ultimately, the research in this paper not only improves the real-time interactive performance of 3D visualization, but also provides theoretical and practical support for future complex 3D applications based on WebGL.

articleTitle: Hierarchical Multi-Domain Fusion Gait Recognition Method Based on FMCW Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Existing radar-based human gait recognition methods suffer from insufficient utilization of radar data, inadequate extraction of spectrogram feature information, and neglect of inter-domain complementary information. To address these issues, this paper proposes a Hierarchical Multi-Domain Gait Fusion Network (HMDGF-Net). Firstly, the FMCW radar is applied to collect the echo data of human gait movements. To fully utilize the radar information, the echo data is preprocessed to obtain three different radar domain spectrums. Subsequently, TFEM and DBFEM modules are designed based on the attributes of each spectrogram to perform feature extraction. Finally, based on the correlation between spectrograms, a hierarchical correlation fusion strategy is employed to fuse the extracted features, thereby enhancing the complementary information between different domains and achieving high-precision human gait recognition. Experimental results show that the proposed method achieves an average recognition accuracy of 95.28% for six types of gait movements, effectively improving the recognition performance compared to the state-of-the-art methods.

articleTitle: Dynamic Transmission and Spectrum Scheduling for Air-Ground Collaborative Communications
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) and UAV-assisted communications are expected to play an important role in the Internet of Things (IoT). Due to the widespread line-of-sight channels and the potential spectrum congestion, dynamic transmission/spectrum scheduling is recognized as an essential component of air-ground collaborative communications. Nevertheless, state-of-the-art decision-making on transmission/spectrum scheduling can suffer from multi-granularity and complex decision-making tasks, as well as the curse of dimensionality caused by the increasing of the number of UAVs and terrestrial user equipment (UE), i.e. agents. To handle this issue, this paper proposes a joint trajectory planning and transmission/spectrum scheduling scheme, based on hierarchical reinforcement learning (HRL) and mean-field theory. We propose to formulate the decision-making problem of the multi-granularity trajectory planning and transmission/spectrum scheduling as a semi-Markov decision process (SMDP), i.e. the basis of developing an URL-based algorithm. In order to optimize the joint scheduling (including trajectory planning) policy in the presence of a large number of UAVs and UEs, mean-field theory is integrated with HRL. It is shown that the proposed algorithm is capable of learning a joint scheduling policy in the presence of many agents and significantly mitigating the long-term average backlog of data bits in the network.

articleTitle: ALIEN-YOLO: Low-Light Object Detection with Edge Extraction and Convolutional Attention
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In the field of security monitoring, the detection of targets in low-light nighttime images is essential for identifying potential security threats. However, this task is challenged by factors such as increased noise, loss of detail, and reduced contrast, which often result in the suboptimal performance of existing detection algorithms under these conditions. To address these challenges, this study introduces an enhanced model based on YOLOv8, termed ALIEN-YOLO. This model incorporates the Adaptive Edge Extraction Low-light Image Enhancement Network (ALIEN), which is specifically designed to mitigate noise and enhance contrast. Additionally, it integrates the Head Depthwise Convolution Attention (HDCA) module to improve the detection of small and occluded objects, and the C2F-SH module, which is optimized with a Shrinkage mechanism to enhance robustness and accuracy through denoising. Experimental evaluations conducted on the ExDark and DARK FACE datasets demonstrated that the improved model achieved a mean Average Precision (mAP) of 81.2% and 54.3%, respectively, indicating a significant enhancement over the baseline YOLOv8. Notably, despite the integration of multiple modules, the model maintains a real-time processing capability of 60 frames per second. These findings underscore the effectiveness of the proposed ALIEN-YOLO model in enhancing target detection performance in low-light conditions, thereby underscoring its potential value for practical applications.

articleTitle: Dynamic Spectrum Collaboration for UAV Swarms Under Interference Conditions: A Multi-Agent Deep Reinforcement Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: This paper investigates the issue of spectrum collaboration under dynamic changes in the number of unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) swarms under jamming conditions. We focus on the scenario where multiple UAV swarms conduct reconnaissance tasks, the head UAV (H-UAV) of each swarm relays the detected information gathered by the swarm back to the ground control station (GCS). To achieve spectrum collaboration among H-UAVs, first, we model the problem as an optimization that maximizes the sum of the achievable rates of H-UAVs to GCS. Then, we treat H-UAVs as agents and adopt the classic multi-agent proximal policy optimization (MAPPO) for centralized training of the agents. By setting the number of agents to a specific value, we make it applicable for distributed spectrum collaboration scenarios with dynamic changes in the number of UAV swarms. Finally, we measure the effectiveness of the algorithm by the spectrum conflict occurrences. Simulation results show that the proposed algorithm can significantly reduce the number of spectrum conflicts among H-UAVs, achieving effective spectrum collaboration under dynamic changes in the number of UAV swarms in jamming conditions.

articleTitle: A Multi-Objective Optimization Based LEO Satellite Beam Hopping Resource Allocation Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In satellite communication systems, due to the characteristics of low-orbit satellites, such as their high mobility and extensive coverage, issues arise including uneven distribution of satellite terminal users in time and space, as well as significant variations in communication service types and traffic volumes. To satisfy diverse user demands, there is an urgent need for efficient and integrated allocation of limited resources within satellite communication systems. Currently, most resource allocation schemes for satellite communication systems are based on ground requests and focus on single-objective optimization for a specific type of resource allocation, lacking comprehensive consideration of integrated resource allocation. This paper proposes a resource allocation scheme for beam-hopping systems based on multi-objective optimization. In the process of modeling satellite communication scenarios, satellite resources are divided into three dimensions: time, frequency, and beam. The primary research focuses on timeslot resource allocation, incorporating multiple objective optimization functions. Additionally, given the interconnected and mutually constrained nature of frequency, power, and beam resources in hopped-beam systems, frequency and beam allocation strategies are introduced for holistic resource allocation and scheduling. Finally, under various ground terminal distribution scenarios, the system delay, throughput performance, and the impact of timeslot length on system performance are analyzed and verified.

articleTitle: Over-the-Air Federated Edge Learning with Error-Feedback One-Bit Quantization and Power Control
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Over-the-air federated edge learning (Air-FEEL) is a communication-efficient framework for distributed machine learning using training data distributed at edge devices. This framework enables all edge devices to transmit model updates simultaneously over the entire available bandwidth, allowing for over-the-air aggregation. The existing one-bit digital over-the-air aggregation scheme features one-bit gradient quantization at edge devices and majority voting-based decoding at edge server, and therefore offers enhanced communication efficiency. However, the low-resolution one-bit gradient quantization slows down the model convergence and leads to performance degradation, while the aggregation errors caused by channel fading in Air-FEEL further impair the performance. To address these issues, we propose the error-feedback one-bit broadband digital aggregation (EFOBDA) with an optimized power control policy. To this end, we first derive the impact of aggregation errors on the convergence of FEEL with EFOBDA. Then, we further introduce a power control policy by maximizing the convergence rate under instantaneous power constraints. The analytical results and optimized power control policy are validated by the experiments, which show that the proposed scheme achieves significantly faster convergence and higher test accuracy in image classification tasks compared with the vanilla one-bit quantization scheme without error feedback or optimized power control policy.

articleTitle: Distributed Beam Pattern Design Scheme in Multi-Satellite System
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellites have attracted wide attention due to their advantages of flexible networking, low transmission latency and wide coverage. Beam-hopping technology can circumvent inter-beam interference through spatial isolation and frequency multiplexing, thus significantly increasing the capacity of LEO communication satellites. However, traditional multi-satellite beam-hopping schemes are mostly centralized strategies which put all decision-making tasks on one decision center, and their computational complexity will surge with the increase of the number of satellites. Therefore, this paper proposes a distributed multi-satellite beam-hopping algorithm (DMS-BH) that treats each satellite as a rational decision maker, according to a probability-based inter-satellite interference assessment method, each satellite capable of deciding time slot simultaneously. Simulation results show that the DMS-BH can achieve the trade-off between illuminating more hotspot cells and reducing co-channel interference.

articleTitle: Research on High-Dimensional Matrix Multiplication in Machine Learning for MEC
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Machine learning (ML) algorithms have been widely deployed in mobile edge computing (MEC). Howerver, algorithms in MEC always demands high computational power to process complex models and large datasets in real-time. A critical component of this computational workload is matrix multiplication, a fundamental operation in many ML algorithms, particularly in deep learning. To meet the stringent latency and performance requirements of MEC applications, leveraging Graphics Processing Unit (GPU) acceleration for matrix multiplication is essential. GPUs, with their massive parallel processing capabilities, can significantly enhance the efficiency and speed of matrix computations, enabling rapid inference and training at the edge. This acceleration not only reduces the latency but also offloads the central cloud, providing a more distributed and scalable solution for real-time ML applications at the edge. To this end, this paper first introduces the background of using matrix multiplication to accelerate model training speed in ML for MEC, clarifies the significance of accelerating matrix multiplication to ML and MEC, then reviews and experiments on existing schemes for accelerating matrix multiplication and compares and summarizes various schemes from the perspective of different sparsity of matrices on the GPU. Finally, we points out the possible future research directions and technical challenges, and provides the certain reference value for the research in related fields.

articleTitle: A Multiple Objective Particle Swarm Optimization Algorithm for Time Series Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Time series segmentation is aimed at representing a time series by using a set of segments. In most cases, time series segmentation can reduce approximation error by increasing number of segments, implying a conflict between these two factors. Different techniques have been applied to time series segmentation and achieved good results, yet the simultaneous optimization of the number of segments and approximation error is seldom considered. For this, this paper proposes a Multiple Objective Particle Swarm Optimization algorithm for Time Series Segmentation (MOPSOTTS). MOPSOTTS improves a Dynamic Exploitation Barebones Particle Swarm Optimization (DBBePSO) algorithm, aiming for multiple objective optimization in time series segmentation. To generate segmentation solutions with varying numbers of segments and different cut points, MOPSOTTS designs crossover and mutation operators to update the particle vectors throughout the iterative process. On two time series from real-world problems and four time series from UCR repository, we compare MOPSOTTS with three traditional algorithms for time series segmentation, conduct a controlled study on MOPSOTTS, and analyze the computation time overhead of these algorithms. According to the experimental results, MOPSOTTS generally outperforms three traditional algorithms for time series segmentation, and the improved DBBePSO algorithm and the crossover and mutation operators can effectively enhance the performance of MOPSOTTS.

articleTitle: Resource-Aware Heterogeneous Cluster Scheduling System for Deep Neural Network Training Tasks
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) have become integral to various modern artificial intelligence applications. As DNN models grow in complexity, diverse accelerators are increasingly utilized for training. Current heterogeneous cluster schedulers recognize performance disparities among models across different GPU types, managing costly GPU resources for users. However, these schedulers often neglect the significance of auxiliary resources in allocation decisions, relying on a GPU-based proportional distribution for CPU and memory resources. This study investigates the sensitivity of various DNN models to auxiliary resources through empirical experiments, revealing that training throughput for image and speech models is highly reliant on CPU allocation, while language models exhibit lower sensitivity. In response, we developed Nexus, a resource-aware scheduler designed to optimize resource utilization in heterogeneous GPU clusters. Experimental results demonstrate that Nexus can reduce average task completion time by up to 2.26x compared to traditional scheduling systems.

articleTitle: PSCA: Position-Syntax and Cross-Aspect for Aspect-based Sentiment Analysis in One Model
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Aspect-based sentiment analysis (ABSA) is a fine-grained sentiment analysis task that aims to identify the senti-ment polarity of specific aspects within sentence.methods based on graph neural networks that heavily rely on Syntax tree and semantic composition tree have been used to mine syntactic information In recent years, However, these methods overlook the feature of location influence factor of words and may provide irrelevant or even interfering noisy signals for ABSA due to the word association relationship mined by the Syntax tree and semantic composition tree. To alleviate the impact of noise information and fully explore the multiple factors of ABSA, In this paper, we propose a new framework PSCA which Integrating Position,Syntax and Cross-Aspect module and mining infor-mation on position importance, syntax and semantic structure dependencies and cross-aspect correlation information. Moreover, Experimental results on four real-world datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of PSCA compared to previous state-of-the-art methods.

articleTitle: SEQD: An Optimized Approach for Microservice Function Chain Placement in Satellite Edge Clouds
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In the era of sixth-generation (6G) networks, satellite edge clouds have become essential for delivering globally accessible, low-latency services. However, deploying microservices within these networks presents significant challenges due to resource limitations, high latency, and the dynamic nature of satellite environments. This paper addresses the optimization problem of microservice function chain placement in satellite edge clouds, with a dual objective of minimizing end-to-end latency and placement costs. To tackle this, we propose the Q-Learning Enhanced Drops in Satellite Edge Clouds(SEQD) algorithm, which integrates reinforcement learning with heuristic optimization to achieve efficient and adaptive microservice placement. Simulation results demonstrate that SEQD achieves faster convergence and greater latency reduction compared to baseline algorithms, particularly in large-scale network scenarios, showcasing its potential for enhancing resource utilization and performance in satellite edge networks.

articleTitle: Research on Task Planning Key Technology for UAV Communication Optical Cable Line Inspection
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Traditional communication Optical Cable Line Inspections (OCLI) often use labor inspection method, but traditional method will take long inspection time and high labor consumption. In contrast, OCLI by unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) inspections have many advantages, such as good visibility, low cost, flexibility and high efficiency. There are many key issues and technologies need to be addressed, which significantly impact the execution of OCLI tasks. This paper proposes a UAV OCLI task planning method based on the combination of the Analytic Hierarchy Process and Genetic Algorithm, and its feasibility and practicality are verified through simulation experiments.

articleTitle: Travel Distance Aware ISAC Enabled IoV: An Intelligent Power Allocation Solution
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) is a key technology for next-generation wireless networks, and the problem of dynamic resource allocation in Internet of vehicles (IoV) scenarios needs to be studied. In this paper, we study the problem of power allocation in an ISAC enabled IoV scenario based on deep reinforcement learning techniques. Specifically, we consider an ISAC base station that senses information about multiple vehicles on the road while sending the sensed vehicle information as well as information about the surrounding environment to the vehicles on the road. The spectral efficiency of communication, as well as the sensed mutual information, is chosen as the quality of service (QoS) metrics for both communication and sensing, with the objective of minimizing the maximum distance traveled by the vehicles during the duration of the message sending. To solve this problem, we propose a proximal policy optimization (PPO)-based intelligent power allocation scheme, which minimizes the objective while satisfying the communication and sensing QoS. Simulation results show that our proposed scheme outperforms other compared schemes.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of Q-Learning-Based List Scheduling Algorithms in Heterogeneous Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Task scheduling plays a crucial role in Heterogeneous Systems (HS). The makespan (or scheduling length) minimization is the key criterion of the task scheduling algorithm in HS. Recently, the rapid development of machine learning has led to its widespread application in various fields. This paper extends existing heuristic-based task scheduling algorithms using Reinforcement learning techniques. Moreover, we use the Q-learning technique to extend two heuristic scheduling algorithms, the PEFT and IPPTS. We aim to combine these algorithms with Q-learning to improve their task prioritization. We compare the HEFT, QL-HEFT, QL-PEFT, QL-PPTS, and QL-IPPTS using real-world scientific workflows. The experimental results show that QL-HEFT outperforms QL-PEFT, QL-PPTS, and QL-IPPTS by 27.12 percent, 16.75 percent, and 10.7 percent, respectively

articleTitle: An Intrusion Detection Method Based on Transfer Component Analysis and an Extreme Learning Machine
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Intrusion detection technology is an active network defense technology that has quickly become an important means of ensuring network security since it was proposed. With the development of machine learning, its application in intrusion detection has effectively improved the detection effect. However, due to the increasing volume and dimension of the current network data, the model training speed of machine learning-based intrusion detection technology is slow, and the update cost is high. In addition, different distributions of intrusion detection data affect the detection effect. In this paper, the extreme learning machine (ELM) model is extended. An intrusion detection method, TCA-ELM, based on transfer component analysis (TCA) and an extreme learning machine is proposed. TCA-ELM utilizes TCA to extract data features and project data to a new space by greatly reducing the distance and dimension between the data distributions and then trains the ELM in the new feature space to improve the training efficiency and detection rate. Experimental tests are performed on the famous NSL-KDD dataset, and the experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed TCA-ELM method. Compared with the other four benchmark algorithms, the training time is significantly improved, and the detection accuracy is also significantly improved.

articleTitle: Zero-Trust Single-Package Authorization Authentication Scheme Supporting Privacy Protection and Traceability
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Single Packet Authorization (SPA) mechanism, as an essential component of the standard Software-Defined Perimeter in zero-trust architecture, has demonstrated significant advantages in achieving resource stealth access, authentication of access identities, and reduction of network attack surfaces. However, conventional SPA mechanisms employ a traditional centralized structure for storing and distributing keys, lacking privacy protection for user identity information and the ability to effectively trace and identify visitor information during the authentication process. In this paper, we propose a scheme that uses group signatures to anonymize user identity information and combines blockchain technology to supervise and authenticate the identities of anonymous users, thus achieving anonymous identity authentication and supervision. This forms a privacy-preserving and traceable zero-trust SPA authentication scheme, expanding and perfecting the functions of the software-defined perimeter in the zero-trust architecture.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Wireless Communication Systems for Self-Developed SDR Hardware Platforms and Simulink
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: With the rapid development of wireless communication technology and the increasing diversification of communication standards, communication systems need to support a variety of different standards and be configured in a more flexible manner. Against this backdrop, modern communication systems are increasingly adopting Software Defined Radio (SDR) technology. The emergence of heterogeneous architecture devices that integrate dedicated processors and programmable logic resources has further propelled the development of SDR technology. This thesis, based on the self-developed SDR hardware platform using Xilinx Zynq-7000 series heterogeneous architecture SoC and ADI AD9361 RF transceiver, and targeting the MATLAB Simulink framework, constructs a wireless communication system using Quadrature Phase Shift Keying (QPSK) modulation and demodulation. On this basis, software simulation within the Simulink environment and actual testing on the self-developed SDR hardware platform have been completed. Through collaborative design, simulation, and debugging of software and hardware, the research content of the thesis provides a more efficient and convenient implementation method for wireless communication systems based on SDR technology, and offers a reference solution for the miniaturization of multifunctional software radio communication devices.

articleTitle: Trusted Secret Sharing Scheme with Verifiable Computation Based on On-Chain and Off-Chain Collaboration for IoT
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Blockchain provides an excellent solution to the centralized trust problems encountered in federated IoT data sharing platforms, such as data tampering and single-point attacks. However, its transparency also undermines the privacy of federated learning in model training and model sharing, thus creating the following challenges: (1) Federated model training needs to be conducted off-chain to ensure privacy. Since off-chain computing is not supervised by the blockchain, the trustworthiness of off-chain training models cannot be guaranteed. (2) Federated models shared on-chain expose intermediate parameters to the public. Malicious users can infer the original training data from these parameters, leading to privacy leakage at the model sharing level. To address these issues, this paper proposes a federal trusted secret sharing model based on on-chain and off-chain collaboration. In this model, we first design a federated trusted verification algorithm to ensure the trustworthiness of models trained off-chain. Then, based on the algorithm, combined with CKKS and threshold homomorphic encryption, a deep federated trusted secret sharing scheme based on on-chain and off-chain collaboration for IoT is constructed to ensure comprehensive trust and privacy in federated blockchain sharing schemes. Simulation experiments show that the scheme is feasible.

articleTitle: A Novel Unsupervised Frequency Recognition Method for SSVEP-Based BCIs Using Adaptive Updating and Transfer Learning Strategy
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: The application of supervised recognition algorithms based on steady-state visual evoked potentials (SSVEP) has gained increasing attention in the field of signal processing. However, these methods typically demand a large amount of training data to ensure accurate recognition, resulting in high training costs and poor human-computer interaction experiences. To address these issues, a novel method called filter bank unsupervised adaptive transfer-extended CCA has been proposed for SSVEP recognition. Unlike previous methods, this approach eliminates the need for calibration data from the current subject for training. It employs a transfer learning strategy to construct a transfer average template, utilizes an adaptive updating strategy to update the transfer template and the spatial filter with the current subject's data, and incorporates the filter bank analysis strategy to achieve high-performance unsupervised SSVEP recognition. This method was compared with three state-of-the-art unsupervised approaches, and experimental results demonstrated its superior recognition accuracy and information transfer rate. Specifically, when the time window length is 1.0 s, FBUAT-eCCA achieves an accuracy of 84.69 ± 6.33% and an information transfer rate of 148.90 ± 15.60 bits/min. Additionally, FBUAT-eCCA shows strong performance in extracting inter-class separation features.

articleTitle: An Efficient Modeling and Analysis Approach for mmWave UAV-Assisted Network Under Jamming Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Millimeter-wave (mmWave) Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV)-assisted networks, with their large bandwidth and ultra-high speeds, are considered to have great potential for application, but there is little research on the analysis of their performance under malicious interference. This paper addresses the significant blocking effects of mmWave UAV-assisted networks and their application in military operations, adopts an antenna model with variable beamwidth and direction, introduces airborne malicious jammers, models the distribution of UAVs through the MHCPP model with repulsion constraints, and uses stochastic geometry to analyze the coverage and capacity characteristics of the network under the existence of malicious interference, and derives the expression for coverage under active interference. Simulation results show that the achievable network throughput can be increased by 47%, and the coverage probability of a typical Ground User (GU) approaches an upper limit of approximately 95%.

articleTitle: Less is More: Channel-Aware Semantic Satellite Access Network Slicing
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Satellites equipped with computing capabilities play a crucial role as access platforms for 5G and NextG (beyond 5G) non-terrestrial networks (NTNs). They facilitate the continuous execution of resource-intensive edge-assisted deep learning (DL) tasks offloaded from user equipment (UEs) in remote areas. To manage this effectively, satellite access network (SAN) resources must be carefully “sliced”, taking into account both the limited energy availability and the inherent scarcity of SAN resources. Existing SAN slicing approaches tend to use semantic communications for UE data transmission but overlook the impact of varying channel qualities between UEs and satellites. A cyclic dependency between the inter-slice and intra-slice resource schedulers makes it challenging to incorporate channel awareness at both levels. Armed with this insight, in this paper, we propose channel-aware semantic SAN (CASemSAN), a semantic SAN slicing algorithm that considers the channel conditions for NextG AI-native NTNs. It not only compresses tasks' data according to their semantics but also exploits the channel conditions of a SAN to support more tasks while still minimizing overall energy consumption. After analyzing the characteristics of this optimization problem, we propose an online greedy CASemSAN slicing algorithm to approximate its optimal solution. Extensive experiments verify the effectiveness of CASemSAN in energy saving and its ability to support a substantial number of tasks, compared with other baselines.

articleTitle: Digital Twin with Delay-Optimal Relay-Assisted Federated Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a secure federated learning (FL) system in the digital twin (DT) based on relay technique and cooperative interference, which realizes accurate real-time prediction of physical entities. First, an optimization problem aiming to minimize the total delay of each FL iteration is established, in which the local device performs model uploading by non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) technique. Then, in order to solve this non-convex problem, a layered optimization algorithm is proposed, the local processing rate of each device, the transmission power of the relay and the interference signal of the jammer are obtained. Finally, numerical results show that the algorithm is effective and the relay-based FL security scheme can be effectively applied to DT.

articleTitle: Tobacco Curing State Recognition Based on a Multi-Sensor Feature Fusion Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: The accurate identification of tobacco curing status is a complex process involving comprehensive analysis of multiple types of feature data sources. The influence of each type of feature on the state recognition model varies with the change in the curing process, and the existing models cannot reasonably utilize these feature data, which makes it difficult to improve the model recognition accuracy. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a dynamic data fusion scheme based on clustering methods and uses the LightGBM algorithm and data fusion method to build a state recognition fusion model that integrates six state recognition sub-models, which can accurately identify the curing status. SRFM aims to integrate curing expertise and automatically adjust the data fusion strategy according to the changes in multi-source data to meet the needs of comprehensive data analysis in recognition. Through experimental comparison, SRFM outperforms the existing models, with an accuracy of 99.8% in identifying the curing status and a macro F1-Score of 99.9%.

articleTitle: A Multi-Modal Learning Framework for MIMO Channel Information Acquisition
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (MIMO) has been proven to be a successful technology in 5G systems. Applying Artificial Intelligence (AI) and machine learning to MIMO is expected to further boost the spectrum efficiency and capacity of MIMO for 5G-advanced and 6G, because more accurate Channel State Information (CSI) will be enabled via intelligent channel estimation and prediction. Low overhead CSI feedback is also possible when AI is utilized in the channel compression and recovery in frequency division duplex systems. However, designing separate AI models for channel estimation, prediction, and compression/recovery requires huge efforts in model training and large memory to store the model parameters. It is highly motivated to explore how to achieve accurate MIMO CSI with minimum AI model training and storage overhead for all the possible CSI related use cases. In this paper, a multi-modal learning framework is proposed for MIMO channel estimation, prediction, and compression. The framework consists of a single common feature extraction module used in all the use cases, followed by alight weight adaptation modules designed for different use cases. This proposed design is able to avoid the supernumerary extraction of shareable features for different use cases and has been demonstrated to significantly reduce the complexity of the AI models.

articleTitle: Collaborative Perception and Collaborative Computing for Value Maximization in Smart Grid
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: With the integration and development of smart grid and vehicle networking, autonomous vehicles make the power grid system and vehicles fully perceive the urban environment and load changes through collaborative perception and computing technology, and carry out power grid management tasks and driving tasks without manual intervention. However, collaborative perception necessitates the sharing of a substantial amount of sensing data, and collaborative computing makes it difficult to consider the interests of each participant simultaneously. Therefore, in this paper, we establish a value evaluation system for sensing block messages to perform collaborative perception and computing among vehicles in the smart grid, which can achieve mutual benefit and win-win situations between vehicles and comprehensive perception of the grid environment. Next, we jointly optimize the allocation of sensing message blocks, communication and computing resources, and formulate a sum value maximization problem for the target vehicle with time delay constraints. Given that the above problem is a mixed-integer nonlinear programming (MINLP) problem, we adopt linear relaxation and a successive convex approximation (SCA) algorithm to solve it. Finally, the simulation results demonstrate the superiority of the proposed scheme compared with existing baseline schemes.

articleTitle: An Artificial Intelligence Based Method for Bartending
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In recent years, artificial intelligence (AI) has made significant advancements, but its application in precision-demanding fields like bartending remains limited. This paper presents an AI-based method for bartending that integrates computer vision and natural language processing (NLP) for precise ingredient identification and action generation. Using the YOLOv8 model, the system achieves real-time detection of bartending tools and ingredients, while Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) are employed to generate customized bartending actions based on user preferences. This method enhances adaptability in dynamic bar environments, addressing gaps in current semi-automated bartending systems. The proposed system significantly improves operational efficiency, precision, and user satisfaction, showcasing the potential for advanced commercial AI applications in hospitality.

articleTitle: Design and Research of a PLC Simulation Training System Based on EtherCAT
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: With the rapid development of industrial automation, PLC (Programmable Logic Controller) plays a crucial role as a core control device in the production process. However, due to limited equipment resources in traditional training, it is difficult to conduct high-quality training activities comprehensively. To solve this issue and enhance students' practical skills, designing a digital PLC simulation training system based on EtherCAT has become essential. This paper utilizes OpenPLC programming, integrating Igh EtherCAT Master as the master station and EtherCAT Slave Stack Code to configure the slave station. Communication is realized through the FC1100 network card, constructing a PLC simulation training system. The system aims to provide students with an intuitive learning platform, helping them understand the working principles of PLC and the application of the EtherCAT protocol, thus improving the quality of experimental teaching.

articleTitle: Combine Pre-Trained Language Model and Classical Recommendation Network for Conversational Recommender Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Conversational recommender systems (CRSs) typically require natural language interaction with users and complete recommendations within the conversation. Existing approaches often struggle with the integration of generated responses and recommended items. To address this, we propose a novel CRS model named KGPLM, incorporating the Knowledge Graph based recommender module and the dialogue module based on the fine-tuned Pre-trained Language Model (PLM). We decompose the dialogue generation task into two subtasks: dialogue goal prediction and response generation. The former enables the system to make recommendations appropriately during the conversation, while the latter, through the introduction of item tokens, achieves the seamless integration between the recommended items and the generated responses. To fine-tune PLM for the CRS, we propose a two-stage fine-tuning approach: (1) multi-task learning explores the connections between the two sub-tasks; (2) prompt learning optimizes the model's performance on specific sub-tasks. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach on both item recommendation and response generation tasks in the final responses.

articleTitle: IRAM-SQL: A Language Model Integrating Relation-Aware Mechanism for Text-to-SQL
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: The task of text-to-SQL aims to convert natural language questions into executable SQL queries within relational databases. This greatly enhances the usability of relational database querying, alleviating the difficulties faced by users who are not proficient in SQL. A major challenge in text-to-SQL task is the model's ability to recognize entities accurately. This paper focuses on this issue and proposes a language model with an integrated relation-aware mechanism for text-to-SQL, named IRAM-SQL. We explore the adaptability of pretrained models for downstream text-to-SQL tasks, ultimately selecting CodeT5+ as the pretrained model, which is trained on a large dataset of source code and annotation, exploring the shared representation between natural language and code. Therefore, the model's ability to generate structured sentences would be explored during the pretraining phase. At the same time, we also integrate a relation-aware mechanism throughout the model fine-tuning process. To this end, we comprehensively models the relational information between natural language questions and database schemas, integrating these relationships effectively within the encoder and decoder of the Transformer architecture. Two denoising tasks is employed during training to help the model learn these relationships more effectively. The integration of relational information during encoding and decoding, along with the emphasis on entity awareness in the training tasks, enhances the model's entity recognition capabilities. We evaluate our proposed framework on the SPIDER dataset and three of its robustness variants: SPIDER-SYN, SPIDER-DK, and SPIDER-REALISTIC. Experimental results indicate that IRAM-SQL, with its comprehensively integrated relation-aware mechanism, demonstrates strong performance and robustness.

articleTitle: A Bi-Path Continuous Convolutional Network for Efficient Lagrangian Fluid Simulation
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Data-driven Lagrangian fluid simulators provide a fast and approximate solution to fluid dynamics problems, offering greater convenience compared to traditional numeri-cal methods. However, current approaches often overlook the importance of fluid-solid coupling and struggle to balance high accuracy with efficiency. To address this issue, we propose a bi-path continuous convolutional network that processes fluid and obstacle features independently on separate paths. The lightweight attention-gated fusion module is seamlessly embedded between the paths to selectively fuse these features, emphasizing critical particle collisions. Moreover, we introduce continuous central difference convolutions and historical velocity inputs to provide more effective features for predicting accurately. Experimental results on multiple datasets show that our approach strikes an excellent balance between prediction accuracy and inference time while achieving great generalizability.

articleTitle: Cooperative Resource Overbooking Based Application Placement in Mobile Edge Computing for Internet of Things
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Mobile edge computing (MEC) is an efficient way to offload computing tasks to edge data centers to reduce end-to-end communication delays for many emerging IoT applications. However, most existing application placement schemes in MEC did not consider the dynamic nature of the aggregated computing resource demand, where applying the resource overbooking policy can achieve higher resource utilization in MEC. This paper focuses on efficient cooperative resource overbooking and application placement strategy in MEC. First, we propose a proportional fairness-based multiple-tenant cooperative resource overbooking (PF-CROB) scheme, and design a bisection search algorithm to determine the minimum aggregate resource demand for application placement in MEC. Second, we propose a First Fit Decreasing-based Application Cooperative Placement (FFD-ACP) scheme, which judges whether an application can be consolidated to some MEC server according to the Resource Demand Violation Ratio (RDVR) performance under cooperative resource overbooking rules. The effectiveness of the proposed schemes is validated by simulation, where the number of RDVR-guaranteed applications admitted into MEC servers almost doubled by using the FFD-ACP scheme.

articleTitle: TCPN-based Resilience Evaluation of SFC with Dynamic Heterogeneous Redundant Structure Towards 6G Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Service Function Chain (SFC) makes easier and more convenient to compose on-demand service chains, which can serve the 6G's six use cases. Compared with 5G networks, resilience is first proposed in 6G networks, which puts higher service requirements on SFC. Different from security, privacy and trust, resilience focuses on ongoing service delivery. With the increasing adverse conditions such as security risks and random failures, the traditional methods are difficult to meet the resilience requirement, which needs to be solved urgently. Endogenous security technique based on Dynamic Heterogeneous Redundant (DHR) structure is a feasible method to empower the resilience ability of SFC. In this paper, we introduce the architecture and workflow of SFC with DHR structure (DHRSFC) and analyze its system failures. To prove its resilience ability, we design a resilience evaluation model based on Time Colored Petri Net (TCPN), which TCPN can accurately describe the response processes to system failures and time property. Evaluation results prove the excellent resilience performance of DHRSFC and can provide guidance for future research on DHRSFC.

articleTitle: Section Steel Alignment Correction Algorithm for Roller Conveyors Based on Double Deep Q-Network
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: The precise alignment of section steel on roller conveyor systems is essential for efficient transportation and processing, yet remains challenging due to the lack of accuracy of manual operation and the randomness of friction. To address the posture correction of section steel during the roller conveyor transport process, this paper proposes a posture correction algorithm for section steel on roller conveyors based on Double Deep Q-Network (DDQN). The objective is to maximize the waiting time before the baffle rises and minimize the time difference between the left and right endpoints of the section steel. First, a mathematical model is established based on the characteristics of section steel on the conveyor, analyzing the baffle operation time, the time difference after control, and the random effects of friction on transport. Then, two actions are designed for the baffle within the model: the waiting time and the control time. Corresponding reward functions are formulated according to the characteristics of each action. In the simulation environment, these two actions are integrated with the DDQN training method, and the training process is optimized. Finally, visual simulation demonstrates that the proposed DDQN-based algorithm can effectively adjust the posture of section steel. The evaluation metrics validate that the algorithm significantly improves posture correction accuracy, highlighting its potential as an effective solution.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Based Target Parameters Estimation for OTFS-ISAC System
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Orthogonal time frequency space (OTFS) modulation is a promising solution to support integrated sensing and communication (ISAC). In this paper, a two-step parameter estimation method based on deep learning is proposed for target sensing in OTFS-ISAC. A pulse compression operation is performed to cancel the influence of multi-path effects and overlapping transmission symbols. Subsequently, a deep residual is designed to discover targets and estimating integer Doppler and delay. Finally, a deep neural network is employed to estimate fractional Doppler and delay. Simulations results show that proposed method is capable of effective target detection and accurate delay and Doppler estimation.

articleTitle: Enhanced Signal Transmission in Integrated Satellite-Terrestrial Networks: A Double Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive investigation of the use of double reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RISs) in an integrated satellite-terrestrial network (ISTN), where the ground base station (GBS) and the satellite respectively serve the users within and outside the coverage of the GBS. However, nonnegligible co-channel interference can be induced, especially during the downlink transmission. To address the issue, two RISs are employed to assist the ISTN in enhancing the desired signal power and mitigating the interference, with one deployed on the satellite and the other near the GBS users. Specifically, our goal is to maximize the weighted sum rate of all users by jointly optimizing the active beamforming vectors of the satellite and GBS, and the passive reflection coefficient vectors of the two RISs. An alternating optimization algorithm based on fractional programming is then derived, which only requires the calculations of closed form or semi-closed form expressions in each iteration. Simulation results validate the performance advantage of the proposed double RIS-aided ISTN with the joint beamforming designs, which demonstrate the potential of integrating double RISs in ISTN to enhance the system performance.

articleTitle: Two-Timescale Transmit Power Minimization in Semi-Passive IRS-Aided ISAC Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Passive intelligent reflecting surfaces (IRS) have become prevalent in integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems, creating a new link for sensing and communication for better performance without additional energy consumption. However, the echo signal will experience significant pathloss due to the passive IRS's high pathloss effect after multiple reflections, which limits the gain brought by IRS. To address this issue, this paper applies semi-passive IRS to mitigate severe pathloss and investigates its impact on the performance of ISAC systems. Leveraging the ability of semi-passive IRS to acquire statistical channel state information (CSI), we introduce a two-timescale design algorithm which employs stochastic successive convex approximation (SSCA) and semi-definite relaxation (SDR) to manage non-convex constraints. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed two-timescale design achieves comparable transmit power to that of designs based on instantaneous CSI, validating the effectiveness and feasibility of the two-timescale design approach in ISAC systems.

articleTitle: Soft Global-Local Representation Learning and Labeling for Cross-Domain Facial Expression Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Cross-Domain Facial Expression Recognition (CD-FER) is concentrated on learning transferable knowledge to understand human emotion states automatically in the cross-domain scenario and has achieved much progress in the past decade. Most works extract both global and local features and adopt adversariallearning mechanism to learn domain-invariant features, which takes facial landmarks as prior knowledge and overlooks the unreliability, resulting in suboptimal performance. To solve this limitation, we propose a Soft Global-Local Representation Learning and Labeling (SGLRLL) framework for reliable and effective unsupervised facial expression domain adaptation. Specifically, instead of extracting local features with unreliable prior facial landmarks, we propose a Local Clue Searching (LCS) module to look up the local regions adaptively and extract the local features in a soft manner. We also propose a Joint Soft Pseudo Label Generator (JSPLG) based on learned Joint Gaussian distributions for assigning pseudo labels and weights to the features of unlabeled samples from the target domain, which considers the correlation between global-local learning and achieves a trade-off between the quality and quantity of pseudo labels. The cross-dataset results demonstrate that the proposed framework outperforms existing competing methods while requiring fewer parameters and enabling faster inference.

articleTitle: Single-Cloud Single-Edge Model Distribution Network Based on Dynamic Lossy Pruning
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Realizing semantic communication requires semantic extraction (SE) through artificial intelligence (AI) model, and the SE process requires certain hardware conditions. However, SE on terminal devices is challenging due to hardware limitations such as computational power and memory constraints. Therefore, in order to perform SE on mobile terminals, the SE model needs to be lightweight and distributed to the mobile terminal. This paper proposes a method for model distribution that is based on user requirements and hardware conditions. This method includes a dynamic lossy pruning algorithm proposed in this paper, which is applied to the cloud-edge-terminal network for model distribution. Simultaneously, a model knowledge repository (MKR) is established to enhance network operational efficiency. Through simulations of a single-cloud single-edge communication system, the performance of the cloud-edge-terminal dynamic model distribution network (CDMDN) is evaluated. Experimental results demonstrate that our network outperforms networks distributing fixed versions of models, exhibiting shorter service times and better performance under low signal-to-noise ratios (SNR) and limited bandwidth conditions.

articleTitle: Design of HII and OI for Dynamic Interference Coordination in UAV Communication Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In the communication network where the Base Stations (BSs) are deployed on Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs), the line-of-sight air-ground wireless channel leads to not only the strong desired signal but also the strong interference. Additionally, the flexible deployment and mobility of UAVs cause the rapidly fluctuation in signal strength, and there is an urgent need to study the dynamic Inter-Cell Interference Coordination (ICIC) technologies. This paper addresses the up-link transmission in the UAV communication networks, where the edge user will suffer severe interference if users served by other BSs use the same Resource Blocks (RBs) to transmit signals in close proximity. To mitigate this issue, the Soft Frequency Reuse (SFR) technology is adopted and the edge frequency band is expanded and further subdivided. Considering the rapid changes in up-link interference caused by both mobility and dynamic scheduling, improvements have been made to the High Interference Indicator (HII) and Overload Indicator (OI) by assessing communication satisfaction to determine the interference level and selectively transmitting signalling to neighboring UAV-BSs. Based on the new design of HII and OI, a Dynamic SFR and Dynamic Scheduling-based ICIC algorithm is proposed, and simulations are implemented for verification.

articleTitle: A Platform Based on Game Engine to Support UAV in 5G Network
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: This paper presents a software platform to support Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAV) within the context of 5G cellular networks, including the rationale for utilizing game engine to implement this platform and its main functions. It addresses three key scenarios: UAV trajectory planning to mitigate the impact of 5G handovers by improved A* algorithm, strategic site selection for Intelligent Reflecting Surfaces (IRS) by reverse ray tracing within urban 3D environments, and impact location determination of UAVs under unexpected conditions. These scenarios demonstrate the platform's effectiveness in tackling the multifaceted challenges of 5G-integrated UAV operations.

articleTitle: Joint Optimization of Deployment and Caching for HAPS Assisted Multi-UAV Communications
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: The Air Access Network (AAN) provides rapid emergency communication, leveraging its flexible deployment and extensive coverage. Specifically, the High-Altitude Platform Station (HAPS) aids multi-Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) communications, delivering superior service by reducing transmission distance and latency. This is achieved through real-time UAV deployment and content caching. The optimization of this system, modeled as a continuous-discrete Markov Decision Process (MDP), is addressed using the Multi-Agent Hybrid Double-Layer Soft Actor Critic (MAHDSAC) algorithm. This algorithm integrates continuous and discrete SAC to effectively manage mixed UAV deployment and cache control. Simulation results indicate that MAHDSAC outperforms traditional Multi-Agent Deep Reinforcement Learning (MADRL) methods in performance.

articleTitle: Reconstruction-Based Spectrogram Augmentation for Anomalous Sound Detection System
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Unsupervised anomalous sound detection(ASD) without anomalous samples is a challenging task, it has received much attention in the fields of industrial automation and medical information. In order to obtain representations that are conducive to the detection of anomalies, many studies focus on using meta-information for self-supervised representation learning. In this study, we propose an approach that includes data augmentation and contrastive learning to train the detector. This method is applied to the Log-Mel spectrogram of the waveform, converting it into an enhanced counterpart that highlights key information while reducing noise. Subsequently, we obtain temporal features through a TDNN extractor and merge them with the enhanced spectrogram. These two features are then fed into a Convolutional Neural Network(CNN) model for the ASD task. Furthermore, aiming to achieve inter-class dispersion and intra-class compactness through additional contrastive learning, we construct positive and negative samples using this AE and the CutMix method, respectively. We conduct a series of experiments, including comparative experiments with previous ASD systems, and two ablation studies for the data augmentation and contrastive learning modules, respectively. These experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed method and its superior performance compared to previous methods.

articleTitle: A Single-Factor Prediction Method for Air Quality Pollution Based on Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In recent years, with rapid societal development, the issue of air pollution has become increasingly significant, especially with PM2.5 particles posing a serious threat to human health. This study introduces a novel air quality prediction model based on neural networks-AR-LSTM, which incorporates advanced artificial intelligence technologies such as Residual Networks (ResNet), Graph Convolutional Networks (GCN), attention mechanisms, and Long Short-Term Memory networks (LSTM). This model effectively captures the spatiotemporal dependencies of air pollutant concentrations, thereby predicting the PM2.5 levels for the next 24 hours. By analyzing the air quality data from Shenyang, the AR-LSTM model demonstrated superior predictive accuracy and robustness compared to traditional machine learning models and other deep learning models. The results of this study not only verify the effectiveness of the model but also provide a scientific basis for air quality management and policy-making in the field of environmental science

articleTitle: Software Engineering M.S. Program for Safety Critical System with Artificial Intelligence
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Currently, AI is applied at a pace that challenges the verification of its suitability to the domains of application. A team of computer science researchers will combine their knowledge and skills to formulate a pedagogical strategy for a graduate-level program in software engineering (SE) that is developed from a foundational set of learning theories from which a set of principles is derived. These principles are used to define a set of learning techniques that are then amalgamated into methods for a comprehensive teaching and learning methodology. The graduate program will address the use of artificial intelligence (AI) in SE education, as the trending approach in 21st century application development. Academic and international industrial software development standards are incorporated into the course and program curricula to diminish the gap between classroom education and professional practices. Fundamental to this approach is the use of established learning theories for SE and AI in designing the educational modules. The outcome of this proposed research will be a graduate program in software engineering.

articleTitle: A New Method for OFDM Signal Modulation Recognition Based on Optimized Convolutional Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Due to the rapid development of communication technology, the environment in which electromagnetic signals are located is complicated and intricate. For the problem of OFDM signal modulation recognition in a complex electromagnetic environment, this paper proposes a new method based on deep learning model. Firstly, the structure of convolutional neural network is optimized and the model parameters are designed to be more suitable for the actual environment and the structure of the convolutional neural network is optimized, and then the convolutional neural network and Transformer network model are integrated to enhance the recognition effects, thus making the new method more robust and noise-resistant. The simulation demonstrate that the proposed method has better recognition performance in low signal-to-noise ratio situations, and the ability to improve the performance of OFDM signal modulation recognition.

articleTitle: Fusion Method of Tobacco Leaf State Recognition Based on Bayesian Algorithm and Xgboost
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: The three-stage curing process is the key link to determining the quality of tobacco products, which is affected by the curing process parameters such as heating point and stable temperature time. In this paper, multiple sensors were used to collect baking temperature, humidity, tobacco weight, and tobacco images during baking. Naive Bayes and extreme gradient lifting tree algorithms and data fusion methods were adopted, and a fusion model for baking state recognition was designed. The accurate identification of baking state is realized. The accuracy of state recognition of tobacco curing state by fusion model reached 99.2%. This model can predict the key parameters of baking objectively and accurately, and assist baking personnel to adjust.

articleTitle: A Nested DRL-Based Method for Power Allocation and AP Sleep Control in Cell-Free Massive MIMO Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: Cell-free massive MIMO (CFmMIMO) systems are increasingly recognized as a key technology to enhance 6G network performance. The large-scale coverage of access points (APs) and irrational power allocation leads to low energy efficiency and suboptimal Quality of Service (QoS). This paper proposes a nested deep reinforcement learning (DRL)-based optimization method utilizing novel double nested actor-critic (AC) frameworks to optimize power allocation and AP sleep control, which efficiently addresses the complex decision-making processes involved in dynamic environments. Extensive simulations results show that our proposed method enhances the peak energy efficiency in CFmMIMO systems by 19.6% and achieves a better trade-off between QoS and power consumption than the state-of-the-art and heuristic alternatives.

articleTitle: Collaborative Cloud-Edge Channel Prediction for Dynamic Industrial Wireless Networks: An Obstacle-Aware Channel Transformative Architecture
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
abstract: In the era of Industry 4.0, predicting channel states in Industrial Wireless Networks (IWNs) poses significant chal-lenges due to factors like communication delays, device mobility, and obstacle interference. Traditional methods fail to accurately capture the dynamic changes in channel states, particularly in environments with multiple obstacles and rapid device movement, which significantly reduces prediction accuracy. To overcome these challenges, this paper proposes a high-precision channel prediction method based on a cloud-edge-end collaborative architecture. The architecture leverages real-time obstacle detection and multi-dimensional feature extraction to enhance prediction accuracy. At its core, the Obstacle-aware Channel Transformative Architecture (OCTA) model integrates spatial and temporal feature modeling, enabling robust adaptability to dynamic en-vironments. The model is continuously optimized via system feedback and regularly updated to maintain high prediction accuracy and adaptability. Experimental results demonstrate that OCTA significantly improves the accuracy and generalization of channel state prediction in complex industrial environments, outperforming traditional approaches, especially when facing dynamic changes and various types of obstacles.

articleTitle: Distributed Intelligent Scheduling for Multi-Level eMBB Services in IoT
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computer and Communications (ICCC)
